308|## Consistency Check Process
309|
310|### Process Step 1: Harness Architecture Scan
311|1. **File Discovery**: Use `find` to enumerate all harness architecture files
312|2. **Comprehensive Line-by-Line Scanning**: **SCAN** each file line by line to examine all documents within scope without skipping anything - comprehensive examination required for governance compliance
313|3. **Pattern Matching**: Use `grep` to extract specific patterns from files as supplemental checks only
314|4. **Cross-Reference Analysis**: Verify all file references exist
315|5. **Structure Validation**: Validate workflow structure compliance
316|6. **Terminology Analysis**: Check for inconsistent terminology
317|
318|### Process Step 2: Detailed Variable Analysis
319|1. **File Reference Validation**: Check each referenced file exists
320|2. **Workflow Structure Validation**: Compare workflows against template for mandated sections only
321|3. **Governance Rule Validation**: Check rule file structure consistency
322|4. **Documentation Validation**: Verify INDEX.md and documentation structure
323|5. **Framework Coverage Validation**: Check universal framework usage
324|
325|### Process Step 3: Issue Aggregation
326|1. **Severity Classification**: Classify issues as Critical/High/Medium/Low
327|2. **Categorization**: Group issues by consistency variable
328|3. **Impact Analysis**: Assess impact on harness functionality
329|4. **Recommendation Generation**: Generate fix recommendations
330|
331|### Process Step 4: Report Generation
332|1. **Report Structure**: Create comprehensive report with findings
333|2. **Issue Prioritization**: Order issues by severity and impact
334|3. **Fix Recommendations**: Provide specific fix suggestions
335|4. **Metrics Summary**: Provide consistency metrics

  1|# Architect Workflow Template
  2|
  3|**Purpose**: Architect-specific template for creating agent workflows.
  4|
  5|## Template Overview
  6|
  7|This template is used by the Architect agent to create workflows for other agents. All workflows must follow this structure for consistency.
  8|
  9|## Workflow Types
 10|
 11|Architect creates two types of workflows with different Phase 10 patterns:
 12|
 13|### 1. Continuous Operation Workflows (Standard Agent Workflows)
 14|- **Purpose**: Agents that should always be ready for new tasks
 15|- **Phase 10 Pattern**: Include "Return to step 1" for continuous operation
 16|- **Examples**: Architect_General_Workflow, Planner_Plan_Workflow, Executor_Implementation_Cycle
 17|- **Behavior**: Workflow cycles indefinitely, agent always ready for next task
 18|- **Use Case**: Primary agent workflows that handle ongoing agent operations
 19|
 20|### 2. Single-Execution Workflows (Utility/Tool Workflows)
 21|- **Purpose**: Utility workflows that execute once and terminate
 22|- **Phase 10 Pattern**: Exclude or modify to termination (no "Return to step 1")
 23|- **Examples**: Architect_Consistency_Check_Workflow, Architect_Consistency_Fix_Workflow
 24|- **Behavior**: Workflow executes once and terminates, no automatic looping
 25|- **Use Case**: Specialized workflows that run on-demand and complete
 26|
 27|### Workflow Type Selection Guidelines
 28|- **Use Continuous Operation**: For primary agent workflows that should always be available
 29|- **Use Single-Execution**: For utility workflows, validation workflows, maintenance workflows
 30|

 32|
 33|- **Location**: Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Workflow_Template.md
 34|- **Owner**: Architect Agent
 35|- **Usage**: Architect uses this template to create workflows for all agents
 36|- **Updates**: Only Architect should modify this template

  9|# Architect Agent Rules
 10|
 11|## Overview
 12|Declarative policy for Architect agent implementation following infrastructure-first principles. Rules are organized into Conventions (behavioral guidance) and Constraints (hard boundaries).
 13|
 14|## Conventions
 15|
 16|- **Best Practices**: Web search must be used before implementing major architectural decisions or when uncertain about implementation approaches. Best practices are established industry standards that must be researched before proceeding.
 17|- Check index files (Docs/index.md, Docs/Research/index.md, Docs/Websites/index.md, Docs/Code/index.md) before web searching (reduces token cost, prioritizes local knowledge)
 18|- Present function and test result after each successful test. Wait for user confirmation before proceeding (ensures quality control, prevents cascading errors)
 19|- Answer questions first when user requests end with "?". Ask for permission before making changes after answering (ensures user understanding, prevents unintended modifications)
 20|- Use capital letters at the start of items unless lowercase is needed (maintains consistency, improves readability)
 21|- All **{CAPITALIZED}** commands and terms are defined in Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Terminology_Glossary.md (SSOT for terminology)
 22|
 23|## Execution Modes
 24|
 25|Three execution modes govern workflow behavior when encountering failures:
 26|
 27|- **Manual**: Stop at failures for human oversight - workflow halts at any failure point and awaits user intervention to decide on retry, modification, or abort
 28|- **Auto**: Don't continue on failures - workflow automatically stops on any failure without requiring human intervention, ensuring errors are not silently ignored
 29|- **Complete**: Continue past failures - workflow automatically continues through all failures, ignoring errors to reach completion regardless of success/failure status
 30|
 31|## Constraints
 32|
 33|- Build exactly one function at a time. Test immediately. Never write a second function before first is tested (ensures modular validation, prevents hidden bugs)
 34|- Treat user-confirmed functions as locked. Never modify without explicit user permission (maintains stability, prevents unintended changes)
 35|- Check local research using index files when function fails. Web search only if local info unavailable. Never retry blindly without research (reduces token cost, ensures correct implementation)
 36|- Place scripts in Scripts/<Category>/ folder matching primary function. Never create ad-hoc folders or place outside established categories (maintains organization, prevents file chaos)
 37|- Place IDE harness tests in Scripts/Tests/ folder only. Never place IDE harness tests in App/ directory (maintains clear separation between application code and harness infrastructure)
 38|- Always use popups for yes/no questions. Never use text-only confirmations (ensures clear user intent, prevents miscommunication)
 39|- Always categorize files when adding to documentation directories. Never place files uncategorized (maintains organization, enables efficient navigation)
 40|- Never skip compliance checks. Always verify architectural compliance before proceeding (ensures quality, prevents rule violations)
 41|- Never reference or modify App/ directory (reference only for application context, prevents scope creep into implementation)
 42|- Never test governance systems in isolated environments. Always test in actual project context with real tool executions (ensures real-world functionality, prevents false confidence)
 43|- Never perform actions outside workflow scope. Always follow defined workflow processes and never perform tasks outside the current workflow scope unless explicitly requested by the user (prevents token waste, ensures focused execution)
 44|- Never create documentation files unless specifically requested. Never create README.md, CHANGELOG.md, or other documentation files unless specifically requested by the user (prevents token waste, maintains workflow scope discipline)
 45|- Never run subagents unless explicitly requested by the user. Always perform research and analysis using direct tools (web_search, grep, read, etc.) unless user specifically requests subagent delegation (prevents unexpected subagent usage, maintains user control over execution)
 46|
 47|## Architecture
 48|
 49|- Infrastructure-first architecture: Authority lives in deterministic software, intelligence lives in agents (maintains architectural purity, enables predictable governance)
 50|- Default script categories: Logging/, Gating/, Rule_Enforcement/, Testing/. Create new categories when no existing category matches the script's primary function or intent (maintains organizational clarity while allowing necessary evolution, aligns with intent-first categorization)
 51|- Governance file locations: Agents/ for other agents' governance files, Rules/ for rule definitions, Workflow/ for workflow definitions, Scripts/ for implementation scripts, Docs/ for documentation (maintains SSOT, enables clear ownership boundaries)
 52|
 53|## Tool Configuration
 54|
 55|- Directory verification: `ls -la <directory>` (verify directory structure exists)
 56|- File discovery: `find <path> -name "*.md"` (find markdown governance files)
 57|- Pattern search: `grep -r "pattern" <directory>` (search for patterns in rule files)
 58|- JSON validation: `python -m json.tool <file>` (validate JSON syntax, exit code indicates success/failure)
 59|- File comparison: `diff <file1> <file2>` (compare files before changes, exit code 0 = identical)
 60|
 61|## Project Structure
 62|
 63|- `Agents/` â€“ Other agents' governance files (EDIT these to enforce standards)
 64|- `Rules/` â€“ Rule definitions for all agents (EDIT these to maintain compliance)
 65|- `Workflow/` â€“ Workflow definitions for all agents (EDIT these to enforce processes)
 66|- `Scripts/` â€“ Implementation scripts organized by category (WRITE scripts here)
 67|- `Docs/` â€“ Documentation and research (organize by category with index files)
 68|- `.devin/` â€“ Devin CLI configuration, skills, and hooks (EDIT to maintain harness)
 69|- `Logs/` â€“ Agent logs and conversation history
 70|- `Plans/` â€“ Project planning documents
 71|- `App/` â€“ SovereignAI application code (reference only)
</file-view>

Rules are organized into Conventions (behavioral guidance) and Constraints (hard boundaries).\n 13|\n 14|## Conventions\n 15|\n 16|- **Best Practices**: Web search must be used before implementing major architectural decisions or when uncertain about implementation approaches. Best practices are established industry standards that must be researched before proceeding.\n 17|- Check index files (Docs/index.md, Docs/Research/index.md, Docs/Websites/index.md, Docs/Code/index.md) before web searching (reduces token cost, prioritizes local knowledge)\n 18|- Present function and test result after each successful test. Ask for permission before making changes after answering (ensures user understanding, prevents unintended modifications)\n 20|- Use capital letters at the start of items unless lowercase is needed (maintains consistency, improves readability)\n 21|- All **{CAPITALIZED}** commands and terms are defined in Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Terminology_Glossary.md (SSOT for terminology)\n 22|\n 23|## Execution Modes\n 24|\n 25|Three execution modes govern workflow behavior when encountering failures:\n 26|\n 27|- **Manual**: Stop at failures for human oversight - workflow halts at any failure point and awaits user intervention to decide on retry, modification, or abort\n 28|- **Auto**: Don't continue on failures - workflow automatically stops on any failure without requiring human intervention, ensuring errors are not silently ignored\n 29|- **Complete**: Continue past failures - workflow automatically continues through all failures, ignoring errors to reach completion regardless of success/failure status\n 30|\n 31|## Constraints\n 32|\n 33|- Build exactly one function at a time. Test immediately. Never write a second function before first is tested (ensures modular validation, prevents hidden bugs)\n 34|- Treat user-confirmed functions as locked. Always test in actual project context with real tool executions (ensures real-world functionality, prevents false confidence)\n 43|- Never perform actions outside workflow scope. Always follow defined workflow processes and never perform tasks outside the current workflow scope unless explicitly requested by the user (prevents token waste, ensures focused execution)\n 44|- Never create documentation files unless specifically requested.   1|# SovereignAI Harness Terminology Glossary
  2|
  3|**Purpose**: Single source of truth (SSOT) for all capitalized terminology used across the SovereignAI harness architecture. This glossary ensures consistent understanding of governance terminology across all agents and workflows.
  4|
  5|**Governance**: This document is maintained by the Architect agent and serves as the authoritative source for terminology definitions. All agents must reference this glossary for terminology understanding.
  6|
  7|---
  8|
  9|## Core Workflow Commands
 10|
 11|### **SCAN**
 12|**Definition**: Examine all documents within scope line by line without skipping anything - comprehensive examination required for governance compliance.
 13|
 14|**Usage**: Used when comprehensive examination of documents is required for governance compliance, quality assurance, or consistency verification. This is the primary scanning method and cannot be replaced by pattern matching tools like grep.
 15|
 16|**Examples**:
 17|- **SCAN** all harness architecture files for consistency checks
 18|- **SCAN** App/ directory line by line for compliance verification
 19|- **SCAN** workflow files to validate template compliance
 20|
 21|---
 22|
 23|### **PRINT**
 24|**Definition**: Output text to chat interface for user visibility (not to files or logs).
 25|
 26|**Usage**: Used to communicate workflow status, progress updates, and important information to the user during workflow execution. This command does not write to files or logs.
 27|
 28|**Examples**:
 29|- **PRINT** "Workflow initialization complete"
 30|- **PRINT** "Scan strategy selected - Full Comprehensive"
 31|- **PRINT** "Consistency check complete - 0 issues found"
 32|
 33|---
 34|
 35|### **VALIDATION**
 36|**Definition**: Validate step completion before proceeding to next phase.
 37|
 38|**Usage**: Used to ensure that workflow steps have completed successfully and meet quality criteria before moving to the next phase. This is a quality validation mechanism.
 39|
 40|**Examples**:
 41|- **VALIDATION**: Validate file reference extraction completed successfully
 42|- **VALIDATION**: Validate workflow structure check completed successfully
 43|- **VALIDATION**: Validate that all referenced files exist
 44|
 45|---
 46|
 47|### **STATUS TRACKING**
 48|**Definition**: Update workflow status for monitoring and recovery.
 49|
 50|**Usage**: Used to track workflow progress, enable recovery from failures, and provide visibility into workflow execution state. Status updates are typically written to workflow_state.json or similar tracking mechanisms.
 51|
 52|**Examples**:
 53|- **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_0_complete"
 54|- **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_3_in_progress"
 55|- **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_7_complete"
 56|
 57|---
 58|
 59|### **TERMINATE**
 60|**Definition**: End workflow execution (do not return to step 1).
 61|
 62|**Usage**: Used in single-execution workflows to signal completion and prevent automatic looping. This is the workflow termination command for utility workflows.
 63|
 64|**Examples**:
 65|- **TERMINATE**: End workflow execution (do not return to step 1)
 66|- **TERMINATE**: Workflow execution complete - workflow terminated
 67|
 68|---
 69|
 70|## Workflow-Specific Commands
 71|
 72|### **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**
 73|**Definition**: Apply execution mode handling patterns based on selected mode (Manual/Auto/Complete).
 74|
 75|**Usage**: Used to determine how the workflow should respond to failures based on the user-selected execution mode.
 76|
 77|**Modes**:
 78|- **Manual**: Stop at failures for human oversight
 79|- **Auto**: Don't continue on failures (auto-stop on errors)
 80|- **Complete**: Continue past failures (ignore all errors)
 81|
 82|**Examples**:
 83|- **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Apply execution mode handling patterns
 84|- **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Apply review mode handling patterns
 85|
 86|---
 87|
 88|### **CONVERGENCE CHECK**
 89|**Definition**: Verify panelist scores against quality thresholds.
 90|
 91|**Usage**: Used in Round Table review processes to determine if panelists have reached agreement on quality assessments.
 92|
 93|**Thresholds**:
 94|- Clean pass: â‰¥4.5 score
 95|- Acceptable pass: 3.5-4.4 score with documented rationale
 96|- Fail: <3.5 score
 97|
 98|**Examples**:
 99|- **CONVERGENCE CHECK**: Check if all panelists chose PASS (â‰¥4.5 score or 3.5-4.4 with rationale)
100|- **CONVERGENCE CHECK**: Verify convergence criteria met
101|
102|---
103|
104|### **QUOTA AWARENESS**
105|**Definition**: Monitor internal subagent quota usage for recovery tracking.
106|
107|**Usage**: Used to track subagent resource consumption and enable recovery if quota limits are approached or exceeded.
108|
109|**Examples**:
110|- **QUOTA AWARENESS**: Monitor internal subagent quota usage and track step progress
111|- **QUOTA AWARENESS**: Track quota usage for recovery if needed
112|
113|---
114|
115|### **LOOP DECISION**
116|**Definition**: Determine workflow continuation based on conditions.
117|
118|**Usage**: Used to control workflow flow and determine whether to loop back to previous phases or proceed forward.
119|
120|**Examples**:
121|- **LOOP DECISION**: If more plan steps remain â†’ Return to step 25 with next step
122|- **LOOP BACK**: Return to Phase 4 for next iteration
123|
124|---
125|
126|### **HANDOFF VALIDATION**
127|**Definition**: Verify handoff file integrity and completeness.
128|
129|**Usage**: Used when transferring work between agents to ensure all required information is present and accessible.
130|
131|**Examples**:
132|- **HANDOFF VALIDATION**: Verify handoff file integrity per template requirements
133|- **HANDOFF VALIDATION**: Validate all required fields are present
134|
135|---
136|
137|## Decision and Planning Commands
138|
139|### **ARCHITECT OPINION**
140|**Definition**: Provide analysis and recommendation BEFORE user selection.
141|
142|**Usage**: Used by Architect agent to provide expert analysis and recommendations when presenting implementation options to users.
143|
144|**Examples**:
145|- **ARCHITECT OPINION**: Provide analysis and recommendation BEFORE user selection
146|- **ARCHITECT OPINION**: Recommend optimal approach based on analysis
147|
148|---
149|
150|### **PRESENTATION PATTERN**
151|**Definition**: Present options with metrics, provide architect opinion, use popup menu for selection.
152|
153|**Usage**: Used to standardize how options are presented to users, ensuring consistent format and decision-making process.
154|
155|**Examples**:
156|- **PRESENTATION PATTERN**: Present options with metrics, provide architect opinion, use popup menu
157|- **PRESENTATION PATTERN**: Use popup menu for selection
158|
159|---
160|
161|### **RULE ENFORCEMENT**
162|**Definition**: Ensure options comply with agent rules.
163|
164|**Usage**: Used to validate that proposed options or approaches comply with the relevant agent's governance rules.
165|
166|**Examples**:
167|- **RULE ENFORCEMENT**: Ensure options comply with Architect rules
168|- **RULE ENFORCEMENT**: Validate compliance with governance constraints
169|
170|---
171|
172|### **SPECIFICATION CONFIRMATION**
173|**Definition**: Ask user to confirm specification or request modifications using popup menu.
174|
175|**Usage**: Used to get user approval on detailed specifications before proceeding with implementation.
176|
177|**Examples**:
178|- **SPECIFICATION CONFIRMATION**: Ask user to confirm specification or request modifications
179|- **SPECIFICATION CONFIRMATION**: Use popup menu with [Confirm/Modify] options
180|
181|---
182|
183|### **IMPLEMENTATION MODE SELECTION**
184|**Definition**: Ask user to choose implementation mode using popup menu.
185|
186|**Usage**: Used to determine whether implementation should be automated or manual based on user preference.
187|
188|**Examples**:
189|- **IMPLEMENTATION MODE SELECTION**: Ask user to choose using popup menu
190|- **IMPLEMENTATION MODE SELECTION**: Select automated vs manual implementation
191|
192|---
193|
194|## Information and Notes
195|
196|### **AUTOMATED PROGRESSION NOTE**
197|**Definition**: Validation system behavior notes for context.
198|
199|**Usage**: Used to provide explanatory notes about how the validation system behaves in specific situations.
200|
201|**Examples**:
202|- **AUTOMATED PROGRESSION NOTE**: The validation system allows state-mutating tools automatically during this step
203|- **AUTOMATED PROGRESSION NOTE**: User confirmation requests use ask_user_question for approval without triggering failure intervention
204|
205|---
206|
207|### **IMPORTANT**
208|**Definition**: Important notes that require attention but are not critical failures.
209|
210|**Usage**: Used to highlight important information that users should be aware of during workflow execution.
211|
212|**Examples**:
213|- **IMPORTANT**: Real-world testing required to avoid fake passes from isolated testing
214|- **IMPORTANT**: Hook file changes require Devin CLI restart
215|
216|---
217|
218|## Severity and Priority Markers
219|
220|### **CRITICAL**
221|**Definition**: Critical issues or required actions that must be addressed immediately.
222|
223|**Usage**: Used to mark issues that require immediate attention or actions that are mandatory for workflow success.
224|
225|**Examples**:
226|- **CRITICAL**: Violations that must be fixed (missing tests, hardcoded dependencies)
227|- **CRITICAL**: Hook file changes require Devin CLI restart before testing
228|
229|---
230|
231|### **HIGH**
232|**Definition**: High priority issues that should be addressed soon.
233|
234|**Usage**: Used to mark significant issues that should be resolved but are not immediately blocking.
235|
236|**Examples**:
237|- **HIGH**: Major quality issues that should be fixed (monolithic functions, poor modularity)
238|- **HIGH**: High priority issues requiring attention
239|
240|---
241|
242|### **MEDIUM**
243|**Definition**: Medium priority issues for improvement.
244|
245|**Usage**: Used to mark issues that represent improvements but are not urgent.
246|
247|**Examples**:
248|- **MEDIUM**: Best practices improvements (code readability, maintainability)
249|- **MEDIUM**: Medium priority issues for improvement
250|
251|---
252|
253|### **LOW**
254|**Definition**: Low priority minor suggestions.
255|
256|**Usage**: Used to mark minor suggestions or improvements that are optional.
257|
258|**Examples**:
259|- **LOW**: Minor suggestions (comments, formatting)
260|- **LOW**: Low priority issues for consideration
261|
262|---
263|
264|## Governance Terms
265|
266|### **BP** (Best Practice)
267|**Definition**: Established industry standards that must be researched before proceeding with major decisions.
268|
269|**Usage**: Used to indicate when web search for current best practices is required before making architectural or implementation decisions.
270|
271|**Examples**:
272|- **BP**: Web search for best practices before major architectural decisions
273|- **BP**: Research industry standards before implementation
274|
275|**Implementation**: When user input is "BP?" (Best Practice?), perform web search for current best practices relevant to the task at hand.
276|
277|---
278|
279|### **SSOT** (Single Source of Truth)
280|**Definition**: Centralized repository for authoritative information that eliminates duplication and inconsistencies.
281|
282|**Usage**: Used to indicate the authoritative source for specific information, ensuring all agents reference the same accurate data.
283|
284|**Examples**:
285|- **SSOT**: Workflow/Terminology_Glossary.md is the SSOT for terminology definitions
286|- **SSOT**: INDEX.md is the SSOT for directory structure information
287|
288|**Best Practice**: Establish SSOT for critical information to prevent inconsistencies and ensure all stakeholders work from the same data.
289|
290|---
291|
292|## Standard Terms
293|
294|### **ID**
295|**Definition**: Unique identifier for workflows, documents, or entities.
296|
297|**Usage**: Used to provide unique identification for workflows, documents, and other entities within the harness architecture.
298|
299|**Examples**:
300|- **ID**: WF-ARCH-001
301|- **ID**: WF-PLAN-001
302|
303|---
304|
305|### **DO**
306|**Definition**: Required actions that must be performed according to rules.
307|
308|**Usage**: Used in rule files to specify mandatory actions that agents must perform.
309|
310|**Examples**:
311|- **DO**: Verify each function follows single responsibility principle
312|- **DO**: Check that functions have clear inputs and outputs
313|
314|---
315|
316|## Terminology Governance
317|
318|### Glossary Maintenance
319|- **Owner**: Architect Agent
320|- **Update Process**: Architect agent reviews and updates glossary based on new terminology needs
321|- **Version Control**: All changes tracked with version history
322|- **Approval**: Architect agent approval required for new terms or definition changes
323|
324|### Term Addition Process
325|1. Identify new terminology need from workflow or rule updates
326|2. Research standard definitions and best practices
327|3. Draft definition with clear usage examples
328|4. Add to appropriate section in glossary
329|5. Update AGENTS.md to reference glossary if needed
330|6. Update workflows to reference new terms via glossary
331|
332|### Reference Pattern
333|All workflows and rules should reference this glossary for terminology understanding:
334|```markdown

336|```

341|

345|4. **Updates**: Propagate terminology changes through Architect agent

  1|# Planner Plan Creation Workflow
  2|
  3|**ID**: WF-PLAN-SCAN-001  
  4|**Owner**: Planner Agent  
  5|**Frequency**: On-demand  
  6|**Duration**: Standard (plan creation from existing scan results)  
  7|**Priority**: High
  8|**Workflow Type**: Single-Execution (Utility Workflow)
  9|**Execution Modes**: Manual
 10|
 11|## Purpose
 12|Create implementation-ready plans from existing governance scan results. This workflow accepts scan findings as input (from scanning processes performed by other agents or workflows) and structures them into planning-focused recommendations following the authoritative Plan Template format. The workflow focuses on systematically processing entire scan logs and translating findings into actionable plans (Context, Steps, Dependencies with planning language) based on AI agent planning best practices. Plan number is determined by reading Plans/PLAN_TRACKING.md to identify next available sequential plan number.
 13|
 14|**Plan Output**: Scan findings are structured as planning-focused recommendations following Plan Template format (Context, Steps, Dependencies with planning language) for manual implementation. Plan number is determined by reading Plans/PLAN_TRACKING.md to identify next available sequential plan number.
 15|
 16|## Scope
 17|**Input**: Existing scan results and findings from governance scanning processes (performed by other agents or workflows) - must read entire scan log systematically
 18|
 19|**Plan Output**: Plans/plan-{N}-Rev1.md (single plan following Plan Template format with Context, Steps, Dependencies using planning language)
 20|
 21|## Reference Files (SSOT)
 22|- **Plan Template**: Workflow/Planner/Templates/Plan_Template.md (authoritative format reference)
 23|- **Plan Tracking**: Plans/PLAN_TRACKING.md (single source of truth for plan numbering and history)
 24|- **Quality Assessment**: Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Quality_Assessment_Framework.md (quality assessment criteria)

 26|- **Plan Brief Template**: Workflow/Planner/Templates/Plan_Brief_Template.md (internal review structure)

 29|- **Terminology Glossary**: Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Terminology_Glossary.md (terminology definitions)
 30|
 31|## Roles and Owners
 32|- **Planner Agent**: Creates implementation-ready plans from existing scan results, applies Plan Template format, validates plan structure
 33|- **User**: Provides scan results as input, approves plan structure and content
 34|- **Governance System**: Validation against Plan Template and planning standards
 35|
 36|## Trigger and End State
 37|- **Trigger**: User provides existing scan results and requests plan creation
 38|- **End State**: Implementation-ready plan (with appropriate revision splitting) following Plan Template format for implementation planning, using next available sequential plan number from PLAN_TRACKING.md
 39|
 40|## Workflow Steps (20 steps)

 43|- 1. Read Rules/Planner/Planner_Rules.md to understand planning criteria and infrastructure compliance requirements
 44|- 2. Read Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Terminology_Glossary.md to understand terminology definitions

 52|- 8. Request user to provide existing scan results and findings from governance scanning processes

  1|# Reviewer BP Harness Scanner Workflow
  2|
  3|**ID**: WF-REV-HARNESS-001  
  4|**Owner**: Reviewer Agent  
  5|**Frequency**: On-demand  
  6|**Duration**: Extended (comprehensive per-file analysis with mandatory **{BP}** web search for each file)  
  7|**Priority**: High
  8|**Workflow Type**: Single-Execution (Utility Workflow)
  9|**Execution Modes**: Manual, Manual Batched, Automatic, Automatic Batched
 10|
 11|## Purpose
 12|Comprehensive line-by-line scan of all harness governance files to verify compliance with governance best practices, documentation standards, and architectural consistency. Unlike the App scanner (Reviewer_BP_App_Scanner_Workflow) which focuses on code quality and modularity, this workflow focuses on governance quality: workflow structure compliance, rule definition standards, configuration validity, markdown consistency, and cross-reference accuracy. Every governance file must be checked against governance-specific best practices without exception, with mandatory **{BP}** web search for documentation and governance best practices.
 13|
 14|## Scope
 15|**Harness Governance Only**: All files in Workflow/, Rules/, .devin/, AGENTS.md, INDEX.md (excludes Docs/, Logs/, Plans/, App/ folders)
 16|
 17|**Report Location**: Logs/Reviewer/BP/Harness/harness-best-practice-scan-[YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS].md
 18|
 19|**Incremental Report**: Logs/Reviewer/BP/Harness/incremental-scan-report.md
 20|
 21|## Roles and Owners
 22|- **Reviewer Agent**: Executes harness scanning workflow, coordinates subagents for large-scale scanning, consolidates findings
 23|- **User**: Requests harness scanning, approves findings and recommendations
 24|- **Governance System**: Validation against governance best practices and architectural standards
 25|
 26|## Trigger and End State
 27|- **Trigger**: User requests best practice compliance scan of harness governance files
 28|- **End State**: Comprehensive compliance report with findings, severity ratings, and actionable recommendations for governance improvements
 29|
 30|## Workflow Steps (69 steps)
 31|
 32|### Phase 0. Read Reviewer Rules + Governance
 33|- 1. Read Rules/Reviewer/Reviewer_Rules.md to understand review criteria and governance compliance requirements
 34|- 2. Read Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Terminology_Glossary.md to understand terminology definitions
 35|- 3. Read Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Workflow_Template.md to understand workflow structure patterns
 36|- 4. Parse YAML frontmatter and rule definitions for compliance verification guidance
 37|- 5. Store rule context and compliance criteria for reference throughout workflow execution
 38|- 6. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "phase_0_complete"
 39|- 7. **PRINT** "Reviewer rules and governance compliance criteria loaded"
 40|
 41|### Phase 1. Select Execution Mode
 42|- 8. Ask user to select execution mode for this workflow using popup menu:
 43|  - **Manual**: Process files one by one in alphabetical order, requiring user confirmation at each file for maximum oversight (recommended for first comprehensive scan)
 44|  - **Manual Batched**: Process files in batches of 5-10 files in alphabetical order, requiring user confirmation between batches for balanced efficiency with oversight
 45|  - **Automatic**: Process files one by one in alphabetical order automatically without user confirmation for maximum efficiency
 46|  - **Automatic Batched**: Process files in batches of 5-10 files in alphabetical order automatically without user confirmation for maximum efficiency
 47|- 9. Store selected execution mode for file processing strategy throughout workflow
 48|- 10. **PRINT** "Execution mode selected - [Manual/Manual Batched/Automatic/Automatic Batched] will govern file processing strategy"
 49|
 50|### Phase 2. Scan Scope Definition
 51|- 11. Define scan scope: Harness governance files (Workflow/, Rules/, .devin/, AGENTS.md, INDEX.md)
 52|- 12. Define exclusion scope: Docs/, Logs/, Plans/, App/ folders (excluded from scan)
 53|- 13. Determine scanning strategy based on file count and complexity:

  1|# Architect Execution Mode Patterns
  2|
  3|**Purpose**: Architect-specific execution mode patterns for infrastructure and governance workflows.
  4|
  5|## Architect Execution Mode Definitions
  6|
  7|### Full Comprehensive Mode
  8|**Behavior**: Execute all 12 consistency variables for complete architecture validation
  9|- **Scope**: All consistency checks (file references, terminology, workflow structure, governance rules, documentation, agent capabilities, framework coverage, execution strategy, state management, runtime prerequisites, scoring scale, behavior rules)
 10|- **Checkpoint Handling**: Proceed automatically through all consistency checks
 11|- **Failure Handling**: Continue workflow automatically, logging failures but completing full scan
 12|- **User Control**: Minimal user control with maximum coverage
 13|- **Use Case**: Monthly comprehensive scans, before/after major architectural changes
 14|
 15|### Basic Essential Mode
 16|**Behavior**: Execute essential consistency variables for quick validation
 17|- **Scope**: File references + terminology + workflow structure (3 core variables)
 18|- **Checkpoint Handling**: Proceed automatically through essential checks
 19|- **Failure Handling**: Stop workflow automatically if essential check fails
 20|- **User Control**: Balanced user control with essential coverage
 21|- **Use Case**: Weekly basic scans, quick validation before changes
 22|
 23|### Targeted Mode
 24|**Behavior**: Execute user-selected consistency variables for focused validation
 25|- **Scope**: User selects specific consistency variables from available 12
 26|- **Checkpoint Handling**: Proceed automatically through selected checks
 27|- **Failure Handling**: Stop workflow automatically if selected check fails
 28|- **User Control**: Maximum user control with focused coverage
 29|- **Use Case**: Investigating specific architectural concerns, targeted validation
 30|
 31|### Quick Check Mode
 32|**Behavior**: Execute file reference consistency only for rapid validation
 33|- **Scope**: File references only (1 variable)
 34|- **Checkpoint Handling**: Proceed automatically through file reference check
 35|- **Failure Handling**: Stop workflow automatically if file reference check fails
 36|- **User Control**: Minimal user control with rapid validation
 37|- **Use Case**: Pre-change validation, quick reference checks
 38|
 39|## Architect Execution Mode Handling Patterns
 40|
 41|### Full Comprehensive Mode Pattern
 42|1. Execute all 12 consistency variables sequentially
 43|2. **SCAN** each governance file line by line for comprehensive examination
 44|3. **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Proceed automatically through all checks regardless of individual failures
 45|4. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status for each consistency variable
 46|5. **PRINT**: Progress updates for each consistency variable
 47|6. Continue to next consistency variable automatically
 48|7. Generate comprehensive report with all findings
 49|
 50|### Basic Essential Mode Pattern
 51|1. Execute 3 essential consistency variables (file references, terminology, workflow structure)
 52|2. **SCAN** each governance file line by line for essential examination
 53|3. **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Proceed automatically through essential checks, stop on failure
 54|4. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status for each essential variable
 55|5. **PRINT**: Progress updates for each essential variable
 56|6. Proceed to next essential variable on success, stop on failure
 57|7. Generate basic report with essential findings
 58|
 59|### Targeted Mode Pattern
 60|1. User selects specific consistency variables from available 12
 61|2. **SCAN** each governance file line by line for selected examination
 62|3. **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Proceed automatically through selected checks, stop on failure
 63|4. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status for each selected variable
 64|5. **PRINT**: Progress updates for each selected variable
 65|6. Proceed to next selected variable on success, stop on failure
 66|7. Generate targeted report with selected findings
 67|
 68|### Quick Check Mode Pattern
 69|1. Execute file reference consistency check only
 70|2. **SCAN** each governance file line by line for file reference examination
 71|3. **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Proceed automatically through file reference check, stop on failure
 72|4. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status for file reference check
 73|5. **PRINT**: Progress updates for file reference check
 74|6. Generate quick report with file reference findings
 75|
 76|## Architect Failure Handling Patterns
 77|
 78|### Full Comprehensive Mode Failure Pattern
 79|1. Detect failure in current consistency variable check
 80|2. **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Continue workflow automatically, logging the failure
 81|3. **RETRY LOGIC**: Implement configurable retry with exponential backoff (max 3 retries)
 82|4. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "variable_{N}_failed" but continue workflow
 83|5. **PRINT**: Failure message but continue to next consistency variable
 84|6. Proceed to next consistency variable automatically
 85|
 86|### Basic Essential Mode Failure Pattern
 87|1. Detect failure in current essential variable check
 88|2. **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Stop workflow automatically without requiring human intervention
 89|3. **RETRY LOGIC**: Implement configurable retry with exponential backoff (max 3 retries)
 90|4. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "variable_{N}_failed"
 91|5. **PRINT**: Failure message with retry attempt information
 92|6. Proceed with retry logic automatically, stop if max retries reached
 93|
 94|### Targeted Mode Failure Pattern
 95|1. Detect failure in current selected variable check
 96|2. **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Stop workflow automatically without requiring human intervention
 97|3. **RETRY LOGIC**: Implement configurable retry with exponential backoff (max 3 retries)
 98|4. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "variable_{N}_failed"
 99|5. **PRINT**: Failure message with retry attempt information
100|6. Proceed with retry logic automatically, stop if max retries reached
101|
102|### Quick Check Mode Failure Pattern
103|1. Detect failure in file reference check
104|2. **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Stop workflow automatically without requiring human intervention
105|3. **RETRY LOGIC**: Implement configurable retry with exponential backoff (max 3 retries)
106|4. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "file_reference_failed"
107|5. **PRINT**: Failure message with retry attempt information
108|6. Proceed with retry logic automatically, stop if max retries reached
109|
110|## Architect Execution Mode Selection Guidelines
111|
112|### Full Comprehensive Mode Selection
113|- Monthly comprehensive architecture validation
114|- Before major architectural changes
115|- After major architectural refactoring
116|- Complete governance health assessment
117|- When comprehensive baseline is needed
118|
119|### Basic Essential Mode Selection
120|- Weekly basic architecture validation
121|- Quick validation before minor changes
122|- Essential consistency health check
123|- When core architecture validation is sufficient
124|- Time-constrained validation needs
125|
126|### Targeted Mode Selection
127|- Investigating specific architectural concerns
128|- Validating specific consistency variables
129|- Focused architecture validation
130|- When specific areas need attention
131|- User has specific validation requirements
132|
133|### Quick Check Mode Selection
134|- Pre-change validation for file references
135|- Quick reference validation
136|- Rapid architecture validation
137|- When only file reference integrity is needed
138|- Time-critical validation needs
139|
140|## Architect Retry Logic with Exponential Backoff
141|
142|### Retry Configuration
143|- **Max Retries**: 3 retries maximum
144|- **Backoff Pattern**: Exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, etc.)
145|- **Retry Criteria**: Configurable based on error type
146|- **Retry Logging**: Log each retry attempt with metadata
147|- **Variable Retry**: For targeted checks, retry individual consistency variables
148|
149|### Retry Implementation
150|```python
151|retry_count = 0
152|max_retries = 3
153|backoff_time = 1
154|
155|while retry_count < max_retries:
156|    try:
157|        # Execute consistency variable check
158|        execute_consistency_check()
159|        break  # Success, exit retry loop
160|    except Exception as error:
161|        retry_count += 1
162|        if retry_count >= max_retries:
163|            raise  # Max retries reached
164|        time.sleep(backoff_time)
165|        backoff_time *= 2  # Exponential backoff
166|```
167|
168|## Architect State Management
169|
170|### Mode Storage
171|- **Mode Storage**: Store selected execution mode in workflow state
172|- **Variable Selection**: Store selected consistency variables for Targeted mode
173|- **Current Variable**: Track current consistency variable being checked
174|- **Failure Context**: Store failure context for retry logic
175|
176|### Audit Trail
177|- **Mode Selection**: Log mode selection with reasoning
178|- **Variable Processing**: Log each consistency variable with outcomes
179|- **Failure Handling**: Log failure handling patterns and recovery actions
180|- **Report Generation**: Log report generation with consistency metrics
</file-view>

  1|# Quality Assessment Framework
  2|
  3|**Purpose**: Universal quality assessment framework for all agent workflows.
  4|
  5|## Universal Quality Dimensions
  6|
  7|### Dimension 1: Accuracy
  8|**What it scores**: Factual correctness and alignment with requirements
  9|
 10|**Universal Evaluation Criteria**:
 11|- Work output accurately reflects user requirements
 12|- Steps/codes correctly identify needed changes
 13|- Dependencies/relationships are technically accurate
 14|- No false claims or incorrect assumptions
 15|- Changes/approaches are feasible for implementation
 16|
 17|**Universal Scoring Levels**:
 18|- **5 (Excellent)**: All information accurate, perfect alignment with requirements
 19|- **4 (Good)**: Minor inaccuracies that don't affect implementation
 20|- **3 (Fair)**: Some inaccuracies that may require clarification
 21|- **2 (Poor)**: Significant inaccuracies affecting implementation
 22|- **1 (Critical)**: Major factual errors that would cause implementation failure
 23|
 24|**Hard Fail**: Goal/work misalignment with user requirements or technically impossible changes
 25|
 26|---
 27|
 28|### Dimension 2: Completeness
 29|**What it scores**: Inclusion of all necessary elements
 30|
 31|**Universal Evaluation Criteria**:
 32|- All required sections/patterns present
 33|- Metadata complete where applicable
 34|- Steps/codes cover all aspects of needed changes
 35|- Dependencies account for all relationships
 36|- No missing critical information for implementation
 37|
 38|**Universal Scoring Levels**:
 39|- **5 (Excellent)**: All elements present, fully comprehensive
 40|- **4 (Good)**: Minor omissions that don't affect implementation
 41|- **3 (Fair)**: Some omissions that may require clarification
 42|- **2 (Poor)**: Significant omissions affecting implementation
 43|- **1 (Critical)**: Critical missing elements that would cause implementation failure
 44|
 45|**Hard Fail**: Missing required sections or metadata
 46|
 47|---
 48|
 49|### Dimension 3: Clarity
 50|**What it scores**: Readability and understandability
 51|
 52|**Universal Evaluation Criteria**:
 53|- Goal/statement is clear and user-focused
 54|- Steps/codes are unambiguous and actionable
 55|- Language is precise and not vague
 56|- Context provides necessary background
 57|- Dependencies/relationships are clearly expressed

 59|**Universal Scoring Levels**:
 60|- **5 (Excellent)**: Crystal clear, unambiguous, easy to follow
 61|- **4 (Good)**: Minor ambiguities that can be resolved with context
 62|- **3 (Fair)**: Some ambiguities requiring clarification
 63|- **2 (Poor)**: Significant ambiguities affecting implementation
 64|- **1 (Critical)**: Unclear goals or steps that would cause implementation confusion
 65|
 66|**Hard Fail**: Ambiguous goal statement or unclear critical steps

 77|- No circular dependencies or contradictions

 97|- Context provides necessary background and dependencies
 98|- Rationale is clear and supports the approach
 99|- Context is sufficient for implementation decisions
100|
101|**Universal Scoring Levels**:
102|- **5 (Excellent)**: Rich context, perfect rationale, comprehensive background
103|- **4 (Good)**: Minor context gaps that don't affect implementation
104|- **3 (Fair)**: Some context gaps requiring clarification
105|- **2 (Poor)**: Significant context gaps affecting implementation
106|- **1 (Critical)**: Missing critical context that would cause implementation failure
107|
108|**Hard Fail**: Missing context or rationale for critical decisions

112|## Universal Quality Scoring
113|
114|### Universal Weighting
115|- **Accuracy**: 30% (most critical)
116|- **Completeness**: 25% (critical)
117|- **Clarity**: 20% (important)
118|- **Structure**: 15% (important)
119|- **Context**: 10% (supporting)
120|
121|### Quality Score Calculation
122|```
123|Overall Score = (Accuracy Ã— 0.30) + (Completeness Ã— 0.25) + (Clarity Ã— 0.20) + (Structure Ã— 0.15) + (Context Ã— 0.10)
124|```
125|
126|### Universal Quality Thresholds
127|- **5.0 - 4.5**: Excellent - Clean pass, proceed to next phase
128|- **4.4 - 3.5**: Good - Clean pass, proceed to next phase
129|- **3.4 - 2.5**: Fair - Proceed with documented rationale
130|- **2.4 - 1.5**: Poor - Requires revisions before proceeding
131|- **1.4 - 0.0**: Critical - Block proceeding, mandatory revisions
132|
133|### Hard Fail Conditions
134|If any dimension has a hard fail, the overall quality score is automatically **0.0** regardless of other dimensions.

  1|# Architect Option Criteria
  2|
  3|**Purpose**: Architect-specific criteria for generating and evaluating implementation options.
  4|
  5|## Universal Pattern Reference
  6|
  7|See Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Quality_Assessment_Framework.md for universal quality assessment patterns including:
  8|- Universal quality assessment dimensions and scoring rubrics
  9|- Universal quality evaluation criteria
 10|- Universal quality assessment framework
 11|
 12|## Architect Option Criteria Specifications
 13|
 14|### Viable Option Criteria
 15|
 16|**Different Mechanism of Action**
 17|- Options must represent distinct approaches, not cosmetic variations
 18|- Each option should use a fundamentally different method or technique
 19|- Avoid options that are essentially the same approach with minor differences
 20|- Ensure meaningful differentiation between options
 21|
 22|**Feasible Execution**
 23|- Options must be aligned with available time, budget, and capabilities
 24|- Consider resource constraints and limitations
 25|- Ensure options are realistically implementable
 26|- Account for technical and operational feasibility
 27|
 28|**Evaluability**
 29|- Options must be assessable against defined criteria
 30|- Enable clear comparison and evaluation
 31|- Provide measurable outcomes and success criteria
 32|- Allow for objective assessment and selection
 33|
 34|## Option Requirements
 35|
 36|### Each Option Must Include
 37|
 38|**Summary**
 39|- Clear description of what the option does
 40|- Explanation of the approach and methodology
 41|- Overview of expected outcomes
 42|- Key characteristics and features
 43|
 44|**Impact Score (out of 10)**
 45|- Assessment of the option's impact on the system
 46|- Reasoning for the impact score
 47|- Consideration of both positive and negative impacts
 48|- Alignment with architectural goals
 49|
 50|**Effort Score (out of 10)**
 51|- Assessment of implementation effort required
 52|- Reasoning for the effort score
 53|- Consideration of time, resources, and complexity
 54|- Feasibility within project constraints
 55|
 56|**Risk Score (out of 10)**
 57|- Assessment of potential risks and uncertainties
 58|- Reasoning for the risk score
 59|- Consideration of technical, operational, and business risks
 60|- Mitigation strategies for identified risks
 61|
 62|## Option Generation Process
 63|
 64|### Research-Based Generation
 65|- Base options on research findings and best practices
 66|- Consider industry standards and established patterns
 67|- Incorporate lessons learned from similar implementations
 68|- Ensure options are grounded in current best practices
 69|
 70|### Architect Opinion Framework
 71|- Provide analysis and recommendation BEFORE user selection
 72|- Explain reasoning behind recommendations
 73|- Consider trade-offs between options
 74|- Align with architectural principles and constraints
 75|
 76|### Presentation Pattern
 77|- Present options with clear metrics and scores
 78|- Provide architect opinion alongside objective criteria
 79|- Use popup menu for user selection
 80|- Ensure transparency in evaluation process
 81|
 82|### Rule Enforcement
 83|- Ensure options comply with Rules/Architect/Architect_Rules.md
 84|- Validate options against governance constraints
 85|- Consider security and compliance requirements
 86|- Ensure options align with architectural boundaries
 87|
 88|## Usage Guidelines
 89|
 90|### When Generating Options
 91|1. **Research First**: Conduct thorough research before generating options
 92|2. **Apply Criteria**: Use viable option criteria to filter and refine options
 93|3. **Score Objectively**: Score options objectively using defined metrics
 94|4. **Provide Context**: Include reasoning and context for each score
 95|5. **Recommend Wisely**: Provide architect opinion based on analysis
 96|
 97|### When Evaluating Options
 98|1. **Review Criteria**: Review option criteria for compliance
 99|2. **Assess Scores**: Evaluate impact, effort, and risk scores
100|3. **Consider Trade-offs**: Weigh pros and cons of each option
101|4. **Validate Compliance**: Ensure options comply with architectural rules
102|5. **Select Appropriately**: Select option that best meets requirements
</file-view>
```

  1|# Validation Enforcement Patterns
  2|
  3|**Purpose**: Universal validation enforcement patterns for all agent workflows.
  4|
  5|## Validation Enforcement Overview
  6|
  7|**EVERY STEP HAS A VALIDATION REQUIREMENT**: Each workflow step includes a mandatory validation that must pass before proceeding to the next step.
  8|
  9|## Validation Rules
 10|
 11|- Validation verification must be explicit and actionable
 12|- Validation must have clear PASS/FAIL criteria
 13|- Validation failures must stop progression until resolved
 14|- Validation results must be documented in conversation log
 15|- Validation should validate completion, quality, and compliance of the step
 16|
 17|## Validation Pattern
 18|
 19|1. Perform the step's actions
 20|2. Document the results in conversation log
 21|3. Run the step's validation verification
 22|4. Validation must pass to proceed to next step
 23|5. If validation fails, stop and address the issue
 24|
 25|## Compliance Requirement
 26|
 27|- Skipping any validation is a SCOPE VIOLATION per AGENTS.md
 28|- The validation system provides enforcement for all workflow steps
 29|- Each step is validated individually for comprehensive compliance
 30|- Template compliance requires validation enforcement rules to be defined
 31|
 32|## Agent-Specific Customization
 33|
 34|Each agent should define:
 35|- **Validation Specifications**: Agent-specific validation definitions and criteria
 36|- **Validation System Execution**: Agent-specific validation scripts and commands
 37|- **Validation System Reference**: Agent-specific references to rules, quality frameworks, and delivery processes

 40|

 44|3. **Implement Validation Verification**: Create agent-specific validation scripts
 45|4. **Integrate with Workflow**: Integrate validation enforcement into workflow phases

 47|

 49|- **Universal Rules**: All agents follow the same validation rules
 50|- **Agent-Specific Validation**: Each agent defines its own validation specifications

 52|- **Universal Compliance**: Same compliance requirement (validation cannot be skipped)

  1|# Planner Plan Batch Specifications
  2|
  3|**Purpose**: Planner-specific plan batch execution patterns and scan plan categorization.
  4|
  5|## Plan Batch Structure
  6|
  7|### Batch Execution Pattern
  8|Plans are organized in batches of 5 plans per batch for systematic processing and issue resolution.
  9|
 10|### Plan Numbering Pattern
 11|- **Standard Plans**: Plans 1-4, 6-9, 11-14, 16-19, 21-24, 26-29, 31-34, 36-39 (regular planning tasks)
 12|- **Scan Plans**: Plans 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40 (every 5th plan is a scan plan)
 13|
 14|### Scan Plan Purpose
 15|Scan plans (5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40) are specifically designed to:
 16|- Identify and fix issues discovered in previous plans
 17|- Perform systematic system scans for problems
 18|- Address accumulated issues from previous batch execution
 19|- Provide quality control and system health checks
 20|
 21|## Batch Processing Workflow
 22|
 23|### Batch Structure
 24|```
 25|Batch 1: Plans 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 (Plan 5 = Scan Plan)
 26|Batch 2: Plans 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 (Plan 10 = Scan Plan)
 27|Batch 3: Plans 11, 12, 13, 14, 15 (Plan 15 = Scan Plan)
 28|Batch 4: Plans 16, 17, 18, 19, 20 (Plan 20 = Scan Plan)
 29|Batch 5: Plans 21, 22, 23, 24, 25 (Plan 25 = Scan Plan)
 30|Batch 6: Plans 26, 27, 28, 29, 30 (Plan 30 = Scan Plan)
 31|Batch 7: Plans 31, 32, 33, 34, 35 (Plan 35 = Scan Plan)
 32|Batch 8: Plans 36, 37, 38, 39, 40 (Plan 40 = Scan Plan)
 33|```
 34|
 35|### Standard Plan Characteristics
 36|- **Purpose**: Implement specific features or changes
 37|- **Content**: Regular planning tasks following standard template
 38|- **Execution**: Direct implementation by executor
 39|- **Validation**: Standard validation and delivery process
 40|
 41|### Scan Plan Characteristics
 42|- **Purpose**: Fix issues from previous plans, system health checks
 43|- **Content**: Issue identification, problem resolution, system scans
 44|- **Execution**: Issue-fixing and system maintenance
 45|- **Validation**: Enhanced validation focusing on issue resolution
 46|
 47|## Workflow Integration
 48|
 49|### Planner Workflow Modification
 50|The Planner workflow should:
 51|1. **Batch Mode**: Process plans sequentially through batch (return to Phase 0 after each plan for next plan in sequence)
 52|2. **Single Plan Mode**: Process single plan and terminate (no return to Phase 0)
 53|3. **Follow batch sequence**: Process plans in numerical order when in batch mode
 54|4. **Identify scan plans**: Recognize plan numbers 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40
 55|5. **Apply scan plan logic**: Use different approach for scan plans
 56|6. **Track batch progress**: Monitor batch completion status
 57|
 58|### Scan Plan Detection Logic
 59|```python
 60|def is_scan_plan(plan_number):
 61|    return plan_number % 5 == 0
 62|
 63|def get_plan_type(plan_number):
 64|    if is_scan_plan(plan_number):
 65|        return "scan_plan"
 66|    else:
 67|        return "standard_plan"
 68|```
 69|
 70|### Execution Pattern
 71|1. **Standard Plan**: Follow normal workflow â†’ Save to Plans/ â†’ Execute
 72|2. **Scan Plan**: Enhanced workflow â†’ Scan for issues â†’ Fix problems â†’ Save to Plans/ â†’ Execute
 73|3. **Batch Completion**: After each 5th plan, batch is complete
 74|4. **Next Batch**: Continue with next batch sequence
 75|
 76|## Plan Storage and Organization
 77|
 78|### Directory Structure
 79|```
 80|Plans/
 81|â”œâ”€â”€ plan-1.md
 82|â”œâ”€â”€ plan-2.md
 83|â”œâ”€â”€ plan-3.md
 84|â”œâ”€â”€ plan-4.md
 85|â”œâ”€â”€ plan-5.md (scan plan)
 86|â”œâ”€â”€ plan-6.md
 87|â”œâ”€â”€ plan-7.md
 88|â”œâ”€â”€ plan-8.md
 89|â”œâ”€â”€ plan-9.md
 90|â”œâ”€â”€ plan-10.md (scan plan)
 91|â””â”€â”€ ...
 92|```
 93|
 94|### Plan Metadata
 95|Each plan should include:
 96|- **Plan Number**: Sequential number in batch sequence
 97|- **Plan Type**: Standard or Scan
 98|- **Batch Number**: Which batch this plan belongs to
 99|- **Previous Issues**: Issues found in previous plans (for scan plans)
100|- **Issue Resolution**: How scan plan addresses issues
101|
102|## Usage Guidelines
103|
104|### When Creating Standard Plans
105|1. Follow standard planning workflow
106|2. Use standard plan template
107|3. Focus on feature implementation
108|4. Save with sequential numbering
109|5. Mark as standard plan type
110|
111|### When Creating Scan Plans
112|1. Review previous plans in batch for issues
113|2. Perform system scan for problems
114|3. Create issue-fixing plan
115|4. Use enhanced validation for issue resolution
116|5. Mark as scan plan type
117|6. Document issue resolution approach
118|
119|### Batch Management
120|1. Track which plans have been completed
121|2. Monitor batch progress
122|3. Ensure scan plans address relevant issues
123|4. Validate batch completion before proceeding
124|5. Maintain plan sequence integrity
</file-view>
```

  5|**Status**: âœ… **IMPLEMENTED** - Basic quota tracking for internal subagents
  6|
  7|## Overview
  8|
  9|This document describes patterns for handling quota exhaustion during agent execution, with specific focus on internal subagents that are used in Round Table reviews and other multi-agent coordination scenarios.
 10|
 11|## Implementation Scope
 12|
 13|**Implemented**:
 14|- Basic quota tracking for internal subagents
 15|- Step progress tracking for quota awareness
 16|- Simple recovery patterns for quota exhaustion

 22|
 23|## Context
 24|
 25|**External Agents**: External services (e.g., Chathub.gg) are not subject to quota limitations for this system.
 26|
 27|**Internal Subagents**: Internal subagents used in Round Table reviews and other multi-agent operations are subject to quota limitations and require tracking and recovery mechanisms.
 28|
 29|## Basic Quota Tracking Pattern
 30|
 31|### Internal Subagent Quota Awareness
 32|- **Step Tracking**: Track step progress for internal subagents to understand quota consumption
 33|- **Quota Estimation**: Estimate quota usage per step based on typical token consumption
 34|- **Quota Monitoring**: Monitor quota status before launching internal subagents
 35|- **Fallback Planning**: Have backup plans if quota exhaustion occurs
 36|
 37|### Recovery Pattern for Internal Subagents
 38|- **Quota Exhaustion Detection**: Monitor for quota exhaustion signals during subagent execution
 39|- **Step Recovery**: Resume from last completed step if quota exhaustion occurs
 40|- **Partial Results**: Use partial results from completed steps if full execution fails
 41|- **Escalation**: Escalate to user if quota exhaustion prevents completion
 42|
 43|## Implementation Requirements (Basic)
 44|
 45|### Workflow Integration
 46|- Add quota awareness checks before launching internal subagents
 47|- Track step progress for internal subagents
 48|- Implement fallback mechanisms for quota exhaustion
 49|- Add quota status reporting in workflow logs
 50|
 51|### Subagent Guidelines
 52|- Internal subagents should be designed for efficient quota usage
 53|- Implement step-by-step progress reporting
 54|- Provide checkpoint-style output for recovery
 55|- Design for graceful degradation on quota exhaustion
 56|
 57|## Implementation Status
 58|
 59|**Currently Implemented**:
 60|- Basic quota tracking in Planner workflow for internal Round Table reviews
 61|- Step progress tracking for internal subagents
 62|- Manual quota monitoring and fallback patterns
 63|
 64|**Requires Future Implementation**:

 66|- Full state persistence for subagent sessions
 67|- Agent-to-agent state synchronization protocols
 68|- Audit trail for quota events
 69|

 71|

 73|- Plan work within quota limits for subagent operations
 74|- Implement manual checkpoint strategies for long-running tasks
 75|- Monitor quota usage during execution

  1|# Convergence Loop Patterns
  2|
  3|**Purpose**: Universal convergence loop patterns for iterative improvement processes across all agent workflows.
  4|
  5|## Universal Convergence Loop Pattern
  6|
  7|### Loop Structure
  8|- **Loop Definition**: Iterative process between phases until convergence criteria are met
  9|- **Back-Edge Pattern**: Return to previous phase after current phase completion
 10|- **Loop Exit Condition**: Quality thresholds or stability criteria achieved
 11|- **Loop Cap**: Maximum iterations to prevent infinite loops
 12|
 13|### Convergence Logic
 14|1. **Execute Current Phase**: Complete current phase actions
 15|2. **Evaluate Results**: Assess phase outcomes against convergence criteria
 16|3. **Check Convergence**: Determine if convergence criteria are met
 17|4. **Exit if Converged**: Proceed to next phase if convergence achieved
 18|5. **Loop if Not Converged**: Return to previous phase and iterate
 19|
 20|### Universal Convergence Criteria
 21|- **Quality Score Threshold**: Quality metrics meet defined thresholds
 22|- **Stability Metrics**: Results stabilize across iterations
 23|- **Issue Resolution**: Critical and high-priority issues resolved
 24|- **Panel/Expert Agreement**: Expert consensus achieved (when applicable)
 25|
 26|### Universal Loop Caps
 27|- **Maximum Iterations**: Define maximum iterations per loop type
 28|- **Escalation Procedures**: Define escalation when loop cap reached
 29|- **User Intervention**: Define when to request user decision
 30|- **Alternative Strategies**: Define alternative approaches when loops fail
 31|
 32|## Agent-Specific Customization
 33|
 34|Each agent should define:
 35|- **Loop Definitions**: Agent-specific phase loop structures
 36|- **Convergence Criteria**: Agent-specific quality thresholds and stability metrics
 37|- **Loop Caps**: Agent-specific iteration limits
 38|- **Escalation Procedures**: Agent-specific escalation when loops fail
 39|
 40|## Usage Guidelines
 41|
 42|### Universal Pattern Application
 43|1. **Apply Universal Pattern**: Use the universal convergence loop pattern for iterative improvement
 44|2. **Define Agent-Specific Loops**: Create agent-specific loop definitions in agent Reference/ folders
 45|3. **Set Convergence Criteria**: Define agent-specific quality thresholds and stability metrics
 46|4. **Implement Loop Logic**: Integrate convergence logic into workflow phases
 47|5. **Document Escalation**: Document escalation procedures for loop failures

  5|This workflow follows AI planning best practices with:

  8|- **Convergence-based iteration**: Internal and external Round Table loops until convergence

 15|- **Batch processing**: Plans organized in batches of 5 with scan plans for issue resolution

  1|# Executor Execution Mode Patterns
  2|
  3|**Purpose**: Executor-specific execution mode patterns for plan execution workflows.
  4|
  5|## Executor Execution Mode Definitions
  6|
  7|### Manual Mode
  8|**Behavior**: Require user confirmation at each function implementation step for maximum oversight
  9|- **Checkpoint Handling**: Require user confirmation via popup menu before proceeding to each function implementation
 10|- **Failure Handling**: Stop workflow and await user intervention for retry/modify/abort decision
 11|- **User Control**: Maximum user control over function-by-function progression
 12|- **Risk Mitigation**: Human oversight at each function implementation
 13|- **Use Case**: Critical implementations, complex functions, learning phase
 14|
 15|### Auto Mode
 16|**Behavior**: Execute functions automatically without user confirmation, stopping on errors
 17|- **Checkpoint Handling**: Proceed automatically through function implementations
 18|- **Failure Handling**: Stop workflow automatically if function implementation or tests fail
 19|- **User Control**: Minimal user control with automated function implementation
 20|- **Risk Mitigation**: Automatic failure detection and stopping at function level
 21|- **Use Case**: Standard implementations, well-understood patterns, established processes
 22|
 23|### Complete Mode
 24|**Behavior**: Execute functions automatically without user confirmation, continuing past failures
 25|- **Checkpoint Handling**: Proceed automatically through all function implementations
 26|- **Failure Handling**: Continue workflow automatically, ignoring function implementation failures
 27|- **User Control**: Minimal user control with maximum automated implementation
 28|- **Risk Mitigation**: Minimal risk mitigation, maximum efficiency
 29|- **Use Case**: Experimental implementations, rapid prototyping, non-critical code
 30|
 31|## Executor Execution Mode Handling Patterns
 32|
 33|### Manual Mode Pattern
 34|1. **{BP}** web search for current best practices before file creation/modification
 35|2. Implement single function from plan
 36|3. **{BP}** web search for current testing best practices before test file creation
 37|4. Create test file and run quality checks
 38|5. **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Require user confirmation via popup menu before proceeding to next function (CHECKPOINT)
 39|6. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "function_{N}_complete"
 40|7. **PRINT**: Function completion message with BP research findings and checkpoint confirmation
 41|8. Wait for user approval before proceeding to next function
 42|
 43|### Auto Mode Pattern
 44|1. **{BP}** web search for current best practices before file creation/modification
 45|2. Implement single function from plan
 46|3. **{BP}** web search for current testing best practices before test file creation
 47|4. Create test file and run quality checks
 48|5. **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Proceed automatically to next function if function succeeded, stop if function failed
 49|6. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "function_{N}_complete" (success) or "function_{N}_failed" (failure)
 50|7. **PRINT**: Function completion message (success) or failure message with retry attempt information
 51|8. Proceed automatically to next function on success, apply retry logic on failure
 52|
 53|### Complete Mode Pattern
 54|1. **{BP}** web search for current best practices before file creation/modification
 55|2. Implement single function from plan (even if failures occur)
 56|3. **{BP}** web search for current testing best practices before test file creation
 57|4. Create test file and run quality checks
 58|5. **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Proceed automatically to next function regardless of success/failure
 59|6. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "function_{N}_complete" (even if function failed)
 60|7. **PRINT**: Function completion message (including any failures but continue workflow)
 61|8. Proceed to next function automatically
 62|
 63|## Executor Failure Handling Patterns
 64|
 65|### Manual Mode Failure Pattern
 66|1. Detect failure in current function implementation or testing
 67|2. **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Stop workflow and await user intervention for retry/modify/abort decision (CHECKPOINT)
 68|3. **RETRY LOGIC**: Implement configurable retry with exponential backoff (max 3 retries) upon user approval
 69|4. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "function_{N}_failed"
 70|5. **PRINT**: Failure message with function-level error details and BP research context
 71|6. Await user decision on recovery action
 72|
 73|### Auto Mode Failure Pattern
 74|1. Detect failure in current function implementation or testing
 75|2. **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Stop workflow automatically without requiring human intervention
 76|3. **RETRY LOGIC**: Implement configurable retry with exponential backoff (max 3 retries)
 77|4. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "function_{N}_failed"
 78|5. **PRINT**: Failure message with retry attempt information and BP research context
 79|6. Proceed with retry logic automatically
 80|
 81|### Complete Mode Failure Pattern
 82|1. Detect failure in current function implementation or testing
 83|2. **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Continue workflow automatically, ignoring the failure
 84|3. **RETRY LOGIC**: Implement configurable retry with exponential backoff (max 3 retries)
 85|4. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "function_{N}_complete" (despite failure)
 86|5. **PRINT**: Failure message but continue workflow
 87|6. Proceed to next function automatically
 88|
 89|## Executor BP Research Integration
 90|
 91|### BP Research Requirements
 92|- **CRITICAL REQUIREMENT**: Before any file creation or modification, perform **{BP}** web search for current best practices
 93|- **CRITICAL REQUIREMENT**: Before test file creation, perform **{BP}** web search for current testing best practices
 94|- **Documentation**: Document BP research findings and apply relevant best practices to implementation
 95|- **Presentation**: Present BP research findings alongside function results to user
 96|- **Validation**: Verify BP research was conducted and applied for all file operations in final validation
 97|
 98|### BP Research Process
 99|1. Analyze the specific function or file being created/modified
100|2. **{BP}** web search for current best practices relevant to the specific implementation
101|3. Document findings and determine applicable best practices
102|4. Apply relevant best practices to the implementation
103|5. Include BP research findings in function presentation to user
104|6. Document BP research findings in handoff to Reviewer agent
105|
106|## Executor Retry Logic with Exponential Backoff
107|
108|### Retry Configuration
109|- **Max Retries**: 3 retries maximum
110|- **Backoff Pattern**: Exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, etc.)
111|- **Retry Criteria**: Configurable based on error type
112|- **Retry Logging**: Log each retry attempt with metadata
113|- **Function Retry**: For function implementation failures, retry specific function or related components
114|
115|### Retry Implementation
116|```python
117|retry_count = 0
118|max_retries = 3
119|backoff_time = 1
120|
121|while retry_count < max_retries:
122|    try:
123|        # Execute function implementation
124|        implement_function()
125|        break  # Success, exit retry loop
126|    except Exception as error:
127|        retry_count += 1
128|        if retry_count >= max_retries:
129|            raise  # Max retries reached
130|        time.sleep(backoff_time)
131|        backoff_time *= 2  # Exponential backoff
132|```
133|
134|## Executor State Management
135|
136|### Mode Storage
137|- **Mode Storage**: Store selected execution mode in workflow state
138|- **Function Progress**: Track current function number and implementation status
139|- **BP Research Log**: Store BP research findings for each function
140|- **Failure Context**: Store failure context for retry logic
141|
142|### Audit Trail
143|- **Mode Selection**: Log mode selection with reasoning
144|- **Function Processing**: Log each function with BP research findings and outcomes
145|- **Failure Handling**: Log failure handling patterns and recovery actions
146|- **BP Research Documentation**: Log all BP research conducted during implementation
147|- **User Checkpoints**: Log user checkpoint decisions in Manual mode
148|
149|## Executor Execution Mode Selection Guidelines
150|
151|### Manual Mode Selection
152|- Critical infrastructure implementations
153|- Complex algorithm implementations
154|- Security-critical code modifications
155|- When learning new patterns or technologies
156|- User wants maximum oversight of each function
157|
158|### Auto Mode Selection
159|- Standard plan implementations
160|- Well-understood implementation patterns
161|- When user wants some automation with safety
162|- Routine function implementations
163|- Established codebase patterns
164|
165|### Complete Mode Selection
166|- Experimental or prototyping implementations
167|- Non-critical feature implementations
168|- When user wants maximum automation
169|- Rapid prototyping or exploration
170|- Tasks where function failures are acceptable
</file-view>
