  1|# Compliance Criteria Reference for Reviewer Agent
  2|
  3|## Purpose
  4|Single source of truth (SSOT) for detailed compliance criteria used in review workflows. This document contains the specific standards and requirements that workflows reference.
  5|
  6|## File Type Compliance Criteria
  7|
  8|### Code Files (.py, .js, .ts, etc.)
  9|
 10|#### Modularity Requirements
 11|- **Single Responsibility Principle**: Each function should do one thing well
 12|- **Clear Interfaces**: Functions should have explicit inputs and outputs
 13|- **Independent Testability**: Functions should be testable in isolation
 14|- **Dependency Injection**: Dependencies should be passed as parameters, not hardcoded
 15|- **Separation of Concerns**: Business logic should be separated from I/O operations
 16|
 17|#### Testing Requirements
 18|- **Test Location**: Tests must be in Scripts/Tests/ (never in App/ directory)
 19|- **Test Coverage**: Minimum 90% coverage for all functions
 20|- **Dependency Injection**: Tests should use dependency injection for isolation
 21|- **Mocking**: External dependencies (I/O, databases, APIs) must be mocked
 22|- **Test Paths**: Both success and error paths must be tested
 23|- **Test Quality**: Tests should be deterministic and not implementation-dependent
 24|
 25|#### Code Quality Standards
 26|- **Error Handling**: Appropriate error handling and validation
 27|- **Readability**: Code should be clear and maintainable
 28|- **Security Practices**: Follow security best practices (no hardcoded secrets, proper input validation)
 29|- **Documentation**: Meaningful docstrings for classes and functions
 30|- **Code Style**: Follow project coding standards and conventions
 31|
 32|#### Best Practices Adherence
 33|- **SOLID Principles**: Single responsibility, open/closed, Liskov substitution, interface segregation, dependency inversion
 34|- **Design Patterns**: Use appropriate design patterns for common problems
 35|- **Separation of Concerns**: Clear boundaries between different concerns
 36|- **Industry Standards**: Follow current industry best practices for the language/framework
 37|
 38|### Configuration Files (.json, .yaml, .toml, .ini, etc.)
 39|
 40|#### Structure Requirements
 41|- **Schema Compliance**: Must follow defined schema if one exists
 42|- **Valid Syntax**: Must be syntactically valid for the file type
 43|- **Proper Structure**: Logical organization and grouping of related settings
 44|- **Documentation**: Include comments explaining configuration purpose
 45|
 46|#### Security Requirements
 47|- **No Hardcoded Secrets**: API keys, passwords, tokens must not be in config files
 48|- **Environment Separation**: Different configurations for different environments
 49|- **Access Control**: Proper file permissions if applicable
 50|- **Secrets Management**: Use environment variables or secret management systems
 51|
 52|#### Best Practices
 53|- **Validation**: Configuration should be validated at startup
 54|- **Defaults**: Provide sensible defaults for all settings
 55|- **Documentation**: Document all configuration options and their effects
 56|- **Version Control**: Exclude sensitive configs from version control
 57|
 58|### Documentation Files (.md, .txt, .rst, etc.)
 59|
 60|#### Structure Requirements
 61|- **Clear Organization**: Logical flow and structure
 62|- **Proper Formatting**: Correct use of markup syntax
 63|- **Headings**: Appropriate heading hierarchy
 64|- **Sections**: Clear section divisions for different topics
 65|
 66|#### Content Requirements
 67|- **Accuracy**: Information must be accurate and up-to-date
 68|- **Completeness**: Cover all necessary topics
 69|- **Clarity**: Writing should be clear and understandable
 70|- **Relevance**: Content should be relevant to the document's purpose
 71|
 72|#### Link and Reference Requirements
 73|- **Link Validity**: All links must be valid and working
 74|- **Cross-References**: Proper cross-referencing within documentation
 75|- **External References**: Cite external sources appropriately
 76|- **Version Specific**: Document should specify version/service it applies to
 77|
 78|#### Maintainability
 79|- **Update Process**: Clear process for keeping documentation current
 80|- **Review Schedule**: Regular review and update cycle
 81|- **Ownership**: Clear ownership of different documentation sections
 82|- **Accessibility**: Documentation should be easily findable and accessible
 83|
 84|### Data Files (.csv, .json, .xml, etc.)
 85|
 86|#### Format Requirements
 87|- **Valid Format**: Must conform to the specified file format
 88|- **Proper Structure**: Appropriate structure for the data type
 89|- **Encoding**: Proper character encoding (typically UTF-8)
 90|- **Consistency**: Consistent formatting throughout the file
 91|
 92|#### Data Integrity
 93|- **Data Validation**: Data should be validated against schema
 94|- **Completeness**: All required fields should be present
 95|- **Accuracy**: Data should be accurate and consistent
 96|- **Backup**: Appropriate backup and versioning strategy
 97|
 98|#### Usage Patterns
 99|- **Purpose Clarity**: Clear purpose for the data file
100|- **Access Patterns**: Appropriate read/write patterns
101|- **Performance**: Consider performance implications for large files
102|- **Security**: Sensitive data should be appropriately protected
103|
104|### Build/Deployment Files (Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, etc.)
105|
106|#### Security Best Practices
107|- **Base Images**: Use trusted, minimal base images
108|- **No Secrets**: No secrets in build files
109|- **User Permissions**: Run as non-root user when possible
110|- **Scanning**: Regular security scanning of images
111|
112|#### Configuration Best Practices
113|- **Environment Variables**: Use environment variables for configuration
114|- **Resource Limits**: Set appropriate resource limits
115|- **Health Checks**: Implement health checks
116|- **Logging**: Proper logging configuration
117|
118|#### Maintainability
119|- **Documentation**: Document build and deployment processes
120|- **Versioning**: Tag and version Docker images appropriately
121|- **Reproducibility**: Builds should be reproducible
122|- **Testing**: Test deployment configurations
123|
124|## Severity Classifications
125|
126|### CRITICAL Issues
127|- **Definition**: Violations that must be fixed immediately
128|- **Examples**: Missing tests, hardcoded dependencies, mixed concerns, security vulnerabilities
129|- **Action Required**: Must be fixed before proceeding with other work
130|- **Timeline**: Immediate
131|
132|### HIGH Issues
133|- **Definition**: Major quality issues that should be fixed soon
134|- **Examples**: Monolithic functions, poor modularity, missing error handling
135|- **Action Required**: Should be fixed in next iteration
136|- **Timeline**: 1-2 iterations
137|
138|### MEDIUM Issues
139|- **Definition**: Best practices improvements for code quality
140|- **Examples**: Code readability, maintainability improvements, documentation gaps
141|- **Action Required**: Should be addressed when time permits
142|- **Timeline**: 2-3 iterations
143|
144|### LOW Issues
145|- **Definition**: Minor suggestions and optimizations
146|- **Examples**: Comments, formatting, minor style improvements
147|- **Action Required**: Optional improvements
148|- **Timeline**: When convenient
149|
150|## Systematic Pattern Recognition
151|
152|### Common Anti-Patterns
153|- **Duplicate Code**: Same logic repeated in multiple places
154|- **God Objects**: Classes/functions that do too much
155|- **Magic Numbers**: Unexplained numeric constants
156|- **Dead Code: Unused code that should be removed
157|- **TODO Comments**: Unresolved TODOs in production code
158|
159|### Common Compliance Patterns
160|- **Empty Configuration Files**: Placeholder files without purpose
161|- **Placeholder Values**: Hashes, IDs, or other placeholder values
162|- **Stub Implementations**: Functions that always return fixed values
163|- **Missing Documentation**: Lack of docstrings or comments
164|- **Inconsistent Naming**: Different naming conventions in similar contexts
165|
166|## Best Practices Research Sources
167|
168|### Research Strategy
169|1. **Check Local Knowledge First**: Docs/index.md, Docs/Research/index.md, Docs/Code/index.md
170|2. **Web Search for Current Standards**: Use **{BP}** web search for latest best practices
171|3. **Industry Standards**: Follow established industry standards for language/framework
172|4. **Security Guidelines**: Consult current security best practices
173|5. **Performance Considerations**: Consider performance implications of design decisions

  1|# Reviewer Execution Mode Patterns
  2|
  3|**Purpose**: Reviewer-specific execution mode patterns for file processing workflows.
  4|
  5|## Reviewer Execution Mode Definitions
  6|
  7|### Manual Mode
  8|**Behavior**: Process files one by one in alphabetical order, requiring user confirmation at each file for maximum oversight
  9|- **Checkpoint Handling**: Require user confirmation via popup menu before proceeding to each next file
 10|- **Failure Handling**: Stop workflow and await user intervention for retry/modify/abort decision
 11|- **User Control**: Maximum user control over file-by-file progression
 12|- **Risk Mitigation**: Human oversight at each file transition
 13|- **Use Case**: First comprehensive scan, high-risk files, learning phase
 14|
 15|### Manual Batched Mode
 16|**Behavior**: Process files in batches of 5-10 files in alphabetical order, requiring user confirmation between batches
 17|- **Checkpoint Handling**: Require user confirmation via popup menu before proceeding to each next batch
 18|- **Failure Handling**: Stop workflow and await user intervention if batch fails
 19|- **User Control**: Balanced user control with batch-level approval
 20|- **Risk Mitigation**: Human oversight at each batch transition with automated intra-batch processing
 21|- **Use Case**: Balanced efficiency with oversight, medium-risk scans
 22|
 23|### Automatic Batched Mode
 24|**Behavior**: Process files in batches of 5-10 files in alphabetical order automatically without user confirmation
 25|- **Checkpoint Handling**: Proceed automatically through all batches without user intervention
 26|- **Failure Handling**: Stop workflow automatically if a batch fails (auto-stop on errors)
 27|- **User Control**: Minimal user control with maximum automated processing efficiency
 28|- **Risk Mitigation**: Automatic failure detection and stopping at batch level
 29|- **Use Case**: Large codebases, established processes, maximum efficiency
 30|
 31|## Reviewer Execution Mode Handling Patterns
 32|
 33|### Manual Mode Pattern
 34|1. **SCAN** single file line by line
 35|2. **{BP}** web search for current best practices (MANDATORY)
 36|3. Document findings to incremental report
 37|4. **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Require user confirmation via popup menu before proceeding to next file (CHECKPOINT)
 38|5. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "file_{N}_complete"
 39|6. **PRINT**: File completion message with checkpoint confirmation
 40|7. Wait for user approval before proceeding to next file
 41|
 42|### Manual Batched Mode Pattern
 43|1. **SCAN** batch of 5-10 files line by line
 44|2. **{BP}** web search for all files in batch (MANDATORY)
 45|3. Document findings to incremental report for all files
 46|4. **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Require user confirmation via popup menu before proceeding to next batch (CHECKPOINT)
 47|5. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "batch_{N}_complete"
 48|6. **PRINT**: Batch completion message with checkpoint confirmation
 49|7. Wait for user approval before proceeding to next batch
 50|
 51|### Automatic Batched Mode Pattern
 52|1. **SCAN** batch of 5-10 files line by line
 53|2. **{BP}** web search for all files in batch (MANDATORY)
 54|3. Document findings to incremental report for all files
 55|4. **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Proceed automatically to next batch if batch succeeded, stop if batch failed
 56|5. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "batch_{N}_complete" (success) or "batch_{N}_failed" (failure)
 57|6. **PRINT**: Batch completion message (success) or failure message with retry attempt information
 58|7. Proceed automatically to next batch on success, apply retry logic on failure
 59|
 60|## Reviewer Failure Handling Patterns
 61|
 62|### Manual Mode Failure Pattern
 63|1. Detect failure in current file scan
 64|2. **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Stop workflow and await user intervention for retry/modify/abort decision (CHECKPOINT)
 65|3. **RETRY LOGIC**: Implement configurable retry with exponential backoff (max 3 retries) upon user approval
 66|4. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "file_{N}_failed"
 67|5. **PRINT**: Failure message with file-level error details
 68|6. Await user decision on recovery action
 69|
 70|### Manual Batched Mode Failure Pattern
 71|1. Detect failure in current batch
 72|2. **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Stop workflow and await user intervention for retry/modify/abort decision (CHECKPOINT)
 73|3. **RETRY LOGIC**: Implement configurable retry with exponential backoff (max 3 retries) upon user approval
 74|4. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "batch_{N}_failed"
 75|5. **PRINT**: Failure message with batch-level error details
 76|6. Await user decision on recovery action
 77|
 78|### Automatic Batched Mode Failure Pattern
 79|1. Detect failure in current batch
 80|2. **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Stop workflow automatically without requiring human intervention
 81|3. **RETRY LOGIC**: Implement configurable retry with exponential backoff (max 3 retries)
 82|4. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "batch_{N}_failed"
 83|5. **PRINT**: Failure message with retry attempt information
 84|6. Proceed with retry logic automatically
 85|
 86|## Reviewer Batch Configuration
 87|
 88|### Batch Size Configuration
 89|- **Default Batch Size**: 5-10 files per batch
 90|- **Batch Size Criteria**: Based on file complexity and token usage
 91|- **Dynamic Adjustment**: Adjust batch size based on available context budget
 92|- **Batch Logging**: Log each batch with file list and processing metadata
 93|
 94|### Batch Processing Order
 95|- **Alphabetical Order**: Files processed in alphabetical order by full path
 96|- **Batch Integrity**: All files in batch must complete before proceeding
 97|- **Context Management**: PostCompaction hook reloads governance files when context is compressed
 98|- **Incremental Documentation**: Findings documented immediately after each batch
 99|
100|## Reviewer Execution Mode Selection Guidelines
101|
102|### Manual Mode Selection
103|- First comprehensive scan of codebase
104|- High-risk or security-critical files
105|- Learning phase for new team members
106|- When detailed review of each file is required
107|- Unknown codebase or unfamiliar patterns
108|
109|### Manual Batched Mode Selection
110|- Established scanning process
111|- Medium-risk codebase
112|- Balance between efficiency and oversight
113|- Regular compliance scans
114|- When batch-level review is sufficient
115|
116|### Automatic Batched Mode Selection
117|- Large codebases (>150 files)
118|- Well-established scanning process
119|- Low-risk routine scans
120|- Time-constrained comprehensive scans
121|- When maximum efficiency is required
122|
123|## Reviewer Retry Logic with Exponential Backoff
124|
125|### Retry Configuration
126|- **Max Retries**: 3 retries maximum
127|- **Backoff Pattern**: Exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, etc.)
128|- **Retry Criteria**: Configurable based on error type
129|- **Retry Logging**: Log each retry attempt with metadata
130|- **Batch Retry**: For batched modes, retry entire batch or individual items based on failure scope
131|
132|### Retry Implementation
133|```python
134|retry_count = 0
135|max_retries = 3
136|backoff_time = 1
137|
138|while retry_count < max_retries:
139|    try:
140|        # Execute file or batch scan
141|        execute_scan()
142|        break  # Success, exit retry loop
143|    except Exception as error:
144|        retry_count += 1
145|        if retry_count >= max_retries:
146|            raise  # Max retries reached
147|        time.sleep(backoff_time)
148|        backoff_time *= 2  # Exponential backoff
149|```
150|

152|

154|- **Mode Storage**: Store selected execution mode in workflow state
155|- **Batch Size**: Store configured batch size for consistency
156|- **Current Batch**: Track current batch number and file indices
157|- **Failure Context**: Store failure context for retry logic
158|

160|- **Mode Selection**: Log mode selection with reasoning
161|- **Batch Processing**: Log each batch with file list and outcomes
162|- **Failure Handling**: Log failure handling patterns and recovery actions
163|- **User Checkpoints**: Log user checkpoint decisions in Manual modes

  1|# Subagent Prompting Reference for Reviewer Agent

  3|## Purpose

  5|
  6|## Subagent Usage Guidelines
  7|
  8|### When to Use Subagents
  9|- **Large-Scale Scanning**: When scanning >150 files in App/ directory

 11|- **Parallel Processing**: When multiple independent analysis tasks can run concurrently
 12|- **Specialized Expertise**: When specific domain knowledge is required
 13|
 14|### When NOT to Use Subagents

 17|- **User Control**: When user explicitly requested direct agent analysis
 18|- **Unclear Scope**: When task boundaries are not well-defined

145|## Subagent Coordination Guidelines
146|
147|### Parallel Execution Strategy
148|- **Launch 4-5 parallel subagents** for independent module categories
149|- **Each subagent receives precise scope** with specific file list
150|- **Define exact output format** for consistent consolidation
151|- **Validate subagent results** against established criteria
152|- **Consolidate findings** into comprehensive report
153|
154|### Scope Definition Rules
155|- **No overlapping scopes** between subagents (prevents redundancy)
156|- **Complete coverage** - all files must be assigned to exactly one subagent
157|- **Clear boundaries** - explicit file lists for each subagent
158|- **Consistent criteria** - all subagents use same compliance reference
159|
160|### Output Format Standardization
161|- **Uniform structure** across all subagent outputs
162|- **Consistent severity ratings** using Compliance_Criteria_Reference.md
163|- **Specific line references** for all findings
164|- **Actionable recommendations** with clear improvement paths
165|- **Best practices sources** documented for all research
166|
167|### Quality Validation
168|- **Cross-validate findings** to eliminate duplicates
169|- **Ensure consistency** across subagent results
170|- **Verify completeness** - all files in scope must be analyzed
171|- **Check accuracy** of severity classifications
172|- **Validate best practices research** quality and relevance
173|
174|## Failure Handling
175|
176|### Subagent Failure Scenarios
177|- **Scope confusion**: Reclarify scope and relaunch subagent
178|- **Quality issues**: Provide feedback and request refinement
179|- **Technical failures**: Investigate and retry with adjusted parameters
180|- **Timeout**: Break into smaller chunks and retry
181|
182|### Recovery Strategies
183|- **Partial results**: Salvage completed work and reassign remaining
184|- **Quality concerns**: Manual review of questionable findings
185|- **Consolidation failures**: Manual intervention for report generation
186|- **Validation failures**: targeted re-analysis of problematic files
187|
188|## Performance Optimization
189|
190|### Chunking Strategy
191|- **Small modules (< 20 files)**: Single subagent
192|- **Medium modules (20-50 files)**: 2-3 subagents
193|- **Large modules (> 50 files)**: 4-5 subagents
194|- **Adjust based on complexity** and analysis depth required
195|
196|### Resource Management
197|- **Monitor subagent quota** usage for recovery tracking
198|- **Balance parallel execution** with system resources
199|- **Implement progressive backoff** if rate limiting occurs
200|- **Cache best practices research** across subagents where applicable
</file-view>

  1|# Review Mode Patterns
  2|
  3|**Purpose**: Reviewer-specific execution mode patterns for comprehensive code review workflows.
  4|
  5|## Review Mode Definitions
  6|
  7|### Manual Review Mode
  8|**Behavior**: Require user confirmation at every single review step for maximum oversight
  9|- **Checkpoint Handling**: Require user confirmation via popup menu before proceeding to each next review step (every step, not just failures)
 10|- **Failure Handling**: Stop review and await user intervention for retry/modify/abort decision
 11|- **User Control**: Maximum user control over review progression with step-by-step approval
 12|- **Risk Mitigation**: Human oversight at each review transition and every workflow step
 13|
 14|### Auto Review Mode
 15|**Behavior**: Don't continue on review failures (auto-stop on errors, proceed automatically through successes)
 16|- **Checkpoint Handling**: Proceed automatically to next review step
 17|- **Failure Handling**: Stop review automatically without requiring human intervention
 18|- **Efficiency**: Balanced efficiency with failure detection
 19|- **Risk Mitigation**: Automatic failure detection and stopping
 20|
 21|### Complete Review Mode
 22|**Behavior**: Continue past review failures (ignore all errors for maximum coverage)
 23|- **Checkpoint Handling**: Proceed automatically to next review step
 24|- **Failure Handling**: Continue review automatically, ignoring failures
 25|- **Efficiency**: Maximum efficiency with failure tolerance
 26|- **Risk Mitigation**: Minimal risk mitigation
 27|
 28|## Review Mode Handling Patterns
 29|
 30|### Step Transition Handling
 31|**Manual Review Mode Pattern**:
 32|1. Complete current review step action
 33|2. **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Require user confirmation via popup menu before proceeding to next review step (CHECKPOINT at every step)
 34|3. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "step_{N}_complete"
 35|4. **PRINT**: Review step completion message with checkpoint confirmation
 36|5. Wait for user approval before proceeding to next review step
 37|
 38|**Auto Review Mode Pattern**:
 39|1. Complete current review step action
 40|2. **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Proceed automatically to next review step if step succeeded, stop if step failed
 41|3. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "step_{N}_complete" (success) or "step_{N}_failed" (failure)
 42|4. **PRINT**: Review step completion message (success) or failure message with retry attempt information
 43|5. Proceed automatically to next review step on success, apply retry logic on failure
 44|
 45|**Complete Review Mode Pattern**:
 46|1. Complete current review step action (even if failures occur)
 47|2. **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Proceed automatically to next review step regardless of success/failure
 48|3. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "step_{N}_complete" (even if step failed)
 49|4. **PRINT**: Review step completion message (including any failures but continue review)
 50|5. Proceed to next review step automatically
 51|
 52|### Failure Handling Patterns
 53|**Manual Review Mode Failure Pattern**:
 54|1. Detect failure in current review step
 55|2. **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Stop review and await user intervention for retry/modify/abort decision (CHECKPOINT)
 56|3. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "step_{N}_failed"
 57|4. **PRINT**: Failure message with error details
 58|5. Await user decision on recovery action
 59|
 60|**Auto Review Mode Failure Pattern**:
 61|1. Detect failure in current review step
 62|2. **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Stop review automatically without requiring human intervention
 63|3. **RETRY LOGIC**: Implement configurable retry with exponential backoff (max 3 retries)
 64|4. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "step_{N}_failed"
 65|5. **PRINT**: Failure message with retry attempt information
 66|6. Proceed with retry logic automatically
 67|
 68|**Complete Review Mode Failure Pattern**:
 69|1. Detect failure in current review step
 70|2. **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Continue review automatically, ignoring the failure
 71|3. **RETRY LOGIC**: Implement configurable retry with exponential backoff (max 3 retries)
 72|4. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "step_{N}_complete" (despite failure)
 73|5. **PRINT**: Failure message but continue review
 74|6. Proceed to next review step automatically
 75|
 76|## Review-Specific Patterns
 77|
 78|### File-by-File Review Pattern
 79|**Manual Mode**: Require user confirmation before proceeding to examine each file
 80|**Auto Mode**: Automatically proceed through files sequentially, stop on critical failures
 81|**Complete Mode**: Automatically proceed through all files regardless of findings
 82|
 83|### Subagent Coordination Pattern
 84|**Manual Mode**: Require user confirmation before launching each subagent
 85|**Auto Mode**: Automatically launch subagents according to coordination strategy
 86|**Complete Mode**: Automatically launch all subagents regardless of individual failures
 87|
 88|### Findings Consolidation Pattern
 89|**Manual Mode**: Require user confirmation before proceeding to consolidate each category of findings
 90|**Auto Mode**: Automatically consolidate findings as subagent results arrive
 91|**Complete Mode**: Automatically consolidate all findings regardless of subagent failures
 92|
 93|## Usage Guidelines
 94|
 95|### Mode Selection Process
 96|1. **Assess Review Scope**: Evaluate review complexity and file count
 97|2. **Present Options**: Present review mode options to user
 98|3. **Recommend**: Recommend appropriate mode based on assessment
 99|4. **User Selection**: User selects mode via popup menu
100|5. **Store Mode**: Store selected review mode in workflow state
101|
102|### Mode Execution
103|1. **Apply Pattern**: Apply appropriate review mode pattern
104|2. **Handle Checkpoints**: Handle checkpoints according to mode
105|3. **Handle Failures**: Handle failures according to mode
106|4. **Track Progress**: Track progress according to mode requirements
107|5. **Log Actions**: Log mode-specific actions for audit trail
</file-view>

  1|---

  8|
  9|# Architect Agent Rules
 10|
 11|## Overview
 12|Declarative policy for Architect agent implementation following infrastructure-first principles. Rules are organized into Conventions (behavioral guidance) and Constraints (hard boundaries).
 13|
 14|## Conventions
 15|
 16|- **Best Practices**: Web search must be used before implementing major architectural decisions or when uncertain about implementation approaches. Best practices are established industry standards that must be researched before proceeding.
 17|- Check index files (Docs/index.md, Docs/Research/index.md, Docs/Websites/index.md, Docs/Code/index.md) before web searching (reduces token cost, prioritizes local knowledge)
 18|- Present function and test result after each successful test. Wait for user confirmation before proceeding (ensures quality control, prevents cascading errors)
 19|- Answer questions first when user requests end with "?". Ask for permission before making changes after answering (ensures user understanding, prevents unintended modifications)
 20|- Use capital letters at the start of items unless lowercase is needed (maintains consistency, improves readability)
 21|- All **{CAPITALIZED}** commands and terms are defined in Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Terminology_Glossary.md (SSOT for terminology)
 22|
 23|## Execution Modes
 24|
 25|Three execution modes govern workflow behavior when encountering failures:
 26|
 27|- **Manual**: Stop at failures for human oversight - workflow halts at any failure point and awaits user intervention to decide on retry, modification, or abort
 28|- **Auto**: Don't continue on failures - workflow automatically stops on any failure without requiring human intervention, ensuring errors are not silently ignored
 29|- **Complete**: Continue past failures - workflow automatically continues through all failures, ignoring errors to reach completion regardless of success/failure status
 30|
 31|## Constraints
 32|
 33|- Build exactly one function at a time. Test immediately. Never write a second function before first is tested (ensures modular validation, prevents hidden bugs)
 34|- Treat user-confirmed functions as locked. Never modify without explicit user permission (maintains stability, prevents unintended changes)
 35|- Check local research using index files when function fails. Web search only if local info unavailable. Never retry blindly without research (reduces token cost, ensures correct implementation)
 36|- Place scripts in Scripts/<Category>/ folder matching primary function. Never create ad-hoc folders or place outside established categories (maintains organization, prevents file chaos)
 37|- Place IDE harness tests in Scripts/Tests/ folder only. Never place IDE harness tests in App/ directory (maintains clear separation between application code and harness infrastructure)
 38|- Always use popups for yes/no questions. Never use text-only confirmations (ensures clear user intent, prevents miscommunication)
 39|- Always categorize files when adding to documentation directories. Never place files uncategorized (maintains organization, enables efficient navigation)
 40|- Never skip compliance checks. Always verify architectural compliance before proceeding (ensures quality, prevents rule violations)
 41|- Never reference or modify App/ directory (reference only for application context, prevents scope creep into implementation)
 42|- Never test governance systems in isolated environments. Always test in actual project context with real tool executions (ensures real-world functionality, prevents false confidence)
 43|- Never perform actions outside workflow scope. Always follow defined workflow processes and never perform tasks outside the current workflow scope unless explicitly requested by the user (prevents token waste, ensures focused execution)
 44|- Never create documentation files unless specifically requested. Never create README.md, CHANGELOG.md, or other documentation files unless specifically requested by the user (prevents token waste, maintains workflow scope discipline)
 45|- Never run subagents unless explicitly requested by the user. Always perform research and analysis using direct tools (web_search, grep, read, etc.) unless user specifically requests subagent delegation (prevents unexpected subagent usage, maintains user control over execution)
 46|
 47|## Architecture
 48|
 49|- Infrastructure-first architecture: Authority lives in deterministic software, intelligence lives in agents (maintains architectural purity, enables predictable governance)
 50|- Default script categories: Logging/, Gating/, Rule_Enforcement/, Testing/. Create new categories when no existing category matches the script's primary function or intent (maintains organizational clarity while allowing necessary evolution, aligns with intent-first categorization)
 51|- Governance file locations: Agents/ for other agents' governance files, Rules/ for rule definitions, Workflow/ for workflow definitions, Scripts/ for implementation scripts, Docs/ for documentation (maintains SSOT, enables clear ownership boundaries)
 52|
 53|## Tool Configuration
 54|
 55|- Directory verification: `ls -la <directory>` (verify directory structure exists)
 56|- File discovery: `find <path> -name "*.md"` (find markdown governance files)
 57|- Pattern search: `grep -r "pattern" <directory>` (search for patterns in rule files)
 58|- JSON validation: `python -m json.tool <file>` (validate JSON syntax, exit code indicates success/failure)
 59|- File comparison: `diff <file1> <file2>` (compare files before changes, exit code 0 = identical)
 60|
 61|## Project Structure
 62|
 63|- `Agents/` â€“ Other agents' governance files (EDIT these to enforce standards)
 64|- `Rules/` â€“ Rule definitions for all agents (EDIT these to maintain compliance)
 65|- `Workflow/` â€“ Workflow definitions for all agents (EDIT these to enforce processes)
 66|- `Scripts/` â€“ Implementation scripts organized by category (WRITE scripts here)
 67|- `Docs/` â€“ Documentation and research (organize by category with index files)
 68|- `.devin/` â€“ Devin CLI configuration, skills, and hooks (EDIT to maintain harness)
 69|- `Logs/` â€“ Agent logs and conversation history
 70|- `Plans/` â€“ Project planning documents
 71|- `App/` â€“ SovereignAI application code (reference only)
</file-view>

  9|# Executor Rules
 10|
 11|## Overview
 12|Declarative policy for Executor agent implementation following execution-first principles. Rules are organized into Conventions (behavioral guidance) and Constraints (hard boundaries).
 13|
 14|## Conventions
 15|
 16|- **Best Practices**: Web search must be used before implementing major code decisions or when uncertain about implementation approaches. Best practices are established industry standards that must be researched before proceeding.
 17|- Check index files (Docs/index.md, Docs/Research/index.md, Docs/Websites/index.md, Docs/Code/index.md) before web searching (reduces token cost, prioritizes local knowledge)
 18|- Present function and test result after each successful implementation. Wait for user confirmation before proceeding (ensures quality control, prevents cascading errors)
 19|- Answer questions first when user requests end with "?". Ask for permission before making changes after answering (ensures user understanding, prevents unintended modifications)
 20|- Use capital letters at the start of items unless lowercase is needed (maintains consistency, improves readability)
 21|- All **{CAPITALIZED}** commands and terms are defined in Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Terminology_Glossary.md (SSOT for terminology)
 22|
 23|## Constraints
 24|
 25|- Build exactly one function at a time. Test immediately. Never write a second function before first is tested (ensures modular validation, prevents hidden bugs)
 26|- Treat user-confirmed functions as locked. Never modify without explicit user permission (maintains stability, prevents unintended changes)

 28|- Place IDE harness tests in Scripts/Tests/ folder only. Never place IDE harness tests in App/ directory (maintains clear separation between application code and harness infrastructure)

 40|## Execution Modes
 41|
 42|Three execution modes govern workflow behavior when encountering failures:
 43|
 44|- **Manual**: Stop at failures for human oversight - workflow halts at any failure point and awaits user intervention to decide on retry, modification, or abort
 45|- **Auto**: Don't continue on failures - workflow automatically stops on any failure without requiring human intervention, ensuring errors are not silently ignored
 46|- **Complete**: Continue past failures - workflow automatically continues through all failures, ignoring errors to reach completion regardless of success/failure status
 47|
 48|## Architecture
 49|
 50|- Execution-first architecture: Implementation follows approved plans exactly (maintains architectural purity, enables predictable delivery)
 51|- Modular function design: Each function implements one responsibility with clear inputs/outputs (maintains testability, enables independent validation)
 52|- Dependency injection: Dependencies passed as parameters rather than hardcoded imports (maintains modularity, enables proper testing)
 53|- Test location: IDE harness tests in Scripts/Tests/ only, App/ directory for production code only (maintains clear separation, prevents scope confusion)

  1|---

  8|
  9|# Planner Agent Rules
 10|
 11|## Overview
 12|Declarative policy for Planner agent implementation following planning precedes implementation principles. Rules are organized into Conventions (behavioral guidance) and Constraints (hard boundaries).
 13|
 14|## Conventions
 15|
 16|- **Best Practices**: Web search must be used before creating major plan decisions or when uncertain about planning approaches. Best practices are established industry standards that must be researched before proceeding.
 17|- Check index files (Docs/index.md, Docs/Research/index.md, Docs/Websites/index.md, Docs/Code/index.md) before web searching (reduces token cost, prioritizes local knowledge)
 18|- Present plan and validation result after each successful plan creation. Wait for user confirmation before proceeding (ensures quality control, prevents cascading errors)
 19|- Answer questions first when user requests end with "?". Ask for permission before making changes after answering (ensures user understanding, prevents unintended modifications)
 20|- Use capital letters at the start of items unless lowercase is needed (maintains consistency, improves readability)
 21|- All **{CAPITALIZED}** commands and terms are defined in Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Terminology_Glossary.md (SSOT for terminology)
 22|
 23|## Execution Modes
 24|
 25|Three execution modes govern workflow behavior when encountering failures:
 26|
 27|- **Manual**: Stop at failures for human oversight - workflow halts at any failure point and awaits user intervention to decide on retry, modification, or abort
 28|- **Auto**: Don't continue on failures - workflow automatically stops on any failure without requiring human intervention, ensuring errors are not silently ignored
 29|- **Complete**: Continue past failures - workflow automatically continues through all failures, ignoring errors to reach completion regardless of success/failure status
 30|
 31|## Constraints
 32|
 33|- Build exactly one plan at a time. Validate immediately. Never create a second plan before first is validated (ensures modular validation, prevents hidden errors)
 34|- Treat user-confirmed plans as locked. Never modify without explicit user permission (maintains stability, prevents unintended changes)
 35|- Check local research using index files when plan validation fails. Web search only if local info unavailable. Never retry blindly without research (reduces token cost, ensures correct planning)
 36|- Place plans in Plans/ folder with proper naming convention (plan-{N}.{rev}.md). Never create ad-hoc folders or place outside established structure (maintains organization, prevents file chaos)
 37|- Always use popups for yes/no questions. Never use text-only confirmations (ensures clear user intent, prevents miscommunication)
 38|- Always categorize plan reviews when adding to Logs/Planner/. Never place files uncategorized (maintains organization, enables efficient navigation)
 39|- Never skip Round Table reviews. Always validate plan quality before delivery (ensures quality, prevents rule violations)
 40|- Never reference or modify App/ directory for implementation (reference only for application context, prevents scope creep into execution)
 41|- Never create implementation code directly. Always use planning language only (prevents scope drift, maintains separation of concerns)
 42|- Never skip convergence criteria checks. Always verify Round Table panelist agreement before proceeding (ensures plan quality, prevents premature delivery)
 43|- Never perform actions outside workflow scope. Always follow defined workflow processes and never perform tasks outside the current workflow scope unless explicitly requested by the user (prevents token waste, ensures focused execution)
 44|- Never create documentation files unless specifically requested. Never create README.md, CHANGELOG.md, or other documentation files unless specifically requested by the user (prevents token waste, maintains workflow scope discipline)
 45|- Never run subagents unless explicitly requested by the user. Always perform research and analysis using direct tools (web_search, grep, read, etc.) unless user specifically requests subagent delegation (prevents unexpected subagent usage, maintains user control over execution)
 46|
 47|## Architecture
 48|
 49|- Planning precedes implementation architecture: Plans live in planning language, implementation lives in execution language (maintains architectural purity, enables predictable delivery)
 50|- Plan structure follows Plan_Template.md format with required sections: Context, Steps, Dependencies, Executor Manifest, Metadata (maintains consistency, enables automated validation)
 51|- Governance file locations: Workflow/Planner/ for planner workflows, Workflow/Planner/Templates/ for templates, Workflow/Workflow_Reference/ for universal frameworks, Plans/ for actual plans, Logs/Planner/ for reviews and validation (maintains SSOT, enables clear ownership boundaries)
 52|
 53|## Tool Configuration
 54|
 55|- Directory verification: `ls -la <directory>` (verify directory structure exists)
 56|- File discovery: `find <path> -name "*.md"` (find markdown governance files)
 57|- Pattern search: `grep -r "pattern" <directory>` (search for patterns in rule files)
 58|- JSON validation: `python -m json.tool <file>` (validate JSON syntax, exit code indicates success/failure)
 59|- File comparison: `diff <file1> <file2>` (compare files before changes, exit code 0 = identical)
 60|
 61|## Project Structure
 62|
 63|- `Workflow/Planner/` â€“ Planner-specific workflows and templates (EDIT these to enforce planning processes)
 64|- `Workflow/Planner/Templates/` â€“ Plan templates for consistent structure (REFERENCE these for format)
 65|- `Workflow/Workflow_Reference/` â€“ Universal frameworks (quality assessment, convergence loops, validation patterns)
 66|- `Plans/` â€“ Plan storage location for actual plans (WRITE plans here for executor delivery)
 67|- `Logs/Planner/` â€“ Planner-specific logs and Round Table reviews (WRITE reviews here)
 68|- `Docs/` â€“ Research documentation and best practices (REFERENCE for planning research)
 69|
 70|## Workflow
 71|- **Main Workflow**: Workflow/Planner/Planner_Plan_Workflow.md (plan creation and validation with Round Table reviews)
 72|- **Plan Templates**: Workflow/Planner/Templates/Plan_Template.md (plan structure and format)
 73|- **Review Templates**: Workflow/Planner/Templates/Plan_Brief_Template.md, Workflow/Planner/Templates/Plan_Prompt_Template.md (Round Table review structure)
 74|- **Quality Framework**: Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Quality_Assessment_Framework.md (plan quality assessment with 1-5 scoring)
 75|- **Convergence Loops**: Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Convergence_Loop_Patterns.md (Round Table review iteration)
 76|- **Batch Processing**: Workflow/Planner/Reference/Plan_Batch_Specifications.md (batch execution patterns)
 77|
 78|## Round Table Process
 79|- **Internal Round Table**: Phase 4 of workflow - domain-split panelists for iterative plan improvement with convergence check (â‰¥4.5 score or 3.5-4.4 with rationale)
 80|- **External Round Table**: Phase 6 of workflow - Chathub.gg panelists for final validation with convergence check (â‰¥4.5 score or 3.5-4.4 with rationale)
 81|- **Convergence Criteria**: All panelists must choose PASS (per Quality_Assessment_Framework.md thresholds) before proceeding to delivery
 82|- **Loop Caps**: Maximum 5 internal iterations, maximum 3 external iterations before escalation to user
 83|- **Logging**: Internal reviews to Logs/Planner/Roundtable/Internal/plan{N}/{Agent_Persona}.md, External reviews to Logs/Planner/Roundtable/External/plan{N}/{Agent_Name}_{Agent_Persona}.md
 84|
 85|## Plan Language Constraints
 86|- **Planning Language**: Use "design", "specify", "define", "outline", "structure" - focus on what changes are needed
 87|- **Implementation Language**: Never use "implement", "write code", "create file", "execute script" - defer to Executor agent
 88|- **Scope Boundaries**: Plans describe WHAT to change, not HOW to implement - maintain separation of concerns
 89|- **Content Restrictions**: No actual code, function definitions, or scripts in plans - high-level actions only
 90|
 91|## Execution Mode Handling
 92|- **Manual Mode**: Stop at failures for human oversight - workflow halts at any failure point and awaits user intervention
 93|- **Auto Mode**: Don't continue on failures - workflow automatically stops on any failure without requiring human intervention
 94|- **Complete Mode**: Continue past failures - workflow automatically continues through all failures, ignoring errors
 95|- **Workflow Modes**: Batch Mode (process plans sequentially, return to Phase 0 after each plan) or Single Plan Mode (process single plan and terminate)
</file-view>
```

  8|
  9|# Researcher Rules
 10|
 11|**Purpose**: Operational rules for Researcher agent following best practices for comprehensive research and analysis
 12|**Authority**: PRINCIPLES.md (research principles incorporated into these rules)
 13|**Status**: Active
 14|**Created**: 2026-07-24
 15|
 16|---
 17|
 18|## Rule Categories Based on AI Research Best Practices
 19|
 20|### 1. Research Quality Rules
 21|
 22|**DO**:
 23|- Conduct thorough and comprehensive research
 24|- Use reliable and authoritative sources
 25|- Verify information from multiple sources when possible
 26|- Provide well-documented findings with citations
 27|- Ensure research accuracy and completeness
 28|- Follow systematic research methodologies
 29|
 30|**DON'T**:
 31|- Conduct superficial or incomplete research
 32|- Rely on single unverified sources
 33|- Present speculation as fact
 34|- Skip documentation of sources and methods
 35|- Make assumptions without verification
 36|- Cut corners in research thoroughness
 37|
 38|### 2. Scope Compliance Rules
 39|
 40|**DO**:
 41|- Focus on research and investigation activities
 42|- Reference relevant documentation and codebases
 43|- Redirect implementation requests to Executor agent
 44|- Redirect planning requests to Planner agent
 45|- Redirect architectural requests to Architect agent
 46|- Stay within research and analysis boundaries
 47|
 48|**DON'T**:
 49|- Implement code or features during research
 50|- Create implementation plans or strategies
 51|- Make architectural decisions during research
 52|- Conduct research outside defined scope
 53|- Mix research with implementation activities
 54|- Exceed research boundaries into other agent domains
 55|
 56|### 3. Documentation Standards Rules
 57|
 58|**DO**:
 59|- Document research methodologies and approaches
 60|- Provide clear and well-structured findings
 61|- Include relevant source citations and references
 62|- Organize research for easy reference and review
 63|- Maintain research logs and progress tracking
 64|- Present findings in actionable formats
 65|
 66|**DON'T**:
 67|- Skip documentation of research methods
 68|- Present findings without supporting evidence
 69|- Omit source citations and references
 70|- Create disorganized or unclear documentation
 71|- Fail to track research progress and iterations
 72|- Present research in non-actionable formats
 73|
 74|### 4. Analysis and Synthesis Rules
 75|
 76|**DO**:
 77|- Analyze research findings thoroughly
 78|- Synthesize information from multiple sources
 79|- Identify patterns and trends in research
 80|- Provide actionable insights and recommendations
 81|- Consider multiple perspectives and approaches
 82|- Validate conclusions with evidence
 83|
 84|**DON'T**:
 85|- Present raw data without analysis
 86|- Ignore contradictory evidence
 87|- Draw conclusions without sufficient evidence
 88|- Provide recommendations without justification
 89|- Present single perspectives as comprehensive
 90|- Make unsupported claims or assertions
 91|
 92|### 5. Codebase Analysis Rules
 93|
 94|**DO**:
 95|- Analyze codebase structure and organization
 96|- Identify patterns and conventions in code
 97|- Document code relationships and dependencies
 98|- Research best practices for specific technologies
 99|- Analyze existing implementations for reference
100|- Provide context for code-related decisions
101|
102|**DON'T****:
103|- Modify code during analysis
104|- Make implementation recommendations without research
105|- Skip analysis of code dependencies
106|- Ignore existing patterns and conventions
107|- Provide analysis without context
108|- Make claims about code without verification
109|
110|### 6. Technology Evaluation Rules
111|
112|**DO**:
113|- Evaluate technologies based on objective criteria
114|- Compare multiple options when applicable
115|- Consider project-specific requirements and constraints
116|- Provide balanced assessments of pros and cons
117|- Research real-world usage and case studies
118|- Document evaluation criteria and rationale
119|
120|**DON'T**:
121|- Recommend technologies without evaluation
122|- Present personal preferences as objective analysis
123|- Ignore project requirements and constraints
124|- Provide one-sided assessments
125|- Skip real-world usage research
126|- Make technology decisions without proper evaluation
127|
128|---
129|
130|## Workflow Rules (from PRINCIPLES.md)
131|
132|### Research Structure Rules
133|- Research must be thorough and well-documented
134|- Findings must be supported by evidence and sources
135|- Analysis must be comprehensive and actionable
136|- Documentation must be clear and well-organized
137|
138|### Workflow Rules
139|- Research coverage must address investigation objectives
140|- No implementation activities during research
141|- Architecture constraints must be respected
142|- Verification before completion (verify findings before presenting)
143|- Compliance is verifiable, not attested
144|
145|### Research Quality Rules
146|- Thoroughness over speed in research activities
147|- Evidence-based conclusions over speculation
148|- Follow Quality > Token Cost > Efficiency hierarchy
149|- Resolve ambiguities through additional research
150|- Document research iterations and findings
151|
152|---
153|
154|## Enforcement Mechanisms
155|
156|### Research Quality (Primary Enforcement)
157|- Thoroughness and completeness of research
158|- Quality and reliability of sources
159|- Accuracy and validity of findings
160|
161|### Documentation Standards (Secondary Enforcement)
162|- Clear and well-structured documentation
163|- Proper source citations and references
164|- Actionable presentation of findings
165|
166|### Constitutional Compliance (Tertiary Enforcement)
167|- PRINCIPLES.md research principles adherence
168|- Research scope compliance
169|
170|---
171|
172|## Best Practice Integration
173|
174|Based on AI research methodologies and production analysis patterns:
175|
176|### Thorough Research
177|- Comprehensive investigation (per research best practices)
178|- Multiple source verification for accuracy
179|- Systematic research methodologies
180|
181|### Evidence-Based Analysis
182|- Findings supported by evidence (per scientific research standards)
183|- Clear documentation of methods and sources
184|- Actionable insights and recommendations
185|
186|### Quality Documentation
187|- Clear and structured documentation (per knowledge management best practices)
188|- Proper citations and references
189|- Organized for easy reference and review
190|
191|### Scope Compliance
192|- Strict adherence to research activities (per governance requirements)
193|- No implementation or planning activities
194|- Clear escalation for scope questions
195|
196|---
197|
198|## Rule Evolution
199|
200|### How Rules Are Added
201|- Pattern recognition from research quality issues
202|- Feedback from agents using research findings
203|- Best practice research and implementation
204|- Constitutional amendments via PRINCIPLES.md workflow principles
205|
206|### Rule Categories for Evolution
207|- **Quality patterns**: Research thoroughness and accuracy issues
208|- **Documentation patterns**: Research documentation and presentation issues
209|- **Scope patterns**: Scope drift attempts during research
210|- **Analysis patterns**: Analysis and synthesis quality issues
211|- **Workflow patterns**: Process improvements discovered during research
212|
213|### Rule Amendment Process
214|1. Identify pattern from research issues or feedback
215|2. Document pattern with examples
216|3. Add to appropriate category in this document
217|4. Update research procedures if needed
218|5. Update quality standards if enforcement needed
219|

  9|# Reviewer Agent Rules
 10|
 11|## Overview
 12|Declarative policy for Reviewer agent implementation following quality-first principles. Rules are organized into Conventions (behavioral guidance) and Constraints (hard boundaries).
 13|
 14|## Conventions
 15|
 16|- **Best Practices**: Web search must be used before conducting major review decisions or when uncertain about review criteria. Best practices are established industry standards that must be researched before proceeding.
 17|- Check index files (Docs/index.md, Docs/Research/index.md, Docs/Websites/index.md, Docs/Code/index.md) before web searching (reduces token cost, prioritizes local knowledge)
 18|- Present review findings and recommendations after each review completion. Wait for user confirmation before proceeding (ensures quality control, prevents cascading issues)
 19|- Answer questions first when user requests end with "?". Ask for permission before making changes after answering (ensures user understanding, prevents unintended modifications)
 20|- Use capital letters at the start of items unless lowercase is needed (maintains consistency, improves readability)
 21|- All **{CAPITALIZED}** commands and terms are defined in Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Terminology_Glossary.md (SSOT for terminology)
 22|
 23|## Execution Modes
 24|
 25|Three execution modes govern workflow behavior when encountering failures:
 26|
 27|- **Manual**: Stop at failures for human oversight - workflow halts at any failure point and awaits user intervention to decide on retry, modification, or abort
 28|- **Auto**: Don't continue on failures - workflow automatically stops on any failure without requiring human intervention, ensuring errors are not silently ignored
 29|- **Complete**: Continue past failures - workflow automatically continues through all failures, ignoring errors to reach completion regardless of success/failure status
 30|
 31|## Constraints
 32|
 33|- Conduct one review at a time. Validate immediately. Never start a second review before first is validated (ensures modular validation, prevents hidden issues)
 34|- Treat user-confirmed reviews as final. Never modify without explicit user permission (maintains stability, prevents unintended changes)
 35|- Check local research using index files when review criteria are unclear. Web search only if local info unavailable. Never review blindly without research (reduces token cost, ensures correct evaluation)
 36|- Place review logs in Logs/Reviewer/ folder with proper categorization. Never create ad-hoc folders or place outside established structure (maintains organization, prevents file chaos)
 37|- Always use popups for yes/no questions. Never use text-only confirmations (ensures clear user intent, prevents miscommunication)
 38|- Always categorize review findings when adding to review documentation. Never place findings uncategorized (maintains organization, enables efficient navigation)
 39|- Never skip compliance verification. Always verify adherence to Executor rules and standards before concluding review (ensures quality, prevents rule violations)
 40|- Never modify code directly during review (reviewer role only, prevents scope drift into implementation)
 41|- Never skip best practices evaluation. Always assess code against industry standards and established patterns (ensures quality, prevents suboptimal solutions)
 42|- Never perform actions outside workflow scope. Always follow defined review processes and never perform tasks outside the current workflow scope unless explicitly requested by the user (prevents token waste, ensures focused execution)
 43|- Never create documentation files unless specifically requested. Never create README.md, CHANGELOG.md, or other documentation files unless specifically requested by the user (prevents token waste, maintains workflow scope discipline)
 44|- Never run subagents unless explicitly requested by the user. Always perform research and analysis using direct tools (web_search, grep, read, etc.) unless user specifically requests subagent delegation (prevents unexpected subagent usage, maintains user control over execution)
 45|
 46|## Architecture
 47|
 48|- Quality-first architecture: Review ensures code quality before implementation proceeds (maintains quality standards, enables early issue detection)
 49|- Modular compliance verification: Each function reviewed for modularity, testability, and best practices adherence (maintains code quality, prevents technical debt)
 50|- Comprehensive scanning: Line-by-line examination of all files within scope (ensures complete coverage, prevents hidden issues)
 51|- Constructive feedback: Specific, actionable recommendations with clear improvement paths (maintains review effectiveness, enables continuous improvement)
 52|
 53|## Tool Configuration
 54|
 55|- Directory verification: `ls -la <directory>` (verify directory structure exists)
 56|- File discovery: `find <path -name "*.md"` (find markdown governance files)
 57|- Pattern search: `grep -r "pattern" <directory>` (search for patterns in rule files)
 58|- JSON validation: `python -m json.tool <file>` (validate JSON syntax, exit code indicates success/failure)
 59|- File comparison: `diff <file1> <file2>` (compare files before changes, exit code 0 = identical)
 60|
 61|## Project Structure
 62|
 63|- `App/` â€“ Application code to review (READ for quality and compliance verification)
 64|- `Plans/` â€“ Implementation plans to review (READ for quality and completeness)
 65|- `Workflow/` â€“ Workflow definitions to review (READ for process compliance)
 66|- `Rules/` â€“ Rule definitions to reference (READ for compliance verification)
 67|- `Docs/` â€“ Documentation to review (READ for completeness and accuracy)
 68|- `Logs/Reviewer/` â€“ Reviewer-specific logs and review records (WRITE review logs here)
 69|
 70|## Workflow
 71|- **Main Workflow**: Workflow/Reviewer/Reviewer_Review_Workflow.md (comprehensive review process)
 72|- **Best Practice Scanner**: Workflow/Reviewer/Reviewer_Best_Practice_Scanner_Workflow.md (App/ directory compliance scanning)
 73|- **Quality Framework**: Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Quality_Assessment_Framework.md (review quality assessment)
 74|- **Validation Patterns**: Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Validation_Enforcement_Patterns.md (review verification)
 75|
 76|## Modular Compliance Review Rules
 77|
 78|### Function-by-Function Verification
 79|- **DO**: Verify each function follows single responsibility principle
 80|- **DO**: Check that functions have clear inputs and outputs
 81|- **DO**: Ensure functions are independently testable
 82|- **DO**: Verify dependency injection usage for testability
 83|- **DO**: Check separation of business logic from I/O operations
 84|- **DON'T**: Accept monolithic functions that do multiple things
 85|- **DON'T**: Overlook hardcoded dependencies that should be injected
 86|- **DON'T**: Ignore mixed business logic and I/O operations
 87|
 88|### Testing Requirements Verification
 89|- **DO**: Verify tests exist for each function in Scripts/Tests/
 90|- **DO**: Check that tests are placed in correct directory (not App/)
 91|- **DO**: Ensure tests use dependency injection and mocking
 92|- **DO**: Verify test coverage meets plan requirements (â‰¥90%)
 93|- **DO**: Check that both success and error paths are tested
 94|- **DON'T**: Accept missing tests for any function
 95|- **DON'T**: Overlook tests placed in App/ directory
 96|- **DON'T**: Ignore tests that depend on external systems without mocking
 97|
 98|### Code Quality Standards Verification
 99|- **DO**: Verify code follows project coding standards and conventions
100|- **DO**: Check for appropriate error handling and validation
101|- **DO**: Ensure code is readable and maintainable
102|- **DO**: Verify security best practices adherence
103|- **DO**: Check for meaningful comments where necessary
104|- **DON'T**: Accept code that is difficult to understand
105|- **DON'T**: Overlook missing error handling and validation
106|- **DON'T**: Ignore insecure coding practices
107|
108|### Best Practices Evaluation
109|- **DO**: Evaluate code against industry best practices
110|- **DO**: Check for established design patterns
111|- **DO**: Verify adherence to SOLID principles
112|- **DO**: Assess code for testability and maintainability
113|- **DO**: Check for proper separation of concerns
114|- **DON'T**: Accept anti-patterns or poor practices
115|- **DON'T**: Overlook violations of established principles
116|- **DON'T**: Ignore maintainability concerns
117|
118|## Review Quality Rules
119|
120|### Comprehensive Coverage
121|- **DO**: Review all files within scope line by line
122|- **DO**: Ensure no files are skipped during review
123|- **DO**: Verify complete coverage of review criteria
124|- **DO**: Check that all compliance rules are evaluated
125|- **DON'T**: Skip files during review process
126|- **DON'T**: Perform partial reviews when comprehensive is required
127|- **DON'T**: Overlook any compliance verification steps
128|
129|### Constructive Feedback
130|- **DO**: Provide specific, actionable feedback
131|- **DO**: Include clear improvement recommendations
132|- **DO**: Reference specific code sections with line numbers
133|- **DO**: Explain the reasoning behind findings
134|- **DON'T**: Provide vague or general feedback
135|- **DON'T** Make subjective judgments without evidence
136|- **DON'T** Issue feedback without clear improvement paths
137|
138|### Documentation Standards
139|- **DO**: Document all review findings comprehensively
140|- **DO**: Include severity ratings for issues found
141|- **DO**: Provide context for why issues matter
142|- **DO** Maintain clear review logs with timestamps
143|- **DON'T** Skip documentation of review findings
144|- **DON'T** Leave findings without proper categorization
145|- **DON'T** Omit context or rationale for recommendations
146|
147|## Subagent Usage for Large-Scale Scanning
148|
149|### Subagent Prompting Strategy
150|- **DO**: Use subagents for large-scale App/ directory scanning when explicitly requested
151|- **DO**: Provide precise, detailed prompts with clear scope and criteria
152|- **DO**: Define specific compliance rules to check (modularity, testing, best practices)
153|- **DO**: Specify exact output format and structure expected
154|- **DO** Include clear boundaries and deliverable expectations
155|- **DON'T**: Use vague or ambiguous subagent prompts
156|- **DON'T** Skip defining exact scope and evaluation criteria
157|- **DON'T** Accept subagent results without validation
158|
159|### Subagent Coordination
160|- **DO**: Break large scanning tasks into logical chunks (by module, directory, or complexity)
161|- **DO**: Use parallel subagents for independent scanning tasks
162|- **DO**: Validate subagent results against established criteria
163|- **DO**: Consolidate subagent findings into comprehensive report
164|- **DON'T** Create overlapping subagent scopes that cause redundancy
165|- **DON'T** Accept subagent findings without cross-validation
166|- **DON'T** Skip consolidation and verification of subagent results
167|
168|## Current Status
169|
170|**Rules**: Initial version based on code review best practices and quality assurance standards
171|**Categories**: Modular compliance, code quality, best practices evaluation, comprehensive coverage, constructive feedback
172|**Enforcement**: Quality verification (primary), compliance standards (secondary), best practices evaluation (tertiary)
173|**Modular Compliance**: Function-by-function verification against Executor rules with subagent support for large-scale scanning

  1|# State Management Guidelines
  2|
  3|**Purpose**: Universal state management guidelines for all agent workflows.
  4|
  5|## Universal State Management Structure
  6|
  7|### Workflow State File
  8|**Location**: `workflow_state.json` in current working directory
  9|**Purpose**: Track workflow execution state for recovery and monitoring
 10|**Format**: JSON-structured state data
 11|
 12|### Universal State Schema
 13|```json
 14|{
 15|  "workflow_id": "string",
 16|  "agent_type": "string",
 17|  "execution_strategy": "string",
 18|  "current_phase": "string",
 19|  "phase_status": "string",
 20|  "start_time": "timestamp",
 21|  "last_update": "timestamp",
 22|  "total_steps": "number",
 23|  "completed_steps": "number",
 24|  "failed_steps": "number",
 25|  "retry_count": "number",
 26|  "session_metadata": {}
 27|}
 28|```
 29|
 30|---
 31|
 32|## Universal State Management Patterns
 33|
 34|### Phase Status Tracking
 35|**Status Values**:
 36|- `phase_0_complete`: Rules loaded and ready
 37|- `phase_{N}_in_progress`: Phase currently executing
 38|- `phase_{N}_complete`: Phase successfully completed
 39|- `phase_{N}_failed`: Phase failed, requires intervention
 40|- `workflow_complete`: Entire workflow completed
 41|
 42|**Update Pattern**:
 43|1. Set status to `phase_{N}_in_progress` when starting phase
 44|2. Update to `phase_{N}_complete` when phase succeeds
 45|3. Update to `phase_{N}_failed` when phase fails
 46|4. Maintain audit trail of all status changes
 47|
 48|### Execution Strategy Storage
 49|**Storage Pattern**:
 50|- Store selected execution strategy in state file
 51|- Maintain strategy throughout workflow execution
 52|- Enable strategy changes with proper logging
 53|- Track strategy effectiveness for future optimization
 54|
 55|**Strategy Values**:
 56|- `manual`: Manual oversight with checkpoints
 57|- `auto`: Automatic progression with failure detection
 58|- `complete`: Full automation with failure tolerance
 59|- Agent-specific strategies as needed
 60|
 61|### Error Recovery State
 62|**Recovery State Management**:
 63|- Track failure points and recovery actions
 64|- Store retry count and backoff status
 65|- Maintain recovery action history
 66|- Enable recovery from any state point
 67|
 68|**Recovery Metadata**:
 69|```json
 70|{
 71|  "last_failure": {
 72|    "phase": "string",
 73|    "step": "number",
 74|    "error": "string",
 75|    "timestamp": "timestamp"
 76|  },
 77|  "retry_attempts": "number",
 78|  "recovery_actions": ["array of actions"],
 79|  "max_retries": "number"
 80|}
 81|```
 82|
 83|---
 84|
 85|## Universal Audit Trail Patterns
 86|
 87|### State Change Logging
 88|**Logging Requirements**:
 89|- Log every state change with timestamp
 90|- Include change reason and context
 91|- Track user decisions and approvals
 92|- Maintain complete execution history
 93|
 94|**Log Entry Format**:
 95|```json
 96|{
 97|  "timestamp": "timestamp",
 98|  "event": "string",
 99|  "previous_state": "object",
100|  "new_state": "object",
101|  "reason": "string",
102|  "context": "object"
103|}
104|```
105|
106|### Session Metadata
107|**Metadata Requirements**:
108|- Session ID for tracking
109|- User identification
110|- Task description
111|- Execution context
112|- Resource usage tracking
113|
114|**Metadata Schema**:
115|```json
116|{
117|  "session_id": "string",
118|  "user_id": "string",
119|  "task_description": "string",
120|  "execution_context": "object",
121|  "resource_usage": {
122|    "memory": "number",
123|    "cpu": "number",
124|    "time": "number"
125|  }
126|}
127|```
128|
129|---
130|
131|## Universal Recovery Patterns
132|
133|### State Recovery
134|**Recovery Process**:
135|1. Load current state from workflow_state.json
136|2. Identify last successful state point
137|3. Determine recovery strategy
138|4. Execute recovery actions
139|5. Update state with recovery progress
140|6. Resume workflow execution
141|
142|**Recovery Strategies**:
143|- **Retry with Backoff**: Exponential backoff for transient failures
144|- **Checkpoint Recovery**: Resume from last successful checkpoint
145|- **State Rollback**: Rollback to previous stable state
146|- **Manual Intervention**: Request user intervention for complex failures
147|- **Alternative Path**: Try alternative execution path
148|
149|### Checkpoint Management
150|**Checkpoint Creation**:
151|- Create checkpoints at critical phase transitions
152|- Store checkpoint state for recovery
153|- Include checkpoint metadata for validation
154|- Enable rollback to any checkpoint
155|
156|**Checkpoint Schema**:
157|```json
158|{
159|  "checkpoint_id": "string",
160|  "phase": "string",
161|  "step": "number",
162|  "state_snapshot": "object",
163|  "validation_hash": "string",
164|  "timestamp": "timestamp"
165|}
166|```
167|
168|---
169|
170|## Agent-Specific State Management
171|
172|### Planner Agent State
173|**Planner-Specific State Elements**:
174|- Round Table iteration state
175|- Convergence metrics tracking
176|- Validation results history
177|- Plan revision tracking
178|- Panelist review aggregation state
179|
180|**Additional State Schema**:
181|```json
182|{
183|  "planner_state": {
184|    "internal_iteration": "number",
185|    "external_iteration": "number",
186|    "convergence_metrics": {
187|      "findings_count": "number",
188|      "panelist_agreement": "number",
189|      "quality_score": "number"
190|    },
191|    "plan_revision": "string",
192|    "validation_results": "array"
193|  }
194|}
195|```
196|
197|### Architect Agent State
198|**Architect-Specific State Elements**:
199|- Execution mode state
200|- Implementation mode selection
201|- Validation checkpoint state
202|- File placement compliance state
203|- Governance file update tracking
204|
205|**Additional State Schema**:
206|```json
207|{
208|  "architect_state": {
209|    "execution_mode": "string",
210|    "implementation_mode": "string",
211|    "validation_checkpoints": "array",
212|    "file_compliance": "object",
213|    "governance_updates": "array"
214|  }
215|}
216|```
217|
218|---
219|
220|## Universal State Update Patterns
221|
222|### State Update Rules
223|**Update Requirements**:
224|- Update state atomically to prevent corruption
225|- Validate state before persistence
226|- Include change metadata for audit trail
227|- Handle concurrent access safely
228|- Enable rollback on update failure
229|
230|### State Persistence
231|**Persistence Requirements**:
232|- Persist state after each phase completion
233|- Persist state on error conditions
234|- Persist state on user decisions
235|- Persist state on strategy changes
236|- Maintain state file integrity
237|
238|### State Validation
239|**Validation Requirements**:
240|- Validate state schema on load
241|- Validate state consistency before use
242|- Validate state transitions are legal
243|- Validate metadata completeness
244|- Validate no state corruption
245|
246|---
247|
248|## Universal State Monitoring
249|
250|### State Health Monitoring
251|**Health Checks**:
252|- Monitor state file integrity
253|- Monitor state consistency
254|- Monitor state update frequency
255|- Monitor state size and complexity
256|- Monitor state access patterns
257|
258|### State Performance Monitoring
259|**Performance Metrics**:
260|- State update latency
261|- State file size trends
262|- State access patterns
263|- Recovery success rates
264|- State corruption incidents
265|
266|### State Analytics
267|**Analytics Requirements**:
268|- Track state transition patterns
269|- Analyze failure state patterns
270|- Analyze recovery success rates
271|- Analyze execution strategy effectiveness
272|- Generate state management insights
273|
274|---
275|
276|## Usage Guidelines
277|
278|### State Management Implementation
279|1. **Initialize State**: Create initial state file at workflow start
280|2. **Update State**: Update state after each phase completion
281|3. **Handle Failures**: Update state on failures with recovery metadata
282|4. **Enable Recovery**: Enable recovery from any state point
283|5. **Maintain Audit Trail**: Maintain complete state change history
284|
285|### State Management Best Practices
286|- **Atomic Updates**: Update state atomically to prevent corruption
287|- **Validation**: Always validate state before use
288|- **Backup**: Maintain state backups for recovery
289|- **Cleanup**: Clean up old state files periodically
290|- **Security**: Secure state files from unauthorized access
291|
292|### State Recovery Best Practices
293|- **Multiple Recovery Points**: Enable recovery from multiple state points
294|- **Recovery Testing**: Test recovery mechanisms regularly
295|- **Recovery Documentation**: Document recovery procedures
296|- **Recovery Monitoring**: Monitor recovery success rates
297|- **Recovery Optimization**: Optimize recovery based on patterns
</file-view>

  1|# Execution Strategy Guidelines
  2|
  3|**Purpose**: Universal execution strategy specifications for all agent workflows.
  4|
  5|## Universal Strategy Configuration Patterns
  6|
  7|### Strategy Selection Pattern
  8|1. Agent selects appropriate strategy based on task complexity
  9|2. Strategy stored in workflow state for consistent behavior
 10|3. Strategy governs failure handling and progression throughout workflow
 11|4. Strategy can be changed during workflow if conditions change
 12|
 13|### Failure Handling Pattern
 14|- **Manual**: Stop and await user intervention for retry/modify/abort decision
 15|- **Auto**: Stop automatically without requiring human intervention
 16|- **Complete**: Continue automatically, ignoring failures
 17|- **Retry Logic**: Configurable exponential backoff for automatic strategies
 18|
 19|### Checkpoint Pattern
 20|- **Manual Mode**: Require user confirmation via popup menu before proceeding
 21|- **Auto/Complete Modes**: Proceed automatically without checkpoints
 22|- **Checkpoint Criteria**: Major phase transitions, critical decisions, failure points
 23|
 24|## Universal Strategy Guidelines
 25|
 26|### Strategy Consistency
 27|- Maintain consistent strategy behavior throughout workflow execution
 28|- Document strategy changes with rationale
 29|- Update workflow state when strategy changes
 30|- Notify user of strategy transitions
 31|
 32|### Strategy Selection Criteria
 33|- **Task Complexity**: Simple tasks may use faster strategies
 34|- **Risk Level**: High-risk tasks may require manual oversight
 35|- **User Preference**: Allow user to select strategy when appropriate
 36|- **System Constraints**: Resource limits may influence strategy choice
 37|
 38|### Strategy Monitoring
 39|- Track strategy effectiveness across workflow executions
 40|- Monitor failure rates and recovery patterns
 41|- Adjust strategy based on performance metrics
 42|- Document strategy evolution patterns
</file-view>
```
