  1|# Planner Workflow Overview
  2|
  3|## Best Practices
  4|
  5|This workflow follows AI planning best practices with:
  6|- **Incremental verification**: Validation after each phase to catch errors close to source
  7|- **Dual-validation governance**: Early validation (Phase 3) + final validation (Phase 7)
  8|- **Convergence-based iteration**: Internal and external Round Table loops until convergence
  9|- **Incremental logging**: Save reviews as received for audit trail and Reviewer analysis
 10|- **Role separation**: Planner creates plans, Reviewer analyzes quality (separate agent workflow)
 11|- **Domain-split personas**: Panelists adopt specific domain expertise for focused review
 12|- **Web search verification**: All panelists must verify findings against current best practices
 13|- **Quota handling**: State persistence + resume pattern for handling quota exhaustion
 14|- **Plan delivery**: Final plans saved to Plans/ directory for executor execution
 15|- **Batch processing**: Plans organized in batches of 5 with scan plans for issue resolution
 16|
 17|## Phase Structure
 18|
 19|1. **Phase 0**: Read Planner Rules + Governance + Validate
 20|2. **Phase 1**: Select Execution Mode
 21|3. **Phase 2**: Planner Interaction
 22|4. **Phase 3**: Plan Creation + Validate (includes plan type determination)
 23|5. **Phase 4**: Internal Round Table + Validate (Convergence Loop)
 24|6. **Phase 5**: Apply Findings + Validate (Loop Back to Phase 4)
 25|7. **[Loop 4â†’5 until Internal passes - max 5 iterations]**
 26|8. **Phase 6**: External Round Table + Validate (Convergence Loop)
 27|9. **Phase 5**: Apply Findings + Validate (Loop Back to Phase 6)
 28|10. **[Loop 6â†’5 until External passes - max 3 iterations]**
 29|11. **Phase 7**: Final Validation + Save Plan to Plans/ + Delivery Authorization
 30|12. **Phase 8**: Session Logging + Validate
 31|13. **Next Plan**: Continue to next plan in batch sequence
 32|
 33|## Template References
 34|
 35|- **Plan Creation**: Workflow/Planner/Templates/Plan_Template.md (plan structure and format)
 36|- **Brief Creation**: Workflow/Planner/Templates/Plan_Brief_Template.md (review brief structure)
 37|- **Prompt Instructions**: Workflow/Planner/Templates/Plan_Prompt_Template.md (persona adoption instructions)
 38|- **Plan Batch Specifications**: Workflow/Planner/Reference/Plan_Batch_Specifications.md (batch processing and scan plan patterns)
 39|- **Quality Assessment**: Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Quality_Assessment_Framework.md (universal framework)
 40|- **Validation System**: Workflow/Planner/Reference/Validation_System_Specifications.md (planner-specific validation definitions)
 41|- **Convergence Loops**: Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Convergence_Loop_Patterns.md (universal pattern) and Workflow/Planner/Reference/Convergence_Loop_Specifications.md (planner-specific implementation)
 42|- **Delivery Authorization**: Workflow/Planner/Reference/Delivery_Authorization_Specifications.md (planner-specific)
 43|- **Role Responsibilities**: Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Role_Responsibilities_Framework.md (universal framework) and Workflow/Planner/Reference/Role_Responsibilities.md (planner-specific)
 44|- **Performance Metrics**: Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Performance_Metrics_Framework.md (universal framework)
 45|- **State Management**: Workflow/Workflow_Reference/State_Management_Guidelines.md (universal framework)
 46|- **Quota Handling**: Workflow/Workflow_Reference/Quota_Handling_Patterns.md (universal framework)
 47|
 48|## Logging Structure
 49|
 50|- Round Table reviews: Incremental logging as received (Logs/Planner/Roundtable/Internal/ and Logs/Planner/Roundtable/External/)
 51|- Plan iterations: Incremental logging (Logs/Planner/)
 52|- Validation results: JSON logging (Logs/Planner/validation-completions/ and Logs/Planner/validation-failures/)
 53|- Session: Final consolidated logging at Phase 8
</file-view>
```

  1|# Planner Plan Batch Specifications
  2|
  3|**Purpose**: Planner-specific plan batch execution patterns and scan plan categorization.
  4|
  5|## Plan Batch Structure
  6|
  7|### Batch Execution Pattern
  8|Plans are organized in batches of 5 plans per batch for systematic processing and issue resolution.
  9|
 10|### Plan Numbering Pattern
 11|- **Standard Plans**: Plans 1-4, 6-9, 11-14, 16-19, 21-24, 26-29, 31-34, 36-39 (regular planning tasks)
 12|- **Scan Plans**: Plans 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40 (every 5th plan is a scan plan)
 13|
 14|### Scan Plan Purpose
 15|Scan plans (5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40) are specifically designed to:
 16|- Identify and fix issues discovered in previous plans
 17|- Perform systematic system scans for problems
 18|- Address accumulated issues from previous batch execution
 19|- Provide quality control and system health checks
 20|
 21|## Batch Processing Workflow
 22|
 23|### Batch Structure
 24|```
 25|Batch 1: Plans 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 (Plan 5 = Scan Plan)
 26|Batch 2: Plans 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 (Plan 10 = Scan Plan)
 27|Batch 3: Plans 11, 12, 13, 14, 15 (Plan 15 = Scan Plan)
 28|Batch 4: Plans 16, 17, 18, 19, 20 (Plan 20 = Scan Plan)
 29|Batch 5: Plans 21, 22, 23, 24, 25 (Plan 25 = Scan Plan)
 30|Batch 6: Plans 26, 27, 28, 29, 30 (Plan 30 = Scan Plan)
 31|Batch 7: Plans 31, 32, 33, 34, 35 (Plan 35 = Scan Plan)
 32|Batch 8: Plans 36, 37, 38, 39, 40 (Plan 40 = Scan Plan)
 33|```
 34|
 35|### Standard Plan Characteristics
 36|- **Purpose**: Implement specific features or changes
 37|- **Content**: Regular planning tasks following standard template
 38|- **Execution**: Direct implementation by executor
 39|- **Validation**: Standard validation and delivery process
 40|
 41|### Scan Plan Characteristics
 42|- **Purpose**: Fix issues from previous plans, system health checks
 43|- **Content**: Issue identification, problem resolution, system scans
 44|- **Execution**: Issue-fixing and system maintenance
 45|- **Validation**: Enhanced validation focusing on issue resolution
 46|
 47|## Workflow Integration
 48|
 49|### Planner Workflow Modification
 50|The Planner workflow should:
 51|1. **Batch Mode**: Process plans sequentially through batch (return to Phase 0 after each plan for next plan in sequence)
 52|2. **Single Plan Mode**: Process single plan and terminate (no return to Phase 0)
 53|3. **Follow batch sequence**: Process plans in numerical order when in batch mode
 54|4. **Identify scan plans**: Recognize plan numbers 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40
 55|5. **Apply scan plan logic**: Use different approach for scan plans
 56|6. **Track batch progress**: Monitor batch completion status
 57|
 58|### Scan Plan Detection Logic
 59|```python
 60|def is_scan_plan(plan_number):
 61|    return plan_number % 5 == 0
 62|
 63|def get_plan_type(plan_number):
 64|    if is_scan_plan(plan_number):
 65|        return "scan_plan"
 66|    else:
 67|        return "standard_plan"
 68|```
 69|
 70|### Execution Pattern
 71|1. **Standard Plan**: Follow normal workflow â†’ Save to Plans/ â†’ Execute
 72|2. **Scan Plan**: Enhanced workflow â†’ Scan for issues â†’ Fix problems â†’ Save to Plans/ â†’ Execute
 73|3. **Batch Completion**: After each 5th plan, batch is complete
 74|4. **Next Batch**: Continue with next batch sequence
 75|
 76|## Plan Storage and Organization
 77|
 78|### Directory Structure
 79|```
 80|Plans/
 81|â”œâ”€â”€ plan-1.md
 82|â”œâ”€â”€ plan-2.md
 83|â”œâ”€â”€ plan-3.md
 84|â”œâ”€â”€ plan-4.md
 85|â”œâ”€â”€ plan-5.md (scan plan)
 86|â”œâ”€â”€ plan-6.md
 87|â”œâ”€â”€ plan-7.md
 88|â”œâ”€â”€ plan-8.md
 89|â”œâ”€â”€ plan-9.md
 90|â”œâ”€â”€ plan-10.md (scan plan)
 91|â””â”€â”€ ...
 92|```
 93|
 94|### Plan Metadata
 95|Each plan should include:
 96|- **Plan Number**: Sequential number in batch sequence
 97|- **Plan Type**: Standard or Scan
 98|- **Batch Number**: Which batch this plan belongs to
 99|- **Previous Issues**: Issues found in previous plans (for scan plans)
100|- **Issue Resolution**: How scan plan addresses issues
101|
102|## Usage Guidelines
103|
104|### When Creating Standard Plans
105|1. Follow standard planning workflow
106|2. Use standard plan template
107|3. Focus on feature implementation
108|4. Save with sequential numbering
109|5. Mark as standard plan type
110|
111|### When Creating Scan Plans
112|1. Review previous plans in batch for issues
113|2. Perform system scan for problems
114|3. Create issue-fixing plan
115|4. Use enhanced validation for issue resolution
116|5. Mark as scan plan type
117|6. Document issue resolution approach
118|
119|### Batch Management
120|1. Track which plans have been completed
121|2. Monitor batch progress
122|3. Ensure scan plans address relevant issues
123|4. Validate batch completion before proceeding
124|5. Maintain plan sequence integrity
</file-view>

  1|# Plan Review Prompt Template
  2|
  3|**Purpose**: Explicit instructions for Round Table panelists on how to adopt personas and conduct reviews  
  4|**Location**: Workflow/Planner/Templates/Plan_Prompt_Template.md  
  5|**Usage**: Include in brief documents or send directly to panelists  
  6|**Version**: 1.0
  7|
  8|---
  9|
 10|## Persona Adoption Instructions
 11|
 12|**CRITICAL**: You must adopt the specific domain-split persona assigned to you for this review. Do not conduct a general review - focus exclusively on your assigned domain expertise.
 13|
 14|---
 15|
 16|## Persona Definitions
 17|
 18|### Persona 1: Structure and Dependencies Expert
 19|**Domain**: Plan structure, step dependencies, execution order
 20|**Mental Model**: You are a systems architect who specializes in workflow structure and dependency analysis
 21|**Expertise**: 
 22|- Dependency graph theory and best practices
 23|- Execution order optimization
 24|- Circular dependency detection
 25|- Sequential vs parallel execution patterns
 26|**Web Search**: Verify dependency patterns against current planning best practices
 27|**Checks**: No circular dependencies, clear relationships, executable sequence
 28|
 29|### Persona 2: Scope Compliance Expert  
 30|**Domain**: Planning language only, no implementation details
 31|**Mental Model**: You are a governance specialist who ensures plans stay within defined scope boundaries
 32|**Expertise**:
 33|- Agent role boundaries and separation
 34|- Planning vs implementation language
 35|- Infrastructure scope compliance
 36|- Governance rule enforcement
 37|**Web Search**: Verify scope boundaries against current agent governance research
 38|**Checks**: Infrastructure scope, planning vs implementation boundaries
 39|
 40|### Persona 3: Quality and Clarity Expert
 41|**Domain**: Plan clarity, completeness, user-focused language
 42|**Mental Model**: You are a technical communication specialist who ensures plans are clear and actionable
 43|**Expertise**:
 44|- Technical writing best practices
 45|- User-focused communication
 46|- Goal statement clarity
 47|- Requirement specification
 48|**Web Search**: Verify clarity and communication best practices for technical plans
 49|**Checks**: Clear goal statement, well-defined steps, quality rubric assessment
 50|
 51|### Persona 4: Risk Assessment Expert
 52|**Domain**: Implementation risks, edge cases, dependencies
 53|**Mental Model**: You are a risk analyst who identifies potential failure points and edge cases
 54|**Expertise**:
 55|- Risk assessment methodologies
 56|- Edge case identification
 57|- Dependency risk analysis
 58|- Feasibility evaluation
 59|**Web Search**: Verify risk assessment methodologies against current practices
 60|**Checks**: Risk identification, mitigation strategies, feasibility
 61|
 62|### Persona 5: Alternative Approaches Expert (Optional for complex plans)
 63|**Domain**: Alternative planning approaches, optimizations
 64|**Mental Model**: You are a planning strategist who identifies better approaches and optimizations
 65|**Expertise**:
 66|- Planning pattern optimization
 67|- Alternative approach identification
 68|- Trade-off analysis
 69|- Simplification opportunities
 70|**Web Search**: Research current planning patterns and optimization techniques
 71|**Checks**: Better alternatives, simplification opportunities, trade-offs
 72|
 73|### Persona 6: Infrastructure Alignment Expert (Optional for infrastructure changes)
 74|**Domain**: Infrastructure principles, architectural constraints
 75|**Mental Model**: You are an infrastructure architect who ensures alignment with infrastructure principles
 76|**Expertise**:
 77|- Infrastructure development principles
 78|- Architectural constraint verification
 79|- Infrastructure governance
 80|- System architecture patterns

  1|# Compliance Criteria Reference for Reviewer Agent
  2|
  3|## Purpose
  4|Single source of truth (SSOT) for detailed compliance criteria used in review workflows. This document contains the specific standards and requirements that workflows reference.
  5|
  6|## File Type Compliance Criteria
  7|
  8|### Code Files (.py, .js, .ts, etc.)
  9|
 10|#### Modularity Requirements
 11|- **Single Responsibility Principle**: Each function should do one thing well
 12|- **Clear Interfaces**: Functions should have explicit inputs and outputs
 13|- **Independent Testability**: Functions should be testable in isolation
 14|- **Dependency Injection**: Dependencies should be passed as parameters, not hardcoded
 15|- **Separation of Concerns**: Business logic should be separated from I/O operations
 16|
 17|#### Testing Requirements
 18|- **Test Location**: Tests must be in Scripts/Tests/ (never in App/ directory)
 19|- **Test Coverage**: Minimum 90% coverage for all functions
 20|- **Dependency Injection**: Tests should use dependency injection for isolation
 21|- **Mocking**: External dependencies (I/O, databases, APIs) must be mocked
 22|- **Test Paths**: Both success and error paths must be tested
 23|- **Test Quality**: Tests should be deterministic and not implementation-dependent
 24|
 25|#### Code Quality Standards
 26|- **Error Handling**: Appropriate error handling and validation
 27|- **Readability**: Code should be clear and maintainable
 28|- **Security Practices**: Follow security best practices (no hardcoded secrets, proper input validation)
 29|- **Documentation**: Meaningful docstrings for classes and functions
 30|- **Code Style**: Follow project coding standards and conventions
 31|
 32|#### Best Practices Adherence
 33|- **SOLID Principles**: Single responsibility, open/closed, Liskov substitution, interface segregation, dependency inversion
 34|- **Design Patterns**: Use appropriate design patterns for common problems
 35|- **Separation of Concerns**: Clear boundaries between different concerns
 36|- **Industry Standards**: Follow current industry best practices for the language/framework
 37|
 38|### Configuration Files (.json, .yaml, .toml, .ini, etc.)
 39|
 40|#### Structure Requirements
 41|- **Schema Compliance**: Must follow defined schema if one exists
 42|- **Valid Syntax**: Must be syntactically valid for the file type
 43|- **Proper Structure**: Logical organization and grouping of related settings
 44|- **Documentation**: Include comments explaining configuration purpose
 45|
 46|#### Security Requirements
 47|- **No Hardcoded Secrets**: API keys, passwords, tokens must not be in config files
 48|- **Environment Separation**: Different configurations for different environments
 49|- **Access Control**: Proper file permissions if applicable
 50|- **Secrets Management**: Use environment variables or secret management systems
 51|
 52|#### Best Practices
 53|- **Validation**: Configuration should be validated at startup
 54|- **Defaults**: Provide sensible defaults for all settings
 55|- **Documentation**: Document all configuration options and their effects
 56|- **Version Control**: Exclude sensitive configs from version control
 57|
 58|### Documentation Files (.md, .txt, .rst, etc.)
 59|
 60|#### Structure Requirements
 61|- **Clear Organization**: Logical flow and structure
 62|- **Proper Formatting**: Correct use of markup syntax
 63|- **Headings**: Appropriate heading hierarchy
 64|- **Sections**: Clear section divisions for different topics
 65|
 66|#### Content Requirements
 67|- **Accuracy**: Information must be accurate and up-to-date
 68|- **Completeness**: Cover all necessary topics
 69|- **Clarity**: Writing should be clear and understandable
 70|- **Relevance**: Content should be relevant to the document's purpose
 71|
 72|#### Link and Reference Requirements
 73|- **Link Validity**: All links must be valid and working
 74|- **Cross-References**: Proper cross-referencing within documentation
 75|- **External References**: Cite external sources appropriately
 76|- **Version Specific**: Document should specify version/service it applies to
 77|
 78|#### Maintainability
 79|- **Update Process**: Clear process for keeping documentation current
 80|- **Review Schedule**: Regular review and update cycle
 81|- **Ownership**: Clear ownership of different documentation sections
 82|- **Accessibility**: Documentation should be easily findable and accessible
 83|
 84|### Data Files (.csv, .json, .xml, etc.)
 85|
 86|#### Format Requirements
 87|- **Valid Format**: Must conform to the specified file format
 88|- **Proper Structure**: Appropriate structure for the data type
 89|- **Encoding**: Proper character encoding (typically UTF-8)
 90|- **Consistency**: Consistent formatting throughout the file
 91|
 92|#### Data Integrity
 93|- **Data Validation**: Data should be validated against schema
 94|- **Completeness**: All required fields should be present
 95|- **Accuracy**: Data should be accurate and consistent
 96|- **Backup**: Appropriate backup and versioning strategy
 97|
 98|#### Usage Patterns
 99|- **Purpose Clarity**: Clear purpose for the data file
100|- **Access Patterns**: Appropriate read/write patterns
101|- **Performance**: Consider performance implications for large files
102|- **Security**: Sensitive data should be appropriately protected
103|
104|### Build/Deployment Files (Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, etc.)
105|
106|#### Security Best Practices
107|- **Base Images**: Use trusted, minimal base images
108|- **No Secrets**: No secrets in build files
109|- **User Permissions**: Run as non-root user when possible
110|- **Scanning**: Regular security scanning of images
111|
112|#### Configuration Best Practices
113|- **Environment Variables**: Use environment variables for configuration
114|- **Resource Limits**: Set appropriate resource limits
115|- **Health Checks**: Implement health checks
116|- **Logging**: Proper logging configuration
117|
118|#### Maintainability
119|- **Documentation**: Document build and deployment processes
120|- **Versioning**: Tag and version Docker images appropriately
121|- **Reproducibility**: Builds should be reproducible
122|- **Testing**: Test deployment configurations
123|
124|## Severity Classifications
125|
126|### CRITICAL Issues
127|- **Definition**: Violations that must be fixed immediately
128|- **Examples**: Missing tests, hardcoded dependencies, mixed concerns, security vulnerabilities
129|- **Action Required**: Must be fixed before proceeding with other work
130|- **Timeline**: Immediate
131|
132|### HIGH Issues
133|- **Definition**: Major quality issues that should be fixed soon
134|- **Examples**: Monolithic functions, poor modularity, missing error handling
135|- **Action Required**: Should be fixed in next iteration
136|- **Timeline**: 1-2 iterations
137|
138|### MEDIUM Issues
139|- **Definition**: Best practices improvements for code quality
140|- **Examples**: Code readability, maintainability improvements, documentation gaps
141|- **Action Required**: Should be addressed when time permits
142|- **Timeline**: 2-3 iterations
143|
144|### LOW Issues
145|- **Definition**: Minor suggestions and optimizations
146|- **Examples**: Comments, formatting, minor style improvements
147|- **Action Required**: Optional improvements
148|- **Timeline**: When convenient
149|
150|## Systematic Pattern Recognition
151|
152|### Common Anti-Patterns
153|- **Duplicate Code**: Same logic repeated in multiple places
154|- **God Objects**: Classes/functions that do too much
155|- **Magic Numbers**: Unexplained numeric constants
156|- **Dead Code: Unused code that should be removed
157|- **TODO Comments**: Unresolved TODOs in production code
158|
159|### Common Compliance Patterns
160|- **Empty Configuration Files**: Placeholder files without purpose
161|- **Placeholder Values**: Hashes, IDs, or other placeholder values
162|- **Stub Implementations**: Functions that always return fixed values
163|- **Missing Documentation**: Lack of docstrings or comments
164|- **Inconsistent Naming**: Different naming conventions in similar contexts
165|
166|## Best Practices Research Sources
167|
168|### Research Strategy
169|1. **Check Local Knowledge First**: Docs/index.md, Docs/Research/index.md, Docs/Code/index.md
170|2. **Web Search for Current Standards**: Use **{BP}** web search for latest best practices
171|3. **Industry Standards**: Follow established industry standards for language/framework
172|4. **Security Guidelines**: Consult current security best practices
173|5. **Performance Considerations**: Consider performance implications of design decisions

  6|
  7|### Manual Mode
  8|**Behavior**: Process files one by one in alphabetical order, requiring user confirmation at each file for maximum oversight
  9|- **Checkpoint Handling**: Require user confirmation via popup menu before proceeding to each next file
 10|- **Failure Handling**: Stop workflow and await user intervention for retry/modify/abort decision
 11|- **User Control**: Maximum user control over file-by-file progression
 12|- **Risk Mitigation**: Human oversight at each file transition
 13|- **Use Case**: First comprehensive scan, high-risk files, learning phase
 14|
 15|### Manual Batched Mode
 16|**Behavior**: Process files in batches of 5-10 files in alphabetical order, requiring user confirmation between batches
 17|- **Checkpoint Handling**: Require user confirmation via popup menu before proceeding to each next batch
 18|- **Failure Handling**: Stop workflow and await user intervention if batch fails
 19|- **User Control**: Balanced user control with batch-level approval
 20|- **Risk Mitigation**: Human oversight at each batch transition with automated intra-batch processing
 21|- **Use Case**: Balanced efficiency with oversight, medium-risk scans
 22|
 23|### Automatic Batched Mode
 24|**Behavior**: Process files in batches of 5-10 files in alphabetical order automatically without user confirmation
 25|- **Checkpoint Handling**: Proceed automatically through all batches without user intervention
 26|- **Failure Handling**: Stop workflow automatically if a batch fails (auto-stop on errors)
 27|- **User Control**: Minimal user control with maximum automated processing efficiency
 28|- **Risk Mitigation**: Automatic failure detection and stopping at batch level
 29|- **Use Case**: Large codebases, established processes, maximum efficiency
 30|
 31|## Reviewer Execution Mode Handling Patterns
 32|
 33|### Manual Mode Pattern
 34|1. **SCAN** single file line by line
 35|2. **{BP}** web search for current best practices (MANDATORY)
 36|3. Document findings to incremental report
 37|4. **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Require user confirmation via popup menu before proceeding to next file (CHECKPOINT)
 38|5. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "file_{N}_complete"
 39|6. **PRINT**: File completion message with checkpoint confirmation
 40|7. Wait for user approval before proceeding to next file
 41|
 42|### Manual Batched Mode Pattern
 43|1. **SCAN** batch of 5-10 files line by line
 44|2. **{BP}** web search for all files in batch (MANDATORY)
 45|3. Document findings to incremental report for all files
 46|4. **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Require user confirmation via popup menu before proceeding to next batch (CHECKPOINT)
 47|5. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "batch_{N}_complete"
 48|6. **PRINT**: Batch completion message with checkpoint confirmation
 49|7. Wait for user approval before proceeding to next batch
 50|
 51|### Automatic Batched Mode Pattern
 52|1. **SCAN** batch of 5-10 files line by line
 53|2. **{BP}** web search for all files in batch (MANDATORY)
 54|3. Document findings to incremental report for all files
 55|4. **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Proceed automatically to next batch if batch succeeded, stop if batch failed
 56|5. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "batch_{N}_complete" (success) or "batch_{N}_failed" (failure)
 57|6. **PRINT**: Batch completion message (success) or failure message with retry attempt information
 58|7. Proceed automatically to next batch on success, apply retry logic on failure
 59|
 60|## Reviewer Failure Handling Patterns
 61|
 62|### Manual Mode Failure Pattern
 63|1. Detect failure in current file scan
 64|2. **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Stop workflow and await user intervention for retry/modify/abort decision (CHECKPOINT)
 65|3. **RETRY LOGIC**: Implement configurable retry with exponential backoff (max 3 retries) upon user approval
 66|4. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "file_{N}_failed"
 67|5. **PRINT**: Failure message with file-level error details
 68|6. Await user decision on recovery action
 69|
 70|### Manual Batched Mode Failure Pattern
 71|1. Detect failure in current batch
 72|2. **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Stop workflow and await user intervention for retry/modify/abort decision (CHECKPOINT)
 73|3. **RETRY LOGIC**: Implement configurable retry with exponential backoff (max 3 retries) upon user approval
 74|4. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "batch_{N}_failed"
 75|5. **PRINT**: Failure message with batch-level error details
 76|6. Await user decision on recovery action
 77|
 78|### Automatic Batched Mode Failure Pattern
 79|1. Detect failure in current batch
 80|2. **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Stop workflow automatically without requiring human intervention
 81|3. **RETRY LOGIC**: Implement configurable retry with exponential backoff (max 3 retries)
 82|4. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "batch_{N}_failed"
 83|5. **PRINT**: Failure message with retry attempt information
 84|6. Proceed with retry logic automatically

 86|## Reviewer Batch Configuration
 87|
 88|### Batch Size Configuration
 89|- **Default Batch Size**: 5-10 files per batch
 90|- **Batch Size Criteria**: Based on file complexity and token usage
 91|- **Dynamic Adjustment**: Adjust batch size based on available context budget
 92|- **Batch Logging**: Log each batch with file list and processing metadata
 93|
 94|### Batch Processing Order
 95|- **Alphabetical Order**: Files processed in alphabetical order by full path
 96|- **Batch Integrity**: All files in batch must complete before proceeding
 97|- **Context Management**: PostCompaction hook reloads governance files when context is compressed
 98|- **Incremental Documentation**: Findings documented immediately after each batch
 99|
100|## Reviewer Execution Mode Selection Guidelines
101|
102|### Manual Mode Selection
103|- First comprehensive scan of codebase
104|- High-risk or security-critical files
105|- Learning phase for new team members
106|- When detailed review of each file is required
107|- Unknown codebase or unfamiliar patterns
108|
109|### Manual Batched Mode Selection
110|- Established scanning process
111|- Medium-risk codebase
112|- Balance between efficiency and oversight
113|- Regular compliance scans
114|- When batch-level review is sufficient
115|
116|### Automatic Batched Mode Selection
117|- Large codebases (>150 files)
118|- Well-established scanning process
119|- Low-risk routine scans
120|- Time-constrained comprehensive scans
121|- When maximum efficiency is required
122|
123|## Reviewer Retry Logic with Exponential Backoff
124|
125|### Retry Configuration
126|- **Max Retries**: 3 retries maximum
127|- **Backoff Pattern**: Exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, etc.)
128|- **Retry Criteria**: Configurable based on error type
129|- **Retry Logging**: Log each retry attempt with metadata
130|- **Batch Retry**: For batched modes, retry entire batch or individual items based on failure scope
131|
132|### Retry Implementation
133|```python
134|retry_count = 0
135|max_retries = 3
136|backoff_time = 1
137|
138|while retry_count < max_retries:
139|    try:
140|        # Execute file or batch scan
141|        execute_scan()
142|        break  # Success, exit retry loop
143|    except Exception as error:
144|        retry_count += 1
145|        if retry_count >= max_retries:
146|            raise  # Max retries reached
147|        time.sleep(backoff_time)
148|        backoff_time *= 2  # Exponential backoff
149|```
150|

152|

154|- **Mode Storage**: Store selected execution mode in workflow state
155|- **Batch Size**: Store configured batch size for consistency
156|- **Current Batch**: Track current batch number and file indices
157|- **Failure Context**: Store failure context for retry logic
158|

160|- **Mode Selection**: Log mode selection with reasoning
161|- **Batch Processing**: Log each batch with file list and outcomes
162|- **Failure Handling**: Log failure handling patterns and recovery actions
163|- **User Checkpoints**: Log user checkpoint decisions in Manual modes

  1|# Subagent Prompting Reference for Reviewer Agent

  9|- **Large-Scale Scanning**: When scanning >150 files in App/ directory

145|## Subagent Coordination Guidelines
146|
147|### Parallel Execution Strategy
148|- **Launch 4-5 parallel subagents** for independent module categories
149|- **Each subagent receives precise scope** with specific file list
150|- **Define exact output format** for consistent consolidation
151|- **Validate subagent results** against established criteria
152|- **Consolidate findings** into comprehensive report
153|
154|### Scope Definition Rules
155|- **No overlapping scopes** between subagents (prevents redundancy)
156|- **Complete coverage** - all files must be assigned to exactly one subagent
157|- **Clear boundaries** - explicit file lists for each subagent
158|- **Consistent criteria** - all subagents use same compliance reference
159|
160|### Output Format Standardization
161|- **Uniform structure** across all subagent outputs
162|- **Consistent severity ratings** using Compliance_Criteria_Reference.md
163|- **Specific line references** for all findings
164|- **Actionable recommendations** with clear improvement paths
165|- **Best practices sources** documented for all research
166|
167|### Quality Validation
168|- **Cross-validate findings** to eliminate duplicates
169|- **Ensure consistency** across subagent results
170|- **Verify completeness** - all files in scope must be analyzed
171|- **Check accuracy** of severity classifications
172|- **Validate best practices research** quality and relevance
173|
174|## Failure Handling
175|
176|### Subagent Failure Scenarios
177|- **Scope confusion**: Reclarify scope and relaunch subagent
178|- **Quality issues**: Provide feedback and request refinement
179|- **Technical failures**: Investigate and retry with adjusted parameters
180|- **Timeout**: Break into smaller chunks and retry
181|
182|### Recovery Strategies
183|- **Partial results**: Salvage completed work and reassign remaining
184|- **Quality concerns**: Manual review of questionable findings
185|- **Consolidation failures**: Manual intervention for report generation
186|- **Validation failures**: targeted re-analysis of problematic files
187|
188|## Performance Optimization
189|
190|### Chunking Strategy
191|- **Small modules (< 20 files)**: Single subagent
192|- **Medium modules (20-50 files)**: 2-3 subagents
193|- **Large modules (> 50 files)**: 4-5 subagents
194|- **Adjust based on complexity** and analysis depth required
195|
196|### Resource Management
197|- **Monitor subagent quota** usage for recovery tracking
198|- **Balance parallel execution** with system resources
199|- **Implement progressive backoff** if rate limiting occurs
200|- **Cache best practices research** across subagents where applicable

  1|# Review Mode Patterns
  2|
  3|**Purpose**: Reviewer-specific execution mode patterns for comprehensive code review workflows.
  4|
  5|## Review Mode Definitions
  6|
  7|### Manual Review Mode
  8|**Behavior**: Require user confirmation at every single review step for maximum oversight
  9|- **Checkpoint Handling**: Require user confirmation via popup menu before proceeding to each next review step (every step, not just failures)
 10|- **Failure Handling**: Stop review and await user intervention for retry/modify/abort decision
 11|- **User Control**: Maximum user control over review progression with step-by-step approval
 12|- **Risk Mitigation**: Human oversight at each review transition and every workflow step
 13|
 14|### Auto Review Mode
 15|**Behavior**: Don't continue on review failures (auto-stop on errors, proceed automatically through successes)
 16|- **Checkpoint Handling**: Proceed automatically to next review step
 17|- **Failure Handling**: Stop review automatically without requiring human intervention
 18|- **Efficiency**: Balanced efficiency with failure detection
 19|- **Risk Mitigation**: Automatic failure detection and stopping
 20|
 21|### Complete Review Mode
 22|**Behavior**: Continue past review failures (ignore all errors for maximum coverage)
 23|- **Checkpoint Handling**: Proceed automatically to next review step
 24|- **Failure Handling**: Continue review automatically, ignoring failures
 25|- **Efficiency**: Maximum efficiency with failure tolerance
 26|- **Risk Mitigation**: Minimal risk mitigation
 27|
 28|## Review Mode Handling Patterns
 29|
 30|### Step Transition Handling
 31|**Manual Review Mode Pattern**:
 32|1. Complete current review step action
 33|2. **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Require user confirmation via popup menu before proceeding to next review step (CHECKPOINT at every step)
 34|3. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "step_{N}_complete"
 35|4. **PRINT**: Review step completion message with checkpoint confirmation
 36|5. Wait for user approval before proceeding to next review step
 37|
 38|**Auto Review Mode Pattern**:
 39|1. Complete current review step action
 40|2. **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Proceed automatically to next review step if step succeeded, stop if step failed
 41|3. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "step_{N}_complete" (success) or "step_{N}_failed" (failure)
 42|4. **PRINT**: Review step completion message (success) or failure message with retry attempt information
 43|5. Proceed automatically to next review step on success, apply retry logic on failure
 44|
 45|**Complete Review Mode Pattern**:
 46|1. Complete current review step action (even if failures occur)
 47|2. **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Proceed automatically to next review step regardless of success/failure
 48|3. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "step_{N}_complete" (even if step failed)
 49|4. **PRINT**: Review step completion message (including any failures but continue review)
 50|5. Proceed to next review step automatically
 51|
 52|### Failure Handling Patterns
 53|**Manual Review Mode Failure Pattern**:
 54|1. Detect failure in current review step
 55|2. **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Stop review and await user intervention for retry/modify/abort decision (CHECKPOINT)
 56|3. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "step_{N}_failed"
 57|4. **PRINT**: Failure message with error details
 58|5. Await user decision on recovery action
 59|
 60|**Auto Review Mode Failure Pattern**:
 61|1. Detect failure in current review step
 62|2. **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Stop review automatically without requiring human intervention
 63|3. **RETRY LOGIC**: Implement configurable retry with exponential backoff (max 3 retries)
 64|4. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "step_{N}_failed"
 65|5. **PRINT**: Failure message with retry attempt information
 66|6. Proceed with retry logic automatically
 67|
 68|**Complete Review Mode Failure Pattern**:
 69|1. Detect failure in current review step
 70|2. **EXECUTION MODE HANDLING**: Continue review automatically, ignoring the failure
 71|3. **RETRY LOGIC**: Implement configurable retry with exponential backoff (max 3 retries)
 72|4. **STATUS TRACKING**: Update workflow status to "step_{N}_complete" (despite failure)
 73|5. **PRINT**: Failure message but continue review
 74|6. Proceed to next review step automatically
 75|
 76|## Review-Specific Patterns
 77|
 78|### File-by-File Review Pattern
 79|**Manual Mode**: Require user confirmation before proceeding to examine each file
 80|**Auto Mode**: Automatically proceed through files sequentially, stop on critical failures
 81|**Complete Mode**: Automatically proceed through all files regardless of findings
 82|
 83|### Subagent Coordination Pattern
 84|**Manual Mode**: Require user confirmation before launching each subagent
 85|**Auto Mode**: Automatically launch subagents according to coordination strategy
 86|**Complete Mode**: Automatically launch all subagents regardless of individual failures
 87|
 88|### Findings Consolidation Pattern
 89|**Manual Mode**: Require user confirmation before proceeding to consolidate each category of findings
 90|**Auto Mode**: Automatically consolidate findings as subagent results arrive
 91|**Complete Mode**: Automatically consolidate all findings regardless of subagent failures
 92|
 93|## Usage Guidelines
 94|
 95|### Mode Selection Process
 96|1. **Assess Review Scope**: Evaluate review complexity and file count
 97|2. **Present Options**: Present review mode options to user
 98|3. **Recommend**: Recommend appropriate mode based on assessment
 99|4. **User Selection**: User selects mode via popup menu
100|5. **Store Mode**: Store selected review mode in workflow state
101|
102|### Mode Execution
103|1. **Apply Pattern**: Apply appropriate review mode pattern
104|2. **Handle Checkpoints**: Handle checkpoints according to mode
105|3. **Handle Failures**: Handle failures according to mode
106|4. **Track Progress**: Track progress according to mode requirements
107|5. **Log Actions**: Log mode-specific actions for audit trail
</file-view>

  1|# Convergence Loop Patterns
  2|
  3|**Purpose**: Universal convergence loop patterns for iterative improvement processes across all agent workflows.
  4|
  5|## Universal Convergence Loop Pattern
  6|
  7|### Loop Structure
  8|- **Loop Definition**: Iterative process between phases until convergence criteria are met
  9|- **Back-Edge Pattern**: Return to previous phase after current phase completion
 10|- **Loop Exit Condition**: Quality thresholds or stability criteria achieved
 11|- **Loop Cap**: Maximum iterations to prevent infinite loops
 12|
 13|### Convergence Logic
 14|1. **Execute Current Phase**: Complete current phase actions
 15|2. **Evaluate Results**: Assess phase outcomes against convergence criteria
 16|3. **Check Convergence**: Determine if convergence criteria are met
 17|4. **Exit if Converged**: Proceed to next phase if convergence achieved
 18|5. **Loop if Not Converged**: Return to previous phase and iterate
 19|
 20|### Universal Convergence Criteria
 21|- **Quality Score Threshold**: Quality metrics meet defined thresholds
 22|- **Stability Metrics**: Results stabilize across iterations
 23|- **Issue Resolution**: Critical and high-priority issues resolved
 24|- **Panel/Expert Agreement**: Expert consensus achieved (when applicable)
 25|
 26|### Universal Loop Caps
 27|- **Maximum Iterations**: Define maximum iterations per loop type
 28|- **Escalation Procedures**: Define escalation when loop cap reached
 29|- **User Intervention**: Define when to request user decision
 30|- **Alternative Strategies**: Define alternative approaches when loops fail
 31|
 32|## Agent-Specific Customization
 33|
 34|Each agent should define:
 35|- **Loop Definitions**: Agent-specific phase loop structures
 36|- **Convergence Criteria**: Agent-specific quality thresholds and stability metrics
 37|- **Loop Caps**: Agent-specific iteration limits
 38|- **Escalation Procedures**: Agent-specific escalation when loops fail
 39|
 40|## Usage Guidelines
 41|
 42|### Universal Pattern Application
 43|1. **Apply Universal Pattern**: Use the universal convergence loop pattern for iterative improvement
 44|2. **Define Agent-Specific Loops**: Create agent-specific loop definitions in agent Reference/ folders
 45|3. **Set Convergence Criteria**: Define agent-specific quality thresholds and stability metrics
 46|4. **Implement Loop Logic**: Integrate convergence logic into workflow phases
 47|5. **Document Escalation**: Document escalation procedures for loop failures
 48|
 49|### Convergence Loop Consistency
 50|- **Universal Pattern**: All agents follow the same convergence loop pattern
 51|- **Agent-Specific Criteria**: Each agent defines its own convergence criteria
 52|- **Consistent Logic**: Same convergence logic across all agents (execute â†’ evaluate â†’ check â†’ exit/loop)
 53|- **Universal Escalation**: Same escalation pattern when loops fail
</file-view>

  1|# Execution Mode Patterns (General Reference)
  2|
  3|**Purpose**: General reference for execution mode patterns across all agent workflows.
  4|
  5|## Agent-Specific Execution Mode Patterns
  6|
  7|Each agent defines its own execution mode patterns based on its operational needs and workflow types. Refer to agent-specific Reference folders for detailed execution mode definitions:
  8|
  9|### Architect Execution Mode Patterns
 10|- **Location**: Workflow/Architect/Reference/Execution_Mode_Patterns.md
 11|- **Modes**: Full Comprehensive, Basic Essential, Targeted, Quick Check
 12|- **Focus**: Architecture consistency validation workflows
 13|- **Use Case**: Infrastructure and governance validation
 14|
 15|### Reviewer Execution Mode Patterns
 16|- **Location**: Workflow/Reviewer/Reference/Execution_Mode_Patterns.md
 17|- **Modes**: Manual, Manual Batched, Automatic Batched
 18|- **Focus**: File processing and compliance scanning workflows
 19|- **Use Case**: Code review and best practice verification
 20|
 21|### Other Agent Execution Modes
 22|- **Executor**: Implementation and execution patterns (see Workflow/Executor/Reference/)
 23|- **Planner**: Planning and strategy patterns (see Workflow/Planner/Reference/)
 24|- **Researcher**: Research and analysis patterns (see Workflow/Researcher/Reference/)
 25|
 26|## Universal Execution Mode Concepts
 27|
 28|### Common Execution Mode Elements
 29|All agent-specific execution modes should include:
 30|- **Mode Definitions**: Clear behavior specifications for each mode
 31|- **Checkpoint Handling**: How checkpoints are managed in each mode
 32|- **Failure Handling**: How failures are handled in each mode
 33|- **User Control**: Level of user control in each mode
 34|- **Use Cases**: When to use each mode
 35|- **Handling Patterns**: Step-by-step execution patterns
 36|- **Failure Patterns**: Failure recovery patterns
 37|- **Retry Logic**: Retry configuration and implementation
 38|
 39|### Universal Retry Logic
 40|All execution modes should implement consistent retry logic:
 41|- **Max Retries**: 3 retries maximum
 42|- **Backoff Pattern**: Exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, etc.)
 43|- **Retry Criteria**: Configurable based on error type
 44|- **Retry Logging**: Log each retry attempt with metadata
 45|
 46|### Universal State Management
 47|All execution modes should implement consistent state management:
 48|- **Mode Storage**: Store selected execution mode in workflow state
 49|- **Progress Tracking**: Track progress according to mode requirements
 50|- **Audit Trail**: Log mode-specific actions for audit trail
 51|
 52|## Execution Mode Design Principles
 53|
 54|### Agent-Specific Customization
 55|- Each agent defines execution modes based on its operational needs
 56|- Modes should reflect the agent's specific workflow types and use cases
 57|- Agent-specific patterns are stored in agent Reference folders
 58|
 59|### Universal Consistency
 60|- All execution modes should follow universal retry logic patterns
 61|- All execution modes should implement consistent state management
 62|- All execution modes should provide clear checkpoint and failure handling
 63|
 64|### Workflow Integration
 65|- Execution modes are defined in workflow headers
 66|- Phase 1 of each workflow presents execution mode options
 67|- Workflows reference their agent-specific execution mode patterns

 73|- **Header**: Include "Execution Modes" field with agent-specific options

  1|# Implementation Mode Patterns
  2|
  3|**Purpose**: Universal implementation mode patterns for all agent workflows.
  4|
  5|## Implementation Mode Options
  6|
  7|### Mode 1: Automated
  8|**Description**: Agent implements automatically
  9|- Agent executes all implementation steps without user intervention
 10|- Continuous progression through implementation phases
 11|- Automatic testing and validation
 12|- Minimal user interaction required
 13|
 14|**Benefits**:
 15|- Faster implementation
 16|- Consistent execution
 17|- Reduced user overhead
 18|- Efficient for standard tasks
 19|
 20|**Risks**:
 21|- Less user control over implementation
 22|- Potential for unexpected decisions
 23|- May not handle edge cases optimally
 24|- Less visibility into implementation process
 25|
 26|### Mode 2: Manual
 27|**Description**: User and agent use iterative pattern for implementation
 28|- Agent and user collaborate on implementation
 29|- User provides guidance and approval at key points
 30|- Iterative approach with frequent user feedback
 31|- User maintains control over implementation direction
 32|
 33|**Benefits**:
 34|- Greater user control
 35|- Better handling of edge cases
 36|- Domain expertise integration
 37|- Increased visibility
 38|
 39|**Risks**:
 40|- Slower implementation
 41|- Higher user time commitment
 42|- Potential for user fatigue
 43|- May introduce inconsistencies
 44|
 45|## Mode Selection Criteria
 46|
 47|### Complexity Assessment
 48|- **Low Complexity**: Consider Automated mode
 49|- **Medium Complexity**: Assess based on risk and user preference
 50|- **High Complexity**: Manual mode recommended
 51|
 52|### Risk Assessment
 53|- **Low Risk**: Can use Automated mode
 54|- **Medium Risk**: Assess based on complexity and user confidence
 55|- **High Risk**: Manual mode recommended
 56|
 57|### User Confidence
 58|- **High Confidence**: Agent has relevant expertise and track record
 59|- **Medium Confidence**: Assess based on task complexity
 60|- **Low Confidence**: Manual mode recommended
 61|
 62|### Time Constraints
 63|- **Tight Timeline**: Automated mode for faster execution
 64|- **Moderate Timeline**: Balance based on complexity and risk
 65|- **Flexible Timeline**: Manual mode for quality focus
 66|
 67|## Implementation Execution Patterns
 68|
 69|### Automated Mode Execution
 70|1. **Specification Phase**: Agent creates detailed specification
 71|2. **Implementation Phase**: Agent implements automatically
 72|3. **Testing Phase**: Agent tests automatically
 73|4. **Validation Phase**: Agent validates automatically
 74|5. **Documentation Phase**: Agent documents automatically
 75|6. **Completion Phase**: Agent notifies user of completion
 76|
 77|### Manual Mode Execution
 78|1. **Specification Phase**: Agent creates specification, user reviews
 79|2. **Implementation Phase**: Agent implements function-by-function, user approves each
 80|3. **Testing Phase**: Agent tests, user reviews results
 81|4. **Validation Phase**: Agent validates, user confirms compliance
 82|5. **Documentation Phase**: Agent documents, user reviews and approves
 83|6. **Completion Phase**: Agent notifies user, user validates and accepts
 84|
 85|## Mode Switching
 86|
 87|### Mid-Workflow Mode Changes
 88|- **Automated to Manual**: User can switch to Manual mode if issues arise
 89|- **Manual to Automated**: Generally not recommended mid-workflow
 90|- **Mode Change Documentation**: Document mode changes with reasoning
 91|- **State Preservation**: Preserve implementation state during mode changes
 92|
 93|### Mode Change Triggers
 94|- **Complexity Increase**: Switch to Manual if complexity increases unexpectedly
 95|- **Risk Discovery**: Switch to Manual if unexpected risks discovered
 96|- **User Preference**: User can request mode change at any time
 97|- **Failure Recovery**: May switch modes for recovery from failures
 98|
 99|## Usage Guidelines
100|
101|### Mode Selection Process
102|1. **Assess Task**: Evaluate task complexity, risk, and user confidence
103|2. **Present Options**: Present both mode options with trade-offs
104|3. **Recommend**: Recommend mode based on assessment
105|4. **User Selection**: User selects mode via popup menu
106|5. **Execute**: Execute implementation according to selected mode
107|
108|### Mode Execution
109|1. **Follow Pattern**: Execute according to selected mode pattern
110|2. **Maintain Communication**: Maintain appropriate communication level
111|3. **Seek Approval**: Seek user approval at appropriate checkpoints
112|4. **Adapt**: Adapt execution based on feedback
113|5. **Complete**: Complete implementation according to mode
114|
115|### Mode Evaluation
116|1. **Track Performance**: Track mode-specific performance metrics
117|2. **User Feedback**: Collect user feedback on mode effectiveness
118|3. **Pattern Analysis**: Analyze which modes work best for which tasks
119|4. **Refine Criteria**: Refine mode selection criteria based on patterns
120|5. **Optimize**: Optimize mode execution patterns over time
</file-view>

  1|# Execution Strategy Guidelines
  2|
  3|**Purpose**: Universal execution strategy specifications for all agent workflows.
  4|
  5|## Universal Strategy Configuration Patterns
  6|
  7|### Strategy Selection Pattern
  8|1. Agent selects appropriate strategy based on task complexity
  9|2. Strategy stored in workflow state for consistent behavior
 10|3. Strategy governs failure handling and progression throughout workflow
 11|4. Strategy can be changed during workflow if conditions change
 12|
 13|### Failure Handling Pattern
 14|- **Manual**: Stop and await user intervention for retry/modify/abort decision
 15|- **Auto**: Stop automatically without requiring human intervention
 16|- **Complete**: Continue automatically, ignoring failures
 17|- **Retry Logic**: Configurable exponential backoff for automatic strategies
 18|
 19|### Checkpoint Pattern
 20|- **Manual Mode**: Require user confirmation via popup menu before proceeding
 21|- **Auto/Complete Modes**: Proceed automatically without checkpoints
 22|- **Checkpoint Criteria**: Major phase transitions, critical decisions, failure points
 23|
 24|## Universal Strategy Guidelines
 25|
 26|### Strategy Consistency
 27|- Maintain consistent strategy behavior throughout workflow execution
 28|- Document strategy changes with rationale
 29|- Update workflow state when strategy changes
 30|- Notify user of strategy transitions
 31|
 32|### Strategy Selection Criteria
 33|- **Task Complexity**: Simple tasks may use faster strategies
 34|- **Risk Level**: High-risk tasks may require manual oversight
 35|- **User Preference**: Allow user to select strategy when appropriate
 36|- **System Constraints**: Resource limits may influence strategy choice
 37|
 38|### Strategy Monitoring
 39|- Track strategy effectiveness across workflow executions
 40|- Monitor failure rates and recovery patterns
 41|- Adjust strategy based on performance metrics
 42|- Document strategy evolution patterns
</file-view>
```

  2|
  3|**Purpose**: Universal performance metrics framework for all agent workflows.
  4|
  5|## Universal Performance Metrics

  1|# Quality Assessment Framework
  2|
  3|**Purpose**: Universal quality assessment framework for all agent workflows.
  4|
  5|## Universal Quality Dimensions
  6|
  7|### Dimension 1: Accuracy
  8|**What it scores**: Factual correctness and alignment with requirements
  9|
 10|**Universal Evaluation Criteria**:
 11|- Work output accurately reflects user requirements
 12|- Steps/codes correctly identify needed changes
 13|- Dependencies/relationships are technically accurate
 14|- No false claims or incorrect assumptions
 15|- Changes/approaches are feasible for implementation
 16|
 17|**Universal Scoring Levels**:
 18|- **5 (Excellent)**: All information accurate, perfect alignment with requirements
 19|- **4 (Good)**: Minor inaccuracies that don't affect implementation
 20|- **3 (Fair)**: Some inaccuracies that may require clarification
 21|- **2 (Poor)**: Significant inaccuracies affecting implementation
 22|- **1 (Critical)**: Major factual errors that would cause implementation failure
 23|
 24|**Hard Fail**: Goal/work misalignment with user requirements or technically impossible changes
 25|
 26|---
 27|
 28|### Dimension 2: Completeness
 29|**What it scores**: Inclusion of all necessary elements
 30|
 31|**Universal Evaluation Criteria**:
 32|- All required sections/patterns present
 33|- Metadata complete where applicable
 34|- Steps/codes cover all aspects of needed changes
 35|- Dependencies account for all relationships
 36|- No missing critical information for implementation
 37|
 38|**Universal Scoring Levels**:
 39|- **5 (Excellent)**: All elements present, fully comprehensive
 40|- **4 (Good)**: Minor omissions that don't affect implementation
 41|- **3 (Fair)**: Some omissions that may require clarification
 42|- **2 (Poor)**: Significant omissions affecting implementation
 43|- **1 (Critical)**: Critical missing elements that would cause implementation failure
 44|
 45|**Hard Fail**: Missing required sections or metadata
 46|
 47|---
 48|
 49|### Dimension 3: Clarity
 50|**What it scores**: Readability and understandability
 51|
 52|**Universal Evaluation Criteria**:
 53|- Goal/statement is clear and user-focused
 54|- Steps/codes are unambiguous and actionable
 55|- Language is precise and not vague
 56|- Context provides necessary background
 57|- Dependencies/relationships are clearly expressed
 58|
 59|**Universal Scoring Levels**:
 60|- **5 (Excellent)**: Crystal clear, unambiguous, easy to follow
 61|- **4 (Good)**: Minor ambiguities that can be resolved with context
 62|- **3 (Fair)**: Some ambiguities requiring clarification
 63|- **2 (Poor)**: Significant ambiguities affecting implementation
 64|- **1 (Critical)**: Unclear goals or steps that would cause implementation confusion
 65|
 66|**Hard Fail**: Ambiguous goal statement or unclear critical steps
 67|
 68|---
 69|
 70|### Dimension 4: Structure
 71|**What it scores**: Organization and logical flow
 72|
 73|**Universal Evaluation Criteria**:
 74|- Work follows template/format requirements exactly
 75|- Steps/codes are logically ordered and sequential
 76|- Dependencies/relationships are properly structured
 77|- No circular dependencies or contradictions
 78|- Work follows length guidelines when applicable
 79|
 80|**Universal Scoring Levels**:
 81|- **5 (Excellent)**: Perfect structure, optimal organization
 82|- **4 (Good)**: Minor structural issues that don't affect execution
 83|- **3 (Fair)**: Some structural issues requiring clarification
 84|- **2 (Poor)**: Significant structural issues affecting execution
 85|- **1 (Critical)**: Structure violations that would cause execution failure
 86|
 87|**Hard Fail**: Circular dependencies or format violations
 88|
 89|---
 90|
 91|### Dimension 5: Context
 92|**What it scores**: Background information and rationale
 93|
 94|**Universal Evaluation Criteria**:
 95|- Context explains why work matters from user perspective
 96|- Context describes what can be done after changes
 97|- Context provides necessary background and dependencies
 98|- Rationale is clear and supports the approach
 99|- Context is sufficient for implementation decisions
100|
101|**Universal Scoring Levels**:
102|- **5 (Excellent)**: Rich context, perfect rationale, comprehensive background
103|- **4 (Good)**: Minor context gaps that don't affect implementation
104|- **3 (Fair)**: Some context gaps requiring clarification
105|- **2 (Poor)**: Significant context gaps affecting implementation
106|- **1 (Critical)**: Missing critical context that would cause implementation failure
107|
108|**Hard Fail**: Missing context or rationale for critical decisions
109|
110|---
111|
112|## Universal Quality Scoring
113|
114|### Universal Weighting
115|- **Accuracy**: 30% (most critical)
116|- **Completeness**: 25% (critical)
117|- **Clarity**: 20% (important)
118|- **Structure**: 15% (important)
119|- **Context**: 10% (supporting)
120|
121|### Quality Score Calculation
122|```
123|Overall Score = (Accuracy Ã— 0.30) + (Completeness Ã— 0.25) + (Clarity Ã— 0.20) + (Structure Ã— 0.15) + (Context Ã— 0.10)
124|```
125|
126|### Universal Quality Thresholds
127|- **5.0 - 4.5**: Excellent - Clean pass, proceed to next phase
128|- **4.4 - 3.5**: Good - Clean pass, proceed to next phase
129|- **3.4 - 2.5**: Fair - Proceed with documented rationale
130|- **2.4 - 1.5**: Poor - Requires revisions before proceeding
131|- **1.4 - 0.0**: Critical - Block proceeding, mandatory revisions
132|
133|### Hard Fail Conditions
134|If any dimension has a hard fail, the overall quality score is automatically **0.0** regardless of other dimensions.

141|- **Focus**: Plan quality assessment with planning-specific criteria

163|- **Reference**: Universal framework with reviewer-specific criteria integration

167|## Usage Guidelines
168|
169|### Universal Framework Application
170|1. **Apply Universal Dimensions**: Use the 5 universal dimensions as baseline
171|2. **Customize for Agent Type**: Add agent-specific criteria within universal framework
172|3. **Weight Adjustments**: Adjust weighting based on agent-specific priorities

189|- Document framework changes with rationale

  1|# Quota Handling Patterns
  2|
  3|**Purpose**: Universal quota handling patterns for agent workflows.
  4|
  5|**Status**: âœ… **IMPLEMENTED** - Basic quota tracking for internal subagents
  6|
  7|## Overview
  8|
  9|This document describes patterns for handling quota exhaustion during agent execution, with specific focus on internal subagents that are used in Round Table reviews and other multi-agent coordination scenarios.
 10|
 11|## Implementation Scope
 12|
 13|**Implemented**:
 14|- Basic quota tracking for internal subagents
 15|- Step progress tracking for quota awareness
 16|- Simple recovery patterns for quota exhaustion
 17|
 18|**Not Implemented**:
 19|- Full state persistence layer (deferred)
 20|- Automated quota exhaustion detection (deferred)
 21|- Agent-to-agent state synchronization (deferred)
 22|
 23|## Context
 24|
 25|**External Agents**: External services (e.g., Chathub.gg) are not subject to quota limitations for this system.
 26|
 27|**Internal Subagents**: Internal subagents used in Round Table reviews and other multi-agent operations are subject to quota limitations and require tracking and recovery mechanisms.
 28|
 29|## Basic Quota Tracking Pattern
 30|
 31|### Internal Subagent Quota Awareness
 32|- **Step Tracking**: Track step progress for internal subagents to understand quota consumption
 33|- **Quota Estimation**: Estimate quota usage per step based on typical token consumption
 34|- **Quota Monitoring**: Monitor quota status before launching internal subagents
 35|- **Fallback Planning**: Have backup plans if quota exhaustion occurs
 36|
 37|### Recovery Pattern for Internal Subagents
 38|- **Quota Exhaustion Detection**: Monitor for quota exhaustion signals during subagent execution
 39|- **Step Recovery**: Resume from last completed step if quota exhaustion occurs
 40|- **Partial Results**: Use partial results from completed steps if full execution fails
 41|- **Escalation**: Escalate to user if quota exhaustion prevents completion
 42|
 43|## Implementation Requirements (Basic)
 44|
 45|### Workflow Integration
 46|- Add quota awareness checks before launching internal subagents
 47|- Track step progress for internal subagents
 48|- Implement fallback mechanisms for quota exhaustion
 49|- Add quota status reporting in workflow logs
 50|
 51|### Subagent Guidelines
 52|- Internal subagents should be designed for efficient quota usage
 53|- Implement step-by-step progress reporting
 54|- Provide checkpoint-style output for recovery
 55|- Design for graceful degradation on quota exhaustion
 56|
 57|## Implementation Status
 58|
 59|**Currently Implemented**:
 60|- Basic quota tracking in Planner workflow for internal Round Table reviews
 61|- Step progress tracking for internal subagents
 62|- Manual quota monitoring and fallback patterns
 63|
 64|**Requires Future Implementation**:
 65|- Automated quota exhaustion detection
 66|- Full state persistence for subagent sessions
 67|- Agent-to-agent state synchronization protocols
 68|- Audit trail for quota events
 69|
 70|## Current Practice
 71|
 72|**For internal subagents**:
 73|- Plan work within quota limits for subagent operations
 74|- Implement manual checkpoint strategies for long-running tasks
 75|- Monitor quota usage during execution
 76|- Use step progress tracking for recovery
 77|
 78|**For external agents**:
 79|- External agents (Chathub.gg) are not subject to quota limitations
 80|- Use external agents for quota-intensive operations when available
 81|
 82|## Architectural Recommendation
 83|
 84|Until the infrastructure for stateful subagent recovery is implemented:
 85|1. **Design subagent tasks** to complete within quota limits
 86|2. **Implement manual recovery** strategies as needed
 87|3. **Use external agents** for quota-intensive operations
 88|4. **Track step progress** for internal subagent recovery
 89|5. **Monitor quota usage** proactively
 90|
 91|## Next Steps
 92|
 93|This framework should be revisited when:
 94|- State persistence infrastructure is available
 95|- Subagent communication protocols are implemented
 96|- Recovery trigger mechanisms are in place
 97|- Audit requirements for quota events are defined
</file-view>

  1|# Role Responsibilities Framework
  2|
  3|**Purpose**: Universal role responsibility framework for all agent workflows.
  4|
  5|## Universal Role Structure
  6|
  7|### Agent (Universal Responsibilities)
  8|- **Primary Responsibility**: Execute workflow steps according to agent type
  9|- **Governance Enforcement**: Enforce governance rules and constraints
 10|- **Task Execution**: Complete assigned tasks with quality and compliance
 11|- **User Communication**: Provide clear communication and status updates
 12|- **Error Handling**: Apply appropriate error recovery strategies
 13|- **Quality Assurance**: Ensure work meets quality standards
 14|- **Documentation**: Maintain proper documentation and logging
 15|
 16|### User (Universal Responsibilities)
 17|- **Task Specification**: Provide clear task requirements and objectives
 18|- **Decision Approval**: Approve key decisions and strategy selections
 19|- **Feedback Provision**: Provide feedback on work quality and execution
 20|- **Requirement Clarification**: Clarify ambiguous requirements when needed
 21|- **Resource Availability**: Ensure required resources and access are available
 22|- **Testing and Validation**: Test implemented work and provide feedback
 23|- **Implementation Execution**: Execute plans according to specifications (when applicable)
 24|
 25|### Governance System (Universal Responsibilities)
 26|- **Validation Enforcement**: Enforce validation rules and compliance checks
 27|- **Permission Management**: Manage tool and resource permissions
 28|- **State Tracking**: Maintain workflow state and progress tracking
 29|- **Audit Trail**: Maintain comprehensive audit trail of all actions
 30|- **Error Detection**: Detect and report errors and compliance violations
 31|- **Security Enforcement**: Enforce security boundaries and access controls
 32|- **Compliance Monitoring**: Monitor compliance with governance rules
 33|
 34|---
 35|
 36|## Agent-Specific Role Responsibilities
 37|
 38|### Planner Agent (Specific Responsibilities)
 39|- **Plan Creation**: Create detailed, implementation-ready plans
 40|- **Dependency Analysis**: Analyze and document dependencies and relationships
 41|- **Quality Assessment**: Ensure plan quality through comprehensive review
 42|- **Scope Definition**: Define clear scope boundaries and constraints
 43|- **Implementation Strategy**: Develop implementation strategies and approaches
 44|- **Plan Validation**: Validate plans through validation-based system
 45|- **Round Table Coordination**: Coordinate internal and external review processes
 46|
 47|### Architect Agent (Specific Responsibilities)
 48|- **Infrastructure Design**: Design infrastructure and governance frameworks
 49|- **Rule Development**: Create and maintain governance rules and constraints
 50|- **Workflow Design**: Design agent workflows and processes
 51|- **System Architecture**: Design system-level architecture and patterns
 52|- **Script Development**: Create implementation scripts and automation
 53|- **Configuration Management**: Manage agent and system configuration
 54|- **Compliance Validation**: Ensure architectural compliance with governance
 55|
 56|### Executor Agent (Specific Responsibilities)
 57|- **Plan Execution**: Execute approved plans according to specifications
 58|- **Code Implementation**: Implement code according to plan requirements
 59|- **Testing Implementation**: Implement tests according to plan specifications
 60|- **Quality Verification**: Verify implementation quality and completeness
 61|- **Integration and Deployment**: Prepare integration and deployment artifacts
 62|- **Documentation**: Create/update documentation as specified
 63|- **Final Validation**: Verify complete implementation matches approved plan
 64|
 65|### Reviewer Agent (Specific Responsibilities)
 66|- **Quality Analysis**: Analyze execution quality and patterns
 67|- **Pattern Recognition**: Identify recurring issues and governance gaps
 68|- **Rule Recommendations**: Recommend improvements to rules and workflows
 69|- **Governance Enhancement**: Suggest governance improvements
 70|- **Validation Analysis**: Analyze validation failure patterns and recommend fixes
 71|- **Quality Metrics**: Evaluate quality metrics and trends
 72|- **Feedback Loop**: Provide feedback to improve agent performance
 73|
 74|### Researcher Agent (Specific Responsibilities)
 75|- **External Research**: Perform external research and investigation
 76|- **Design Documentation**: Create design documents with proper citations
 77|- **Best Practices**: Research and document best practices
 78|- **Analysis**: Provide comprehensive analysis and recommendations
 79|- **Documentation**: Create well-documented research findings
 80|- **Verification**: Verify findings against current best practices
 81|- **Context Provision**: Provide context and background for decisions
 82|
 83|---
 84|
 85|## Universal Interaction Patterns
 86|
 87|### Agent-User Interaction
 88|- **Task Initiation**: User provides task, agent confirms understanding
 89|- **Progress Updates**: Agent provides regular status updates
 90|- **Decision Points**: User approves key decisions and strategies
 91|- **Feedback Loop**: User provides feedback, agent incorporates
 92|- **Clarification**: User clarifies requirements when needed
 93|- **Approval Checkpoints**: User approves work at key checkpoints
 94|- **Final Acceptance**: User accepts completed work
 95|
 96|### Agent-Governance Interaction
 97|- **Rule Loading**: Agent loads governance rules at workflow start
 98|- **Validation Requests**: Agent requests validation at key points
 99|- **Permission Checks**: Governance system validates permissions
100|- **State Updates**: Agent updates workflow state for tracking
101|- **Error Reporting**: Governance system reports errors and violations
102|- **Audit Logging**: Both agent and governance maintain audit trails
103|- **Compliance Enforcement**: Governance enforces compliance automatically
104|
105|### Agent-Agent Interaction
106|- **Handoff Patterns**: Clear handoff protocols between agents
107|- **Context Transfer**: Comprehensive context transfer between agents
108|- **Role Boundaries**: Clear boundaries between agent responsibilities
109|- **Coordination**: Coordination protocols for multi-agent workflows
110|- **Feedback Channels**: Structured feedback channels between agents
111|- **Escalation**: Clear escalation procedures for issues
112|- **Collaboration**: Defined collaboration patterns for complex tasks
113|
114|---
115|
116|## Universal Quality Hierarchy
117|
118|### Quality > Token Cost > Efficiency
119|When making trade-off decisions, follow this universal hierarchy:
120|- **Quality**: Never compromise on quality standards
121|- **Token Cost**: Optimize after quality is ensured
122|- **Efficiency**: Optimize after quality and token cost are addressed
123|
124|### Application by Agent Type
125|- **Planner**: Plan quality > Planning efficiency > Token optimization
126|- **Architect**: Infrastructure quality > Design efficiency > Token optimization
127|- **Executor**: Implementation quality > Execution efficiency > Token optimization
128|- **Reviewer**: Review quality > Analysis efficiency > Token optimization
129|- **Researcher**: Research quality > Investigation efficiency > Token optimization
130|
131|---
132|
133|## Universal Continuous Improvement
134|
135|### Pattern Recognition
136|- **Issue Identification**: Identify recurring patterns across workflows
137|- **Trend Analysis**: Analyze trends in quality and performance
138|- **Root Cause Analysis**: Identify root causes of recurring issues
139|- **Process Improvement**: Recommend process improvements based on patterns
140|
141|### Rules Evolution
142|- **Pattern Integration**: Integrate patterns from failures into rules
143|- **Workflow Updates**: Update workflows based on pattern analysis
144|- **Standard Enhancement**: Enhance standards based on best practices
145|- **Documentation Updates**: Update documentation to reflect improvements
146|
147|### Feedback Integration
148|- **User Feedback**: Integrate user feedback into role responsibilities
149|- **Agent Feedback**: Integrate agent feedback into workflows
150|- **System Feedback**: Integrate system feedback into governance
151|- **Continuous Learning**: Maintain continuous learning and adaptation
152|
153|---
154|
155|## Usage Guidelines
156|
157|### Framework Application
158|1. **Start with Universal**: Begin with universal role responsibilities
159|2. **Add Agent-Specific**: Add agent-specific responsibilities for each agent type
160|3. **Define Interactions**: Define interaction patterns between roles
161|4. **Set Quality Standards**: Apply universal quality hierarchy
162|5. **Enable Improvement**: Enable continuous improvement processes
163|
164|### Role Responsibility Updates
165|1. **Pattern Analysis**: Analyze patterns to identify needed updates
166|2. **Impact Assessment**: Assess impact of role responsibility changes
167|3. **Stakeholder Communication**: Communicate changes to stakeholders
168|4. **Documentation Updates**: Update documentation with new responsibilities
169|5. **Training**: Provide training if responsibilities change significantly
170|
171|### Cross-Agent Consistency
172|- **Universal Elements**: Maintain consistent universal elements across agents
173|- **Agent-Specific**: Allow agent-specific customization where needed
174|- **Interaction Patterns**: Ensure consistent interaction patterns
175|- **Quality Standards**: Apply consistent quality standards
176|- **Continuous Improvement**: Maintain consistent improvement processes
</file-view>

  1|# State Management Guidelines
  2|
  3|**Purpose**: Universal state management guidelines for all agent workflows.
  4|
  5|## Universal State Management Structure
  6|
  7|### Workflow State File
  8|**Location**: `workflow_state.json` in current working directory
  9|**Purpose**: Track workflow execution state for recovery and monitoring
 10|**Format**: JSON-structured state data
 11|
 12|### Universal State Schema
 13|```json
 14|{
 15|  "workflow_id": "string",
 16|  "agent_type": "string",
 17|  "execution_strategy": "string",
 18|  "current_phase": "string",
 19|  "phase_status": "string",
 20|  "start_time": "timestamp",
 21|  "last_update": "timestamp",
 22|  "total_steps": "number",
 23|  "completed_steps": "number",
 24|  "failed_steps": "number",
 25|  "retry_count": "number",
 26|  "session_metadata": {}
 27|}
 28|```
 29|
 30|---
 31|
 32|## Universal State Management Patterns
 33|
 34|### Phase Status Tracking
 35|**Status Values**:
 36|- `phase_0_complete`: Rules loaded and ready
 37|- `phase_{N}_in_progress`: Phase currently executing
 38|- `phase_{N}_complete`: Phase successfully completed
 39|- `phase_{N}_failed`: Phase failed, requires intervention
 40|- `workflow_complete`: Entire workflow completed
 41|
 42|**Update Pattern**:
 43|1. Set status to `phase_{N}_in_progress` when starting phase
 44|2. Update to `phase_{N}_complete` when phase succeeds
 45|3. Update to `phase_{N}_failed` when phase fails
 46|4. Maintain audit trail of all status changes
 47|
 48|### Execution Strategy Storage
 49|**Storage Pattern**:
 50|- Store selected execution strategy in state file
 51|- Maintain strategy throughout workflow execution
 52|- Enable strategy changes with proper logging
 53|- Track strategy effectiveness for future optimization
 54|
 55|**Strategy Values**:
 56|- `manual`: Manual oversight with checkpoints
 57|- `auto`: Automatic progression with failure detection
 58|- `complete`: Full automation with failure tolerance
 59|- Agent-specific strategies as needed
 60|
 61|### Error Recovery State
 62|**Recovery State Management**:
 63|- Track failure points and recovery actions
 64|- Store retry count and backoff status
 65|- Maintain recovery action history
 66|- Enable recovery from any state point
 67|
 68|**Recovery Metadata**:
 69|```json
 70|{
 71|  "last_failure": {
 72|    "phase": "string",
 73|    "step": "number",
 74|    "error": "string",
 75|    "timestamp": "timestamp"
 76|  },
 77|  "retry_attempts": "number",
 78|  "recovery_actions": ["array of actions"],
 79|  "max_retries": "number"
 80|}
 81|```

 84|
 85|## Universal Audit Trail Patterns
 86|
 87|### State Change Logging
 88|**Logging Requirements**:
 89|- Log every state change with timestamp
 90|- Include change reason and context
 91|- Track user decisions and approvals
 92|- Maintain complete execution history
 93|
 94|**Log Entry Format**:
 95|```json
 96|{
 97|  "timestamp": "timestamp",
 98|  "event": "string",
 99|  "previous_state": "object",
100|  "new_state": "object",
101|  "reason": "string",
102|  "context": "object"
103|}
104|```
105|
106|### Session Metadata
107|**Metadata Requirements**:
108|- Session ID for tracking
109|- User identification
110|- Task description
111|- Execution context
112|- Resource usage tracking
113|
114|**Metadata Schema**:
115|```json
116|{
117|  "session_id": "string",
118|  "user_id": "string",
119|  "task_description": "string",
120|  "execution_context": "object",
121|  "resource_usage": {

123|    "cpu": "number",
124|    "time": "number"
125|  }
126|}
127|```

131|## Universal Recovery Patterns
132|
133|### State Recovery
134|**Recovery Process**:
135|1. Load current state from workflow_state.json
136|2. Identify last successful state point
137|3. Determine recovery strategy
138|4. Execute recovery actions
139|5. Update state with recovery progress
140|6. Resume workflow execution
141|
142|**Recovery Strategies**:
143|- **Retry with Backoff**: Exponential backoff for transient failures
144|- **Checkpoint Recovery**: Resume from last successful checkpoint
145|- **State Rollback**: Rollback to previous stable state
146|- **Manual Intervention**: Request user intervention for complex failures
147|- **Alternative Path**: Try alternative execution path
148|
149|### Checkpoint Management
150|**Checkpoint Creation**:
151|- Create checkpoints at critical phase transitions
152|- Store checkpoint state for recovery
153|- Include checkpoint metadata for validation
154|- Enable rollback to any checkpoint
155|
156|**Checkpoint Schema**:
157|```json
158|{
159|  "checkpoint_id": "string",
160|  "phase": "string",
161|  "step": "number",
162|  "state_snapshot": "object",
163|  "validation_hash": "string",
164|  "timestamp": "timestamp"
165|}
166|```

171|
172|### Planner Agent State
173|**Planner-Specific State Elements**:

177|- Plan revision tracking
178|- Panelist review aggregation state

220|## Universal State Update Patterns
221|
222|### State Update Rules
223|**Update Requirements**:
224|- Update state atomically to prevent corruption
225|- Validate state before persistence
226|- Include change metadata for audit trail
227|- Handle concurrent access safely
228|- Enable rollback on update failure
229|
230|### State Persistence
231|**Persistence Requirements**:
232|- Persist state after each phase completion
233|- Persist state on error conditions
234|- Persist state on user decisions
235|- Persist state on strategy changes
236|- Maintain state file integrity
237|
238|### State Validation
239|**Validation Requirements**:
240|- Validate state schema on load
241|- Validate state consistency before use
242|- Validate state transitions are legal
243|- Validate metadata completeness
244|- Validate no state corruption
245|
